# FrameAssembly (`frameassembly`)

> Rootless "Packets as Code" / "PCAP as Code" DSL & Rust compiler (v1.4.4) that compiles declarative `.fasm` (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) packet definitions into deterministic, nanosecond-accurate `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures across 81 native Layer 2 through Layer 7 protocols, with IPv4/IPv6 flow reuse, automatic TCP SEQ/ACK and reply-port tracking, and SNMPv3 USM (RFC 3414/3826/7860) cryptography. Built as the upstream companion compiler to Wireshark/`tshark` (inspection), `tcpreplay` (wire injection), and Suricata/Zeek (IDS/IPS testing).

FrameAssembly (`https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly`, `https://crates.io/crates/frameassembly`, `https://docs.rs/frameassembly`) synthesizes bit-exact, reproducible `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures offline in userspace with no `libpcap` or raw sockets required. Every protocol compiles with **zero mandatory sub-keywords** (emitting RFC-compliant wire defaults and ports) and supports explicit field and payload overrides via `frameassembly <input.fasm> [-o <output.pcap>]` and `frameassembly show <input.fasm>`.

### Zero-Shot `.fasm` Grammar & Anti-Hallucination Reference

1. **Three-Block Program Structure & Case-Insensitivity**: Every compilable `.fasm` file declares one or more `HOST <id> { IP <ip> [MAC <mac>] }` blocks (`MAC` natively accepts colon `00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e`, hyphen `00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E`, and Cisco dotted-quad `001a.2b3c.4d5e`), one or more parameterized `FLOW <id>(<param1>, <param2>, ...) { <statements> }` blocks, and one `COMPILE { <flow_calls_or_loops> }` block. All keywords, protocols, modifiers, time suffixes (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`), and identifiers (`HOST`, `FLOW`, parameters) are ASCII case-insensitive (`host` or `HOST`).
2. **1 Statement = 1 Wire Frame & Shared 4-Tuple State**: Each statement (`<a> -> <b> <PROTO> ...` or `<a> <- <b> <PROTO> ...`) emits 1 frame. TCP-based L7 statements emit a `PSH ACK` segment on that protocol's well-known port and share 4-tuple `SEQ`/`ACK` counters and bidirectional port inheritance with raw `TCP` statements on the same connection.
3. **Dual-Stack Endpoint Homogeneity**: A `FLOW` is polymorphic across IPv4 and IPv6 host pairs, but both endpoints in any single statement must share the same IP family (both IPv4 or both IPv6).
4. **Comment Syntax, `.fasm` Disambiguation & File-Size Rules**: `.fasm` (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) comments always use `//` (never `#` or `;`). FrameAssembly `.fasm` network packet specifications are completely distinct from unregistered x86 Flat Assembler files (`; ` comments, `format PE`/`ELF`, CPU mnemonics) and SymbiFlow/F4PGA FPGA bitstream assembly files (`#` comments, tile bit paths). Human-facing docs (`README.md`, `docs/*.md` except `docs/for_nerds.md`) use plain `//` comments and have no `< 50 KB` cap; AI-critical files (`src/**/*.rs`, `tests/*.rs`, `examples/**/*.fasm`) are strictly `< 50 KB` (`50,000` bytes), and `examples/**/*.fasm` files require `// PROMPT:`, `// TOKENS:`, and `// INSTRUCTION:` headers.

| Construct | ❌ NEVER WRITE (Invalid / Hallucinated) | ✅ ALWAYS WRITE (Canonical `.fasm` Syntax) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Comments** | `# comment` or `/* block comment */` | `// single-line comment` (only `//` is valid in `.fasm`) |
| **Host Block** | `HOST c = { IPV4: "10.0.0.1", MASK: 24 }` | `HOST c { IP 10.0.0.1 MAC 00:11:22:33:44:55 }` |
| **Flow Signature** | `FLOW web { FROM c TO s SEND HTTP }` | `FLOW web(c, s) { c -> s HTTP GET URI "/" }` |
| **Return Direction** | `s -> c REVERSE TCP` or `REPLY s -> c` | `c <- s TCP SYN ACK` (or `s -> c TCP SYN ACK`) |
| **Inter-Frame Delay** | `[+5ms] c -> s TCP ACK` or standalone `WAIT 5ms` | `c -> s TCP ACK WAIT 5ms` (inline modifier; `ns`,`us`,`ms`,`s`,`m`) |
| **Ports & TCP Ack** | `SPORT 1234 DPORT 80 ACK 100` | `SRCPORT 1234 DSTPORT 80 SEQ 1 ACKNUM 100` |
| **TCP Flags** | `FLAGS [SYN, ACK]` or `FLAGS="SA"` | `TCP SYN ACK` (bare space-separated tokens: `SYN ACK FIN RST PSH URG ECE CWR`) |
| **IPv4/IPv6 Hop Limit** | `HOP_LIMIT 64` or `HOPLIMIT 255` | `TTL 64` or `TTL 255` (canonical across both IPv4 and IPv6) |
| **802.1ad QinQ Tags** | `QINQ 100 200` or `SVLAN 100 CVLAN 200` | `QINQ 100 INNER_VLAN 200` |
| **HTTP Host Header** | `c -> s HTTP GET HOST "example.com"` | `c -> s HTTP GET URI "/" HOST_HDR "example.com"` |
| **SNMP Request ID** | `REQ_ID 10` or `REQUEST_ID 10` | `REQID 10` |
| **Compile Block** | Bare `COMPILE` or `COMPILE { web }` | `COMPILE { web(client, server) LOOP 3 { web(client, server) } }` |

### Complete 81 Native Protocol Keywords by OSI Layer

- **Layer 2 (`8` protocols)**: `ARP`, `VLAN`, `QINQ`, `LLDP`, `STP`, `LACP`, `EAPOL`, `MPLS`.
- **Layer 3 (`20` protocols)**: `ICMP`, `NDP`, `IGMP`, `MLD`, `GRE`, `VXLAN`, `GENEVE`, `IPSEC`, `ESP`, `AH`, `IKEV2`, `WIREGUARD`, `OSPF`, `BGP`, `RIP`, `VRRP`, `HSRP`, `PIM`, `BFD`, `OPENFLOW`.
- **Layer 4 (`3` protocols)**: `TCP`, `UDP`, `SCTP`.
- **Layer 7 SNMP (`3` protocols)**: `SNMP1`, `SNMP2`, `SNMP3` (9 `VARBIND <oid> <TYPE> <val>` types: `STRING`, `INT`, `COUNTER32`, `GAUGE32`, `TIMETICKS`, `COUNTER64`, `IPVAL`, `OIDVAL`, `NULLVAL`).
- **Layer 7 Infra & Telemetry (`11` protocols)**: `DNS`, `MDNS`, `DHCP`, `NTP`, `PTP`, `RADIUS`, `TACACS`, `SYSLOG`, `NETFLOW`, `IPFIX`, `SFLOW`.
- **Layer 7 Web, Security, VoIP & Access (`16` protocols)**: `HTTP`, `HTTP2`, `GRPC`, `WEBSOCKET`, `TLS`, `QUIC`, `STUN`, `SIP`, `RTP`, `RTSP`, `SSDP`, `TFTP`, `FTP`, `SSH`, `TELNET`, `WHOIS`.
- **Layer 7 Mail, Auth, Storage, DB & Messaging (`14` protocols)**: `SMTP`, `IMAP`, `POP3`, `KERBEROS`, `LDAP`, `SMB`, `NFS`, `REDIS`, `MEMCACHED`, `MYSQL`, `POSTGRES`, `MQTT`, `COAP`, `AMQP`.
- **Layer 7 Industrial ICS / SCADA / OT (`6` protocols)**: `MODBUS`, `BACNET`, `DNP3`, `S7COMM`, `ETHERNETIP`, `OPCUA`.
- **Universal Frame Modifiers**: `SRCMAC <mac>`, `DSTMAC <mac>`, `ETHERTYPE <u16>`, `VLAN <1..4094> [PCP <0..7>] [DEI <0..1>]`, `QINQ <1..4094> [INNER_VLAN <1..4094>]`, `MPLS <label> [EXP <0..7>] [BOS <0..1>] [MPLS_TTL <u8>]`, `TTL <u8>`, `DSCP <0..63>`, `ECN <0..3>`, `FLOWLABEL <u32>`, `IPID <u16>`, `DF`, `MF`, `FRAGOFFSET <u16>`, `SRCPORT <u16>`, `DSTPORT <u16>`, `TRANSPORT TCP|UDP`, `SEQ <u32>`, `ACKNUM <u32>`, `WIN <u16>`, `MSS <u16>`, `WSCALE <u8>`, `SACK_PERM`, `TSVAL <u32>`, `TSECR <u32>`, `URGENT <u16>`, `PAYLOAD "<str>"`, `HEXPAYLOAD "<hex>"`, `WAIT <int><ns|us|ms|s|m>`.

### Minimal Canonical `.fasm` Template & Public Rust API

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Stateful TCP 3-way handshake, HTTP/1.1 GET/200 OK, and SNMPv3 USM SHA-256/AES trap
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, TCP, SYN, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, WIN, MSS, WAIT, ACK, HTTP, GET, URI, HOST_HDR, STATUS, REASON, BODY, SNMP3, TRAP, USER, ENGINEID, AUTH, SHA256, PRIV, AES, OID, VARBIND, STRING, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Declare IPv4 endpoints
HOST client { IP 10.0.0.10 MAC 00:11:22:33:44:55 }
HOST server { IP 10.0.0.80 MAC aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff }

// INSTRUCTION: Define stateful web and SNMPv3 flow
FLOW demo_flow(c, s) {
    c -> s TCP SYN SRCPORT 51234 DSTPORT 80 WIN 65535 MSS 1460 WAIT 1ms
    c <- s TCP SYN ACK WIN 65535 MSS 1460 WAIT 1ms
    c -> s TCP ACK WAIT 1ms
    c -> s HTTP GET URI "/health" HOST_HDR "api.internal" WAIT 5ms
    c <- s HTTP STATUS 200 REASON "OK" BODY "{\"ok\":true}" WAIT 2ms
    s -> c SNMP3 TRAP USER "admin" ENGINEID "80001f8880112233" AUTH SHA256 "authpass123" PRIV AES "privpass123" OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "srv01" WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile flow for client and server
COMPILE {
    demo_flow(client, server)
}
```

- **Companion CLI Workflows (`frameassembly` + `wireshark` / `tshark` + `tcpreplay` + `suricata` / `zeek`)**:
  - Compile `.fasm` to `.pcap`: `frameassembly demo.fasm -o demo.pcap`
  - Show frames in terminal without writing `.pcap`: `frameassembly show demo.fasm`
  - Inspect frames in Wireshark GUI or terminal: `wireshark demo.pcap` / `tshark -r demo.pcap -V`
  - Replay capture onto wire interface: `sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 demo.pcap`
  - Validate IDS/IPS sensor rules: `suricata -r demo.pcap` / `zeek -C -r demo.pcap`
- **Multi-Platform Installation Commands**:
  - Homebrew (macOS & Linux): `brew install SteveWinschel/tap-FrameAssembly/frameassembly`
  - WinGet (Windows 10/11): `winget install SteveWinschel.FrameAssembly`
  - Scoop (Windows): `scoop bucket add frameassembly https://github.com/SteveWinschel/homebrew-tap-FrameAssembly && scoop install frameassembly`
  - APT (Debian/Ubuntu): `curl -fsSLo /tmp/frameassembly.deb https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/releases/latest/download/frameassembly_amd64.deb && sudo apt install -y /tmp/frameassembly.deb && rm -f /tmp/frameassembly.deb`
  - AUR (Arch Linux): `yay -S frameassembly-bin`
  - Cargo (All platforms with Rust): `cargo install frameassembly`
  - NPM (WebAssembly): `npm install frameassembly-wasm`
  - VS Code / Cursor Extension: `code --install-extension SteveWinschel.frameassembly-vscode`
  - Zero-clone bootstrap script: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh | sh`
- **Public Rust Library Signatures (`frameassembly` crate v1.4.4)**:
  - `frameassembly::lexer::lex(source: &str) -> Result<Vec<SpannedToken<'_>>, CompilerError>`
  - `frameassembly::parser::parse_program(source: &str) -> Result<Program<'_>, CompilerError>` (runs `validate_semantics` automatically)
  - `frameassembly::parser::validate_semantics<'a>(program: &Program<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Result<(), CompilerError>`
  - `frameassembly::backend::compile_program(program: &Program<'_>) -> Result<Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)>, String>` (returns `(raw_ethernet_frame_bytes, timestamp_ns)`)
  - `frameassembly::backend::generate_pcap(program: &Program<'_>, output_path: &str) -> Result<(), String>`
  - `frameassembly::error::CompilerError::{LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, BackendError}`

## Core Documentation

- [README — Problems Solved, Use Cases & Tool Comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/README.md): Minimalistic overview of the problems FrameAssembly solves, core use cases (SNMPv3 traps, firewall ACLs, pentesting, IDS validation), comparison against `Scapy`/`text2pcap`/`Ostinato`, installation, and 81-protocol summary.
- [Getting Started Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/getting_started.md): Beginner walkthrough of `.fasm` files, defaults vs. overrides, automatic TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` and reply ports, cross-layer tags, compiler error diagnostics, and Wireshark/`tshark`/`tcpreplay` workflows.
- [Practical Use Cases & Cookbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/use_cases.md): Ready-to-copy `.fasm` recipes for SNMPv1/v2c/v3 traps & polls, firewall ACL testing, VLAN/QinQ/MPLS/QoS verification, IDS/IPS & telemetry collectors, OT/SCADA dissectors, and zero-noise captures.
- [Layer 2 Switching & Data-Link Protocols](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l2_protocols.md): Complete syntax and wire framing for `ARP`, `VLAN`, `QINQ`, `LLDP`, `STP`, `LACP`, `EAPOL`, and `MPLS` (248 verified examples).
- [Layer 3 Control, Tunneling, VPN & Routing Protocols](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l3_protocols.md): Complete syntax and wire framing for `ICMP`, `NDP`, `IGMP`, `MLD`, `GRE`, `VXLAN`, `GENEVE`, `IPSEC`, `ESP`, `AH`, `IKEV2`, `WIREGUARD`, `OSPF`, `BGP`, `RIP`, `VRRP`, `HSRP`, `PIM`, `BFD`, and `OPENFLOW` (620 verified examples).
- [Layer 4 Transport Protocols](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l4_transports.md): Stateful 4-tuple progression, bidirectional port inheritance, RFC 7323 TCP options, UDP checksums, and SCTP multi-chunk bundling for `TCP`, `UDP`, and `SCTP` (95 verified examples).
- [Layer 7 SNMPv1, SNMPv2c & SNMPv3 USM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l7_snmp.md): ASN.1 BER encoding, `SNMP1`, `SNMP2`, and `SNMP3` USM authentication (`MD5`, `SHA`, `SHA256`, `SHA384`, `SHA512`), privacy encryption (`DES`, `AES`), and all 9 SMI `VARBIND` types (93 verified examples).
- [Layer 7 Infrastructure, Time, AAA & Flow Telemetry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md): Complete reference for `DNS`, `MDNS`, `DHCP`, `NTP`, `PTP`, `RADIUS`, `TACACS`, `SYSLOG`, `NETFLOW`, `IPFIX`, and `SFLOW` (341 verified examples).
- [Layer 7 Web, Cloud-Native, Transport Security, VoIP & Remote Access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md): Complete reference for `HTTP`, `HTTP2`, `GRPC`, `WEBSOCKET`, `TLS`, `QUIC`, `TFTP`, `FTP`, `SSH`, `TELNET`, `WHOIS`, `SIP`, `RTP`, `RTSP`, `STUN`, and `SSDP` (496 verified examples).
- [Layer 7 Mail, Directory, Storage, Databases & Message Brokers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md): Complete reference for `SMTP`, `IMAP`, `POP3`, `KERBEROS`, `LDAP`, `SMB`, `NFS`, `REDIS`, `MEMCACHED`, `MYSQL`, `POSTGRES`, `MQTT`, `COAP`, and `AMQP` (434 verified examples).
- [Layer 7 Industrial Control Systems (ICS) & SCADA/OT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l7_industrial_ot.md): Complete reference for `MODBUS`, `BACNET`, `DNP3`, `S7COMM`, `ETHERNETIP`, and `OPCUA` (186 verified examples).
- [Multi-Protocol Topologies & Dual-Stack Architectures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md): Leaf-Spine EVPN-VXLAN, Zero-Trust 802.1X NAC, 5G Service-Based Architecture, MPLS L3VPN, and Purdue ICS substations (104 verified topologies).
- [`.fasm` File Format & Media Type Specification (`text/vnd.frameassembly`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/fasm-specification.md): Normative RFC 6838 media type specification, UTF-8 encoding rules, lexical magic heuristics, `.fasm` extension disambiguation, and Wikidata/IANA mappings.
- [For Nerds: Compiler Pipeline, Rust Library API & Formal Grammars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/for_nerds.md): Six-stage zero-copy Rust compiler internals, public Rust library API, formal EBNF/GBNF/Lark grammars, constrained decoding, and `examples/` SFT/RLVR corpus conventions.

## Formal Grammars & Constrained Decoding

- [ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF Grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/grammar.ebnf): Formal context-free EBNF specification covering all 81 protocols and 640 uppercase terminal keywords.
- [llama.cpp & XGrammar GBNF Grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/frameassembly.gbnf): Constrained decoding grammar (`root ::= ...`) for `llama.cpp`, `vLLM`, `SGLang`, and `TensorRT-LLM`.
- [Lark / Outlines / llguidance CFG Grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/frameassembly.lark): Earley/LALR Context-Free Grammar (`start: ...`) for `Outlines`, `Guidance`, and `llguidance`.
- [Full Single-Fetch LLM Context Bundle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/llms-full.txt): Consolidated single-file bundle (`< 900 KB`) containing section manifest, all 13 documentation guides, formal grammars, AST specs, and representative `.fasm` corpus scenarios.

## Rust Compiler Architecture

- [Library Crate Root (`src/lib.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/lib.rs): Public Rust API entry point, protocol matrix, and library quickstart.
- [Structured Compiler Errors (`src/error.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/error.rs): `CompilerError` (`LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `BackendError`) with `miette` diagnostic spans.
- [Zero-Copy Lexer (`src/lexer/mod.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/lexer/mod.rs): `logos 0.14` tokenizer defining all 640 uppercase keyword tokens, time units, IP/MAC/OID literals, and source spans.
- [AST Definitions (`src/ast/mod.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/ast/mod.rs): Strongly-typed AST nodes and `*Spec` structs across `src/ast/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/`.
- [Two-Phase Combinator Parser (`src/parser/mod.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/parser/mod.rs): `winnow 1.0` token-slice parser with protocol-scoped field dispatch and semantic validator.
- [Stateful 4-Tuple Backend (`src/backend/mod.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/backend/mod.rs): Flow expansion, `LOOP` unrolling, bidirectional port inheritance, TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` progression, and RFC 1112/2464 multicast MAC derivation.
- [Native Packet Framing (`src/packet.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/packet.rs): Ethernet/VLAN/QinQ/MPLS/IPv4/IPv6/TCP/UDP/SCTP framing and RFC 1071 / RFC 9260 CRC32c checksums.
- [PCAPNG Serializer (`src/pcap.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/pcap.rs): Nanosecond-resolution PCAPNG writer (`IfTsResol(9)`) via `pcap-file 2.0`.

# Public Rust Library API & Structured Compiler Diagnostics (`src/lib.rs` & `src/error.rs`)

- `frameassembly::lexer::lex(source: &str) -> Result<Vec<SpannedToken<'_>>, CompilerError>`
- `frameassembly::parser::parse_program(source: &str) -> Result<Program<'_>, CompilerError>` (automatically runs `validate_semantics`)
- `frameassembly::parser::validate_semantics<'a>(program: &Program<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Result<(), CompilerError>`
- `frameassembly::backend::compile_program(program: &Program<'_>) -> Result<Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)>, String>` (returns `(raw_ethernet_frame_bytes, timestamp_ns)`)
- `frameassembly::backend::generate_pcap(program: &Program<'_>, output_path: &str) -> Result<(), String>`
- `frameassembly::error::CompilerError`:
  - `CompilerError::LexError { src: NamedSource<String>, span: SourceSpan }` (`frameassembly::lexer::unrecognized_token`)
  - `CompilerError::ParseError { src: NamedSource<String>, span: SourceSpan, message: String }` (`frameassembly::parser::syntax_error`)
  - `CompilerError::SemanticError { src: NamedSource<String>, span: SourceSpan, message: String, help: String }` (`frameassembly::semantic::validation_error`)
  - `CompilerError::BackendError { message: String }` (`frameassembly::backend::generation_error`)

# Repository Overview (`README.md`)

# FrameAssembly — Packets as Code

[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/frameassembly.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/frameassembly)
[![Docs.rs](https://docs.rs/frameassembly/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/frameassembly)

[**Use Cases**](#network-and-security-testing-use-cases) • [**How It Works**](#how-frameassembly-works) • [**Comparison**](#why-frameassembly-instead-of-scapy-or-lab-vms) • [**Installation**](#installation) • [**81 Protocols & Docs**](#supported-protocols-and-documentation)

## What Is FrameAssembly?

At first you may think **FrameAssembly** is a programming language for systems development, but ironically it is a tool specifically for the very people who hate programming -> **Networking & Cybersecurity professionals**.

Have you ever wished you could just describe traffic in a few lines of simple networking keywords, get your own `.pcap`, and do a little SQL injection onto your favourite coworker's machine with the help of `tcpreplay`?

Well, here you have it and it's fun and free to use (even commercially) -> as long as **I'm not responsible for what you do with it** :)

FrameAssembly compiles readable `.fasm` packet code into custom `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures across **81 Layer 2–7 protocols**—with no Python setup or root privileges needed—ready to replay or inspect with **`tcpreplay`**, **Wireshark** / **`tshark`**, or **Suricata** / **Zeek**:

```frameassembly
host client   { ip 10.0.0.10 mac 00:11:22:33:44:55 }
host firewall { ip 10.0.0.1  mac aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff }

flow http_check(c, fw) {
    c -> fw tcp syn srcport 51234 dstport 80 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c <- fw tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c -> fw tcp ack wait 1ms
    c -> fw http get uri "/healthz" host_hdr "api.example.com" wait 2ms
    c <- fw http status 200 reason "OK" body "ok"
}

compile { http_check(client, firewall) }
```

```console
$ frameassembly show test.fasm
#      Time (ms)   Source -> Destination                    Proto       Bytes  Summary
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1      0.000       10.0.0.10 -> 10.0.0.1                    TCP         58     51234 -> 80 [SYN] seq=1000 len=0
2      1.000       10.0.0.1 -> 10.0.0.10                    TCP         58     80 -> 51234 [SYN ACK] seq=1000 ack=1001 len=0
3      2.000       10.0.0.10 -> 10.0.0.1                    TCP         54     51234 -> 80 [ACK] seq=1001 ack=1001 len=0
4      3.000       10.0.0.10 -> 10.0.0.1                    HTTP        102    51234 -> 80 [ACK PSH] seq=1001 ack=1001 len=48
5      5.000       10.0.0.1 -> 10.0.0.10                    HTTP        94     80 -> 51234 [ACK PSH] seq=1001 ack=1049 len=40

$ frameassembly test.fasm -o test.pcap && sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 test.pcap
```

## Network and Security Testing Use Cases

### 1. Simulate `linkDown` SNMP Traps & Syslog Alerts Without Unplugging Cables
Testing whether **Zabbix**, **LibreNMS**, **PRTG**, **Checkmk**, **SolarWinds**, **Datadog**, or `snmptrapd` actually pages on an encrypted SNMPv3 `authPriv` trap usually means configuring an SNMP agent, loading vendor MIBs, matching EngineIDs, and pulling a cable out of a switch. With FrameAssembly, you can generate encrypted SNMPv3 traps (`SHA-256` + `AES-128`), SNMPv1/v2c notifications, `Syslog` events, and `NetFlow` / `IPFIX` / `sFlow` records in seconds:

```frameassembly
host core_sw { ip 10.10.1.2  mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:01 }
host zabbix  { ip 10.10.1.50 mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:50 }

flow link_down_alert(sw, nms) {
    sw -> nms vlan 100 snmp3 trap user "netops" engineid "80001f8801" engineboots 5 enginetime 3600 auth sha256 "AuthPass123!" priv aes "PrivPass123!" oid 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.1 int 2 wait 5ms
    sw -> nms vlan 100 syslog facility 16 severity 3 hostname "core-sw-01" app "link" msg "Gi0/1 changed state to down"
}

compile { link_down_alert(core_sw, zabbix) }
```

```console
$ frameassembly snmp_alert.fasm -o snmp_alert.pcap && sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 snmp_alert.pcap
```

### 2. Generate `SYN` Floods & Threat Captures for IDS, NDR & SIEM Testing (`Suricata`, `Snort`, `Zeek`)
Validating detection rules for a TCP `SYN` flood, DNS sinkhole hit, or suspicious TLS `SNI` normally means searching GitHub for third-party `.pcap` files full of background noise or sensitive production IPs. FrameAssembly lets you build clean, repeatable `.pcap` files for detection engineering in a few lines of `.fasm` code:

```frameassembly
host bot_node    { ip 198.51.100.66 mac 00:50:56:c0:00:66 }
host workstation { ip 10.40.5.25     mac 00:50:56:40:05:25 }
host sec_gateway { ip 10.40.5.1      mac 00:1c:73:40:05:01 }

flow syn_flood(bot, gw) {
    bot -> gw tcp syn dstport 443 win 1024 wait 100us
}

flow c2_signature_check(ws, gw) {
    ws -> gw dns query txid 0x4401 qname "c2-beacon.bad-domain.test" qtype "A" wait 1ms
    ws <- gw dns response txid 0x4401 qname "c2-beacon.bad-domain.test" qtype "A" rcode 5 wait 2ms
    ws -> gw tcp syn srcport 53443 dstport 443 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    ws <- gw tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    ws -> gw tcp ack wait 1ms
    ws -> gw tls client_hello sni "shadow-upload.example.net" ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 2ms
    ws <- gw tls alert payload "BLOCKED_BY_SNI_POLICY"
}

compile {
    loop 100 { syn_flood(bot_node, sec_gateway) }
    c2_signature_check(workstation, sec_gateway)
}
```

```console
$ frameassembly ids_test.fasm -o ids_test.pcap && suricata -r ids_test.pcap -k none
```

### 3. Test Stateful Firewalls, VLAN Trunks & OT Rules Without Lab VMs
Sending a single spoofed packet at a stateful firewall (`nftables` / `iptables`, **Palo Alto**, **FortiGate**, **CheckPoint**) won't test your application rules because the firewall drops mid-stream data without a completed 3-way TCP handshake. FrameAssembly tracks TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` numbers and swaps reply ports on `<-` automatically, so you can verify DMZ rules, 802.1Q `VLAN` tags, and industrial OT (`Modbus`, `DNP3`, `S7comm`, `OPC UA`) policies before a maintenance window:

```frameassembly
host eng_ws  { ip 192.168.20.25  mac 00:11:22:33:44:55 }
host dmz_srv { ip 203.0.113.10   mac aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff }
host ot_plc  { ip 192.168.110.50 mac 00:0e:8c:aa:bb:01 }

flow acl_audit(c, srv, plc) {
    c -> srv vlan 20 tcp syn srcport 52000 dstport 443 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c <- srv vlan 20 tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c -> srv vlan 20 tcp ack wait 1ms
    c -> srv vlan 20 tls client_hello sni "portal.example.com" ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 2ms

    c -> srv vlan 20 tcp syn srcport 52001 dstport 22 win 64240 wait 1ms
    c <- srv vlan 20 tcp rst ack wait 1ms

    c -> plc vlan 110 tcp syn srcport 52002 dstport 502 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c <- plc vlan 110 tcp syn ack win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c -> plc vlan 110 tcp ack wait 1ms
    c -> plc vlan 110 modbus read_holding_registers txid 1 unitid 1 addr 0 count 2
}

compile { acl_audit(eng_ws, dmz_srv, ot_plc) }
```

```console
# Replay into a SPAN/TAP sensor port (for inline firewalls, split client/server NICs via tcpprep + tcpreplay -i eth0 -I eth1)
$ frameassembly acl_test.fasm -o acl_test.pcap && sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 acl_test.pcap
```

## How FrameAssembly Works

Every `.fasm` file follows three declarative building blocks—no loops over byte arrays, no manual bit-shifting, and no socket boilerplate:

1. **`host` — Declare Endpoints Once:** Bind readable names to `ip` / `ipv6` and `mac` addresses so topologies stay easy to read and refactor.
2. **`flow` — Describe Exchanges Directionally:** Write packets top-to-bottom using `->` and `<-` arrows, optional `vlan` / tunnel headers, Layer 2–7 protocol keywords, and microsecond-accurate `wait` deltas (`us`, `ms`, `s`).
3. **`compile` — Emit Standard Captures:** Call parameterized flows (with optional `loop` blocks) to compile deterministic `.pcap` or `.pcapng` files.

Under the hood, the Rust compiler handles the tedious packet plumbing automatically:

* **Stateful TCP Tracking:** Advances `SEQ` and `ACK` numbers from payload byte lengths and `SYN`/`FIN` flags, while flipping ports, IPs, and MAC addresses on `<-` replies.
* **Wire-Valid Framing & Checksums:** Computes Ethernet/802.1Q framing, IPv4/IPv6 lengths, and L3/L4 checksums out of the box.
* **Unprivileged & Git-Friendly:** Generates binary captures purely in userspace without `sudo` or raw sockets, turning opaque `.pcap` blobs into reviewable, `git diff`-able `.fasm` source files for CI/CD and regression suites.

## Why FrameAssembly Instead of Scapy or Lab VMs?

| Capability | FrameAssembly (`.fasm`) | Scapy (Python) | Full Lab VMs / GNS3 | Downloaded `.pcap` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Setup Overhead** | Single CLI binary | Python + `venv` + packages | Hypervisor + OS images | None |
| **Root to Build PCAP** | Never required | Not for offline `wrpcap` | Admin / hypervisor access | Not required |
| **TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` Math** | Automatic on `->` / `<-` | Manual state in Python | Real OS TCP stack | Fixed static stream |
| **Version Control** | Clean L2–L7 text DSL | Imperative scripts | Multi-GB disk images | Binary blobs |
| **Capture Hygiene** | Zero background chatter | Clean, high boilerplate | ARP / mDNS / OS noise | Foreign IPs & noise |

FrameAssembly is built to work **alongside** **`tcpreplay`**, **Wireshark** / **`tshark`**, **Suricata**, and **Zeek**—not replace them. Instead of maintaining Python environments or booting multi-VM labs just to synthesize 10 packets, you compile a `.fasm` file in milliseconds and feed the resulting `.pcap` straight into your existing replay and analysis tools.

## Installation

### Linux & macOS Shell Installer
```bash
curl -fsSL [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh) | sh
```

### Cargo (Rust 1.85+)
```bash
cargo install frameassembly
```

### Prebuilt Release Binaries (Linux, Windows, macOS)
Download standalone archives and `SHA-256` checksums from [**GitHub Releases**](https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/releases).

### WebAssembly Package (`npm`)
For browser-based playgrounds, IDEs, and Node/bundler integrations:
```bash
npm install frameassembly-wasm
```

### Quick CLI Usage
```bash
# Inspect packet timing, flags, sequence numbers, and byte lengths in the terminal
frameassembly show capture.fasm

# Compile to standard .pcap or .pcapng
frameassembly capture.fasm -o capture.pcap
frameassembly capture.fasm -o capture.pcapng

# View all CLI flags and options
frameassembly --help
```

## Supported Protocols and Documentation

FrameAssembly natively compiles **81 protocols across Layers 2–7**. Start with the guides below or jump straight into the protocol reference for your layer:

* [**Documentation Hub (`docs/README.md`)**](docs/README.md) — Full overview and index of all 81 supported protocols.
* [**Getting Started (`docs/getting_started.md`)**](docs/getting_started.md) — Core `.fasm` syntax, `host` / `flow` / `compile` mechanics, and your first capture.
* [**Real-World Use Cases (`docs/use_cases.md`)**](docs/use_cases.md) — Copy-paste recipes for NetOps alerting, firewall verification, and SecOps rule validation.
* [**Topologies & Dual-Stack (`docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md`)**](docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md) — Multi-hop gateways, VLAN/QinQ trunks, and IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack flows.
* [**Compiler Architecture (`docs/for_nerds.md`)**](docs/for_nerds.md) — Lexing, parsing, semantic validation, and binary emission internals for curious engineers.

### Layer 2–7 Protocol Reference

* [**Layer 2 — Switching & Data Link (`docs/l2_protocols.md`)**](docs/l2_protocols.md) — Ethernet II, IEEE 802.1Q `VLAN`, 802.1ad `QinQ`, `ARP`, `STP` / `RSTP`, `LLDP`, `CDP`, `LACP`, `MPLS`, `PPPoE`, `EAPOL` (802.1X), `MACsec`, and more.
* [**Layer 3 — Network, Routing & Tunnels (`docs/l3_protocols.md`)**](docs/l3_protocols.md) — `IPv4`, `IPv6`, `ICMP`, `ICMPv6` / `NDP`, `IGMP`, `GRE`, `IPsec` (`ESP` / `AH`), `VXLAN`, `Geneve`, `OSPF`, `VRRP`, `HSRP`, and `WireGuard`.
* [**Layer 4 — Transports (`docs/l4_transports.md`)**](docs/l4_transports.md) — Stateful `TCP` (flags, window, `MSS`, options, automatic `SEQ`/`ACK`), `UDP`, `SCTP`, and `QUIC`.
* [**Layer 7 — SNMPv1 / v2c / v3 (`docs/l7_snmp.md`)**](docs/l7_snmp.md) — `GET`, `GETNEXT`, `GETBULK`, `SET`, `RESPONSE`, `TRAP`, `INFORM`, and encrypted `SNMPv3` USM (`SHA-256` auth + `AES-128` priv).
* [**Layer 7 — Infrastructure & Telemetry (`docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md`)**](docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md) — `DNS`, `DHCP` / `DHCPv6`, `NTP`, `Syslog`, `NetFlow`, `IPFIX`, `sFlow`, `BGP`, `BFD`, and `PTP`.
* [**Layer 7 — Web, Cloud & Messaging (`docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md`)**](docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md) — `HTTP`, `TLS` (`ClientHello`, `SNI`, `ALPN`, Alerts), `SSH`, `WebSocket`, `gRPC`, `MQTT`, `CoAP`, and `AMQP`.
* [**Layer 7 — Mail, Auth, Storage & Databases (`docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md`)**](docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md) — `SMTP`, `IMAP`, `POP3`, `RADIUS`, `TACACS+`, `Kerberos`, `LDAP`, `SMB`, `NFS`, `FTP` / `TFTP`, `PostgreSQL`, `MySQL`, and `Redis`.
* [**Layer 7 — Industrial OT & ICS (`docs/l7_industrial_ot.md`)**](docs/l7_industrial_ot.md) — `Modbus/TCP`, `DNP3`, `S7comm`, `OPC UA`, `BACnet/IP`, `EtherNet/IP`, `IEC 60870-5-104`, and `PROFINET`.

# Repository Agent Guide (`AGENTS.md`)

# AGENTS.md — FrameAssembly AI Agent & LLM Onboarding Guide

**FrameAssembly** (`frameassembly` v1.4.4) is a Rust 2024 Domain-Specific Language (DSL) and optimizing compiler that compiles declarative `.fasm` network traffic specifications into deterministic, nanosecond-precision `.pcap` / `.pcapng` packet captures across **81 native Layer 2 through Layer 7 protocols** (`2,611` verified `.fasm` corpus scenarios).

---

## 1. Quick Build, Test & Verification Commands

```bash
# Cross-platform bootstrap install (prebuilt release binary fast-path or curl + C linker + rustup >= 1.85 + cargo install)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh | sh

# Build compiler and CLI binary
cargo build --release

# Run all unit, integration, and corpus verification tests
cargo test

# Run the corpus verification suite (validates all 2,611 examples/**/*.fasm headers, AST parsing & PCAP output)
cargo test --test corpus_verification_tests

# Compile a single .fasm specification to a .pcap file
cargo run -- demo.fasm -o output.pcap

# Show the terminal packet ladder for a .fasm file without writing a .pcap file
cargo run -- show demo.fasm
```

---

## 2. Unified `<layer>/<protocol>` Repository Architecture

FrameAssembly enforces strict structural symmetry across `src/`, `examples/`, and `docs/`:

- **`src/lexer/mod.rs`**: Zero-copy `logos 0.14` tokenizer defining `Token<'a>` for all 81 protocols, L2–L4 modifiers, SNMP USM parameters, time units (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`), IPv4/IPv6, MAC, and OID literals.
- **`src/ast/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`**: Strongly-typed AST node and `*Spec` definitions. Every AST type includes a `/// Syntax mapping: \`...\`` docstring binding the Rust type to its `.fasm` grammar.
- **`src/parser/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`**: Two-phase `winnow 1.0` token-slice (`Stream<'i, 'a>`) combinator parsers and semantic validator (`validate_semantics` in `src/parser/mod.rs`).
- **`src/builders/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`**: Zero-heap wire payload encoders and `src/builders/l7/snmp/` (`builder.rs`, `crypto.rs`) for RFC 1157 / 3416 / 3414 / 3826 / 7860 BER and USM encryption.
- **`src/backend/mod.rs` & `src/packet.rs` & `src/pcap.rs`**: 4-tuple TCP sequence/acknowledgment progression, bidirectional port inheritance across `->` and `<-`, multicast MAC derivation (RFC 2464 `33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx` and RFC 1112 `01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx`), and `pcap-file 2.0` PCAPNG serialization.
- **`examples/{l2,l3,l4,l7,topologies}/`**: Verified `.fasm` corpus (`2,611` files) organized by `<layer>/<protocol>/<protocol>_<scenario>.fasm`.
- **`docs/*.md`**: 13 canonical Markdown guides (human-first getting started, use-case cookbook, 9 layer/topology references, `.fasm` media type specification, and `for_nerds.md` for compiler/LLM internals):
  - [`docs/getting_started.md`](docs/getting_started.md) — Step-by-step beginner guide: `.fasm` anatomy, defaults vs. overrides, automatic TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` and reply ports, cross-layer tags, compiler error messages, and pairing with Wireshark/`tshark` and `tcpreplay`.
  - [`docs/use_cases.md`](docs/use_cases.md) — Practical cookbook: SNMPv1/v2c/v3 traps & polls, firewall ACL testing, VLAN/QinQ/MPLS/QoS verification, IDS/IPS & telemetry validation, OT/SCADA dissectors, and zero-noise captures.
  - [`docs/l2_protocols.md`](docs/l2_protocols.md) — Layer 2 switching & data-link protocols (`ARP`, `VLAN`, `QINQ`, `LLDP`, `STP`, `LACP`, `EAPOL`, `MPLS`).
  - [`docs/l3_protocols.md`](docs/l3_protocols.md) — Layer 3 control, tunneling, VPN, and routing protocols (`ICMP`, `NDP`, `IGMP`, `MLD`, `GRE`, `VXLAN`, `GENEVE`, `IPSEC`, `ESP`, `AH`, `IKEV2`, `WIREGUARD`, `OSPF`, `BGP`, `RIP`, `VRRP`, `HSRP`, `PIM`, `BFD`, `OPENFLOW`).
  - [`docs/l4_transports.md`](docs/l4_transports.md) — Layer 4 transports (`TCP`, `UDP`, `SCTP`), 4-tuple state tracking, RFC 7323 TCP options, and SCTP multi-chunk signaling.
  - [`docs/l7_snmp.md`](docs/l7_snmp.md) — Layer 7 `SNMP1`, `SNMP2`, and `SNMP3` USM authentication (`MD5`/`SHA`/`SHA256`/`SHA384`/`SHA512`), encryption (`DES`/`AES`), and all 9 ASN.1 SMI `VARBIND` types.
  - [`docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md`](docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md) — Layer 7 infrastructure, time, AAA, and flow telemetry (`DNS`, `MDNS`, `DHCP`, `NTP`, `PTP`, `RADIUS`, `TACACS`, `SYSLOG`, `NETFLOW`, `IPFIX`, `SFLOW`).
  - [`docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md`](docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md) — Layer 7 web, cloud-native, transport security, VoIP, and remote access (`HTTP`, `HTTP2`, `GRPC`, `WEBSOCKET`, `TLS`, `QUIC`, `TFTP`, `FTP`, `SSH`, `TELNET`, `WHOIS`, `SIP`, `RTP`, `RTSP`, `STUN`, `SSDP`).
  - [`docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md`](docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md) — Layer 7 mail, directory, storage, databases, caches, and message brokers (`SMTP`, `IMAP`, `POP3`, `KERBEROS`, `LDAP`, `SMB`, `NFS`, `REDIS`, `MEMCACHED`, `MYSQL`, `POSTGRES`, `MQTT`, `COAP`, `AMQP`).
  - [`docs/l7_industrial_ot.md`](docs/l7_industrial_ot.md) — Layer 7 Industrial Control Systems (ICS) & SCADA/OT (`MODBUS`, `BACNET`, `DNP3`, `S7COMM`, `ETHERNETIP`, `OPCUA`).
  - [`docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md`](docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md) — Multi-host enterprise, data center EVPN-VXLAN, and campus Zero-Trust 802.1X NAC topologies.
  - [`docs/fasm-specification.md`](docs/fasm-specification.md) — Canonical RFC 6838 specification for the FrameAssembly `.fasm` file format (`text/vnd.frameassembly`), UTF-8 encoding, lexical magic rules, and `.fasm` extension disambiguation.
  - [`docs/for_nerds.md`](docs/for_nerds.md) — Six-stage zero-copy Rust compiler architecture, public Rust library API (`parse_program`, `compile_program`, `generate_pcap`), formal grammars (`EBNF`/`GBNF`/`Lark`), constrained decoding, and `examples/` SFT/RLVR corpus conventions.
- **Formal Grammars & `.fasm` Standards Registration (`contrib/`)**:
  - [`grammar.ebnf`](grammar.ebnf): Formal ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF grammar.
  - [`frameassembly.gbnf`](frameassembly.gbnf): `llama.cpp` & MLC `XGrammar` GBNF grammar for constrained decoding (`--grammar-file frameassembly.gbnf`).
  - [`frameassembly.lark`](frameassembly.lark): Earley/LALR Lark grammar for `vLLM`, `Outlines`, `Guidance`, `XGrammar`, and `llguidance`.
  - [`contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md`](contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md): IANA RFC 6838 Vendor Tree registration (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) & Wikidata property mappings (`P31`, `P1195`, `P1163`, `P973`).
  - [`contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`](contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml): Freedesktop.org `shared-mime-info` XML database definition (`*.fasm` glob + lexer-derived `<magic>` rules).
  - [`contrib/linguist/`](contrib/linguist/README.md): GitHub Linguist `languages.yml`, `heuristics.yml` regex disambiguation, and verified `.fasm` samples.
- **AI Routing Maps & Metadata**:
  - [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) & [`.github/copilot-instructions.md`](.github/copilot-instructions.md): Agent & IDE instructions.
  - [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) & [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt): Concise index map and single-fetch full context bundle.
  - [`context7.json`](context7.json), [`codemeta.json`](codemeta.json) & [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff): Structured AI/SEO and academic citation metadata.

---

## 3. Core FrameAssembly DSL Rules & Invariants

1. **Program Structure & Case-Insensitivity**: Every `.fasm` file declares `HOST <id> { IP <ip> [MAC <mac>] }`, `FLOW <id>(<params>) { <statements> }`, and exactly one `COMPILE { <invocations_or_loops> }` block. All keywords, protocols, modifiers, time units (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`), and identifiers (`HOST`, `FLOW`, parameters) are case-insensitive (`host` / `HOST`).
2. **Polymorphic Dual-Stack Flows**: A `FLOW` works identically over IPv4 and IPv6 host pairs. Mixing IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints in the same statement is a semantic error.
3. **Zero-Keyword RFC Defaults**: Every one of the 81 protocols compiles with zero mandatory sub-keywords (emitting RFC-compliant default headers and ports) and supports explicit field overrides.
4. **1 Statement = 1 Frame & Shared 4-Tuple State**: Each statement emits 1 frame. TCP-based L7 statements emit a `PSH ACK` frame on that protocol's well-known port and share 4-tuple sequence/ack counters with raw `TCP` statements on the same connection.
5. **Branding, `.fasm` (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) Disambiguation & Companion Positioning**:
   - Always write the project name as one CamelCase word: `FrameAssembly` (or lowercase `frameassembly` strictly for the crate name, CLI binary, URLs, and code identifiers); never split the name into two words, which collides with CAD queries.
   - Maintain clear, factual disambiguation separating FrameAssembly `.fasm` (`text/vnd.frameassembly`) network packet specifications from unregistered x86 Flat Assembler and SymbiFlow/F4PGA FPGA FASM files.
   - Position FrameAssembly as the upstream "Packets as Code" companion compiler to `Wireshark`, `tshark`, `tcpreplay`, `Suricata`, and `Zeek` (comparing only against packet-crafting generators: `Scapy`, `text2pcap`, `Ostinato`), and describe its architecture accurately ("rootless", "offline", "deterministic", "no `libpcap` or raw sockets required") without claiming zero external crate dependencies.
6. **Corpus, AI Discovery & Documentation Hygiene**:
   - **Audience Architecture & Calling `.fasm` Code (Zero Developer Jargon & Zero Prompt Leaking)**: (1) `llms.txt` is optimized for search engines of AIs and `llms-full.txt` is optimized for pre-training and prompting of AIs; (2) `docs/*.md` are optimized for users proficient in networking and cybersecurity who may have little to no programming knowledge or experience; (3) READMEs (`README.md`, `frameassembly-vscode/README.md`, `frameassembly-wasm/README.md`) are optimized for their target audiences, with root `README.md` kept minimalistic—interesting and informative without being overwhelming—focused on the problems solved (preventing manual device/daemon configuration work, avoiding manual fault triggering on hardware, skipping lab VM setup, avoiding manual checksum/TCP sequence math), use cases (pentesting, testing firewalls, simulating SNMP traps, testing monitoring or cybersecurity solutions), and advantages over other solutions. FrameAssembly is not a tool for software developers: never use compiler/PL jargon (`"DSL"`, `"Domain-Specific Language"`, `"declarative"`, `"polymorphic"`, `"deterministic"`) in `README.md` or `docs/*.md` (except `docs/for_nerds.md`), and never leak or quote informal prompt phrasing into documentation. Always call `.fasm` **code** (`Packets as Code`), never `"plain text"`.
   - Every `.fasm` file in `examples/` must start with `// PROMPT: ...` on line 1, `// TOKENS: ...` on line 2 (matching real `src/lexer/mod.rs` tokens), and include `// INSTRUCTION: ...` before every `HOST`, `FLOW`, and `COMPILE` block (`avg_line_length <= 85`, `max_line_length <= 200`, `words >= 50`). Human-facing docs (`README.md` and `docs/*.md` except `docs/for_nerds.md`) must never include `// PROMPT:`, `// TOKENS:`, or `// INSTRUCTION:` metadata comments.
   - **Canonical Syntax Only (Anti-Hallucination Guardrail)**:
     - Never use `=`, colons, commas, `IPV4`, `IPV6`, or `MASK` in `HOST` blocks (only `HOST <id> { IP <ip> [MAC <mac>] }`).
     - Never declare parameterless `FLOW <id> { ... }` or use `FROM`, `TO`, `REVERSE`, `SEND`, standalone `WAIT` lines, or `+5ms` / `[+delay]` prefixes (always `FLOW <id>(<params>) { <a> -> <b> <PROTO> ... [WAIT <int><ns|us|ms|s|m>] }`).
     - Never use `SPORT`, `DPORT`, `ACK <n>`, or `FLAGS [...]` (always `SRCPORT`, `DSTPORT`, `ACKNUM <n>`, and bare flag tokens `SYN ACK`).
     - Never write bare `COMPILE` or argumentless flow calls inside `COMPILE { <flow>(<hosts>) }`.
   - **Five-Way Grammar, Parser, Specification & MIME Lockstep**: Every keyword in `src/lexer/mod.rs`, `grammar.ebnf`, `frameassembly.gbnf`, `frameassembly.lark`, and `frameassembly.tmLanguage.json` must be wired into `src/parser/` (with protocol-scoped field dispatch so `cut_err` or 0-arg flags never shadow other protocols) and included in `parse_spanned_ident`. Whenever lexer tokens or supported protocols change, automatically synchronize `README.md`, `src/lib.rs`, `docs/fasm-specification.md`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, and `contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`.
   - **100% Compilable Documentation & Examples**: Every `.fasm` file in `examples/` (`2,611` files) and `contrib/linguist/samples/` and every ````frameassembly` / ````fasm` code block in `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `docs/*.md`, `contrib/**/*.md`, `src/**/*.rs`, and `.agents/skills/**/*.md` must compile with zero errors.
   - **Rustdoc & `docs.rs` SEO Hygiene**: Every `src/**/*.rs` file must start with `//!` (`< 50 KB` per file, `>= 50` words). Never place outer `///` comments on `pub mod` declarations that have inner `//!` docs. Keep internal parser submodules `pub(crate) mod` so `docs.rs` never generates empty module pages, use `#[doc(inline)]` on layer re-exports, and annotate all 81 AST `*Spec` structs with `/// Syntax mapping:` and `#[doc(alias = "...")]`.
   - Never write literal NUL bytes (`0x00`) into any `.md` or `.txt` file.
   - Keep AI-critical Rust and corpus files (`src/**/*.rs`, `tests/*.rs`, `examples/**/*.fasm`) strictly `< 50 KB` (`50,000` bytes) (human-facing `README.md` and `docs/*.md` have no `< 50 KB` cap), and maintain zero broken links or orphan `.md` files in `docs/`.
   - Never bump `version` in `Cargo.toml` or run `git commit`, `git push`, or `git tag` unless explicitly instructed by the user.

---

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/getting_started.md`

# Getting Started with FrameAssembly

Crafting custom network traffic is usually way harder than whatever you are actually trying to test. If you want to verify a stateful firewall ACL, check whether Zabbix alerts on an encrypted SNMPv3 trap, or test a new Suricata rule, your options are grim: wire up spare lab hardware and yank cables by hand, wrestle with Python virtual environments and manual TCP sequence numbers in `Scapy` as `root`, or count hexadecimal byte offsets in `text2pcap` until you lose the will to live.

**FrameAssembly** (`frameassembly`) fixes that without needing `sudo` privileges, `libpcap`, or raw sockets. You write the network conversation as readable `.fasm` code ("Packets as Code") using everyday networking terms, compile it into a deterministic `.pcap` / `.pcapng` capture in milliseconds, and feed it straight into **Wireshark**, **`tshark`**, **Suricata**, **Zeek**, or **`tcpreplay`**:

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      The 3-Step Mental Model                           │
├───────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────┤
│ 1. host           │ 2. flow                       │ 3. compile         │
│ Declare endpoints │ Script the packet sequence    │ Emit the .pcap     │
│ IP & optional MAC │ 1 statement = 1 wire frame    │ Wire hosts to flow │
│ (v4, v6, any MAC) │ -> forward, <- reply (swaps)  │ Single or loop N   │
└───────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴────────────────────┘
```

---

## Step 1 — Installing FrameAssembly

Pick the one-liner for your operating system:

| Platform / OS | Method | Installation Command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Linux (Universal)** | One-line installer | `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh \| sh` |
| **Debian / Ubuntu** | APT (`.deb`) | `curl -fsSLo /tmp/frameassembly.deb https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/releases/latest/download/frameassembly_amd64.deb && sudo apt install -y /tmp/frameassembly.deb && rm -f /tmp/frameassembly.deb` |
| **macOS & Linux** | Homebrew | `brew install SteveWinschel/tap-FrameAssembly/frameassembly` |
| **Arch Linux** | AUR | `yay -S frameassembly-bin` |
| **Windows 10 / 11** | WinGet | `winget install SteveWinschel.FrameAssembly` |
| **Windows** | Scoop | `scoop bucket add frameassembly https://github.com/SteveWinschel/homebrew-tap-FrameAssembly && scoop install frameassembly` |
| **Any (Rust 1.85+)** | Cargo | `cargo install frameassembly` |
| **Browser / Node.js** | NPM (WASM) | `npm install frameassembly-wasm` |
| **VS Code / Cursor** | Extension | `code --install-extension SteveWinschel.frameassembly-vscode` |
| **Prebuilt Binaries** | GitHub Releases (`v1.4.4`) | [Download from GitHub Releases (`v1.4.4` / `latest`)](https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/releases/latest) |

Verify that the compiler is on your `PATH` (if you used the universal Linux installer, run `. "$HOME/.cargo/env"` or open a new shell first):

```bash
frameassembly --version   # frameassembly 1.4.4
frameassembly --help
```

---

## Step 2 — Your First `.fasm` Capture in 60 Seconds

You do not need any programming background to write `.fasm` code. Every `.fasm` file has just three sections from top to bottom:
1. **`host` blocks** — Declare the devices on your network diagram (`ip` and optional `mac`).
2. **`flow` blocks** — Script the packet-by-packet conversation between role labels like `(client, gw)`, using `->` for forward packets and `<-` for replies.
3. **`compile` block** — Plug your declared `host` devices into those flow roles in matching left-to-right order to build the `.pcap`.

Save the following code as `ping_test.fasm`:

```frameassembly
// 1. Declare the network devices
host workstation {
    ip 192.168.10.50
    mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:50
}

host default_gw {
    ip 192.168.10.1
    mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:01
}

// 2. Script the packet sequence (1 directional statement = 1 Ethernet frame)
flow verify_gateway_ping(client, gw) {
    client -> gw icmp echo_request id 100 seq 1 payload "ping-check-1" wait 2ms
    client <- gw icmp echo_reply   id 100 seq 1 payload "ping-check-1" wait 10ms
    client -> gw icmp echo_request id 100 seq 2 payload "ping-check-2" wait 2ms
    client <- gw icmp echo_reply   id 100 seq 2 payload "ping-check-2"
}

// 3. Compile the capture (maps workstation -> client, default_gw -> gw)
compile {
    verify_gateway_ping(workstation, default_gw)
}
```

Preview the packet ladder in your terminal, compile it to a `.pcap` file, and inspect or replay it:

```bash
# Preview the packet ladder in your terminal without creating a file
frameassembly show ping_test.fasm

# Compile to a deterministic, nanosecond-precision .pcap capture
frameassembly ping_test.fasm -o ping_test.pcap

# Dissect in Wireshark / tshark, or replay onto a live test interface
tshark -r ping_test.pcap
wireshark ping_test.pcap &
sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 ping_test.pcap
```

---

## Step 3 — Three Ground Rules & Zero-Hassle MAC Addresses

* **Keywords are case-insensitive:** Lowercase (`host`, `tcp syn`, `dstport 443`) is standard, though `HOST` or `Tcp` compiles to the exact same bytes. Quoted text (`"..."`) always preserves exact casing on the wire.
* **Comments start with `//`:** Use `//` anywhere on a line. Never use `#` or `;` for comments.
* **One statement = one Ethernet frame:** Every `a -> b ...` or `a <- b ...` statement inside `flow { ... }` emits **one Ethernet frame**—even if you wrap a long Layer 7 statement across multiple indented lines to keep it readable.

### Copy-Paste Any MAC Format (Or Skip MACs Completely)

Whether you copy a MAC address from `ip link` on Linux, `ipconfig /all` on Windows, or `show mac address-table` on a Cisco switch, **do not waste time reformatting colons, hyphens, and dots**—FrameAssembly accepts all three natively:

```frameassembly
host linux_srv  { ip 10.0.0.10 mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e }
host windows_pc { ip 10.0.0.20 mac 00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5F }
host cisco_sw   { ip 10.0.0.1  mac 001a.2b3c.4d01 }

flow verify_mac_notations(srv, pc, sw) {
    srv -> pc icmp echo_request id 1 seq 1 payload "colon-to-hyphen" wait 1ms
    pc  -> sw arp request sendermac 00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5F senderip 10.0.0.20 targetip 10.0.0.1 wait 1ms
    pc  <- sw arp reply   sendermac 001a.2b3c.4d01    senderip 10.0.0.1  targetmac 00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5F targetip 10.0.0.20
}

compile {
    verify_mac_notations(linux_srv, windows_pc, cisco_sw)
}
```

And if your test only cares about Layer 3–7 behavior, **leave `mac` out of `host` completely**:
1. **Unicast hosts without `mac`:** FrameAssembly assigns clean, direction-aware unicast MACs (`00:00:00:00:00:01` and `00:00:00:00:00:02`) so switch CAM tables never flap during `tcpreplay`.
2. **Multicast hosts without `mac`:** IPv4 multicast (`224.0.0.0/4`) automatically derives RFC 1112 MACs (`01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx`), and IPv6 multicast (`ff00::/8`) automatically derives RFC 2464 MACs (`33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx`).

```frameassembly
host core_rtr     { ip 10.0.0.1 }
host ospf_all_spf { ip 224.0.0.5 }
host core_rtr_v6  { ip fe80::1 }
host ospf6_all    { ip ff02::5 }

flow send_ospf_hello(rtr, mcast) {
    // Auto-derives 01:00:5e:00:00:05 on IPv4 and 33:33:00:00:00:05 on IPv6
    rtr -> mcast ttl 1 ospf hello router_id 10.0.0.1 area_id 0 hello_interval 10 dead_interval 40
}

compile {
    send_ospf_hello(core_rtr, ospf_all_spf)
    send_ospf_hello(core_rtr_v6, ospf6_all)
}
```

---

## Step 4 — Sensible RFC Defaults vs. Custom Overrides

Every one of FrameAssembly's **81 protocols** compiles with **zero required sub-keywords**. Write just the protocol keyword when you want a valid RFC packet on its standard port (`UDP 53` for `dns`, `TCP 179` for `bgp`, `UDP 162` for `snmp3`), and add modifiers in any order only for the fields you want to customize:

```frameassembly
host peer_a { ip 10.10.0.1 }
host peer_b { ip 10.10.0.2 }

// Minimal RFC defaults—zero boilerplate
flow quick_defaults(c, s) {
    c -> s icmp wait 1ms
    c -> s dns  wait 1ms
    c -> s bgp
}

// Explicit header overrides on the same three protocols
flow custom_headers(c, s) {
    c -> s ttl 128 df icmp echo_request id 42 seq 10 payload "MTU_PROBE_1472" wait 2ms
    c -> s dns query txid 0x99a1 qname "db01.corp.internal" qtype "AAAA" wait 2ms
    c -> s ttl 255 dscp 48 bgp update asn 65001 prefix "172.16.0.0/16" nexthop 10.10.0.1
}

compile {
    quick_defaults(peer_a, peer_b)
    custom_headers(peer_a, peer_b)
}
```

---

## Step 5 — Stateful TCP Without Manual Sequence Math

Hand-crafting TCP streams in older packet tools is miserable: if one sequence byte is off, Wireshark flags `[TCP Previous segment not captured]` and stateful firewalls drop the packet cold.

Inside `flow(c, s)`, keep `c` on the left and `s` on the right and flip the arrow (`->` vs. `<-`). That layout matches Wireshark's **Flow Graph** line for line, and FrameAssembly handles the bookkeeping automatically:

```text
  Wireshark Flow Graph               FrameAssembly .fasm Flow Statement
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  10.0.0.10             10.0.0.80
      |                     |
      |   TCP 52100 -> 80   |
      |-------------------->|        c -> s tcp syn srcport 52100 dstport 80 win 65535
      |        [SYN]        |
      |                     |
      |   TCP 80 -> 52100   |
      |<--------------------|        c <- s tcp syn ack win 65535 wait 1ms
      |      [SYN, ACK]     |
      |                     |
      |   TCP 52100 -> 80   |
      |-------------------->|        c -> s tcp ack wait 1ms
      |        [ACK]        |
      |                     |
      |  HTTP GET /status   |
      |-------------------->|        c -> s http get uri "/status" host_hdr "api.local"
      |      [PSH, ACK]     |
      |                     |
      |   HTTP 200 OK       |
      |<--------------------|        c <- s http status 200 reason "OK" body "{\"up\":true}"
      |      [PSH, ACK]     |
```

* **Automatic reply port swapping:** Set `srcport 52100 dstport 80` once on the opening `syn`. Every `c <- s` reply automatically flips the ports to `80 -> 52100`.
* **Shared 4-tuple `seq` & `acknum` state:** `syn` and `fin` advance the sequence counter by `+1`, and any TCP-based Layer 7 statement (`http`, `tls`, `ssh`, `bgp`, `smb`, `modbus`, etc.) emits a `PSH ACK` segment that advances `seq` and `acknum` by the exact byte length of the generated payload:

```frameassembly
host app_client { ip 10.20.1.50 }
host web_server { ip 10.20.1.80 }

flow tracked_http_conversation(c, s) {
    c -> s tcp syn srcport 52100 dstport 80 win 65535 mss 1460 wscale 7 sack_perm wait 1ms
    c <- s tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wscale 7 sack_perm wait 1ms
    c -> s tcp ack wait 2ms

    c -> s http get uri "/api/v1/status" host_hdr "api.internal" user_agent "NOC-Probe/1.0" wait 5ms
    c <- s http status 200 reason "OK" content_type "application/json" body "{\"healthy\":true}" wait 2ms

    c -> s tcp fin ack wait 1ms
    c <- s tcp fin ack wait 1ms
    c -> s tcp ack
}

compile {
    tracked_http_conversation(app_client, web_server)
}
```

Need to test how a firewall or IDS handles **broken** TCP traffic? Override `win 0`, `seq`, `acknum`, or `rst` on any line:

```frameassembly
host client_node { ip 10.30.0.10 }
host server_node { ip 10.30.0.20 }

flow tcp_anomaly_and_zero_window(c, s) {
    c -> s tcp syn srcport 54000 dstport 8080 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c <- s tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c -> s tcp ack wait 1ms

    c -> s http post uri "/upload" host_hdr "ingest.local" body "CHUNK_DATA_01" wait 2ms
    // Server receive buffer fills up (TCP ZeroWindow)
    c <- s tcp ack win 0 wait 50ms
    // Inject an out-of-window segment to verify stateful firewall drop counters
    c -> s tcp psh ack seq 900000 acknum 1 payload "OUT_OF_WINDOW_PROBE" wait 5ms
    // Server reopens receive window and completes response
    c <- s tcp ack win 32768 wait 2ms
    c <- s http status 200 reason "OK" body "UPLOAD_COMPLETE"
}

compile {
    tcp_anomaly_and_zero_window(client_node, server_node)
}
```

---

## Step 6 — VLANs, Carrier QinQ, MPLS, QoS & Fragmentation

Attach Layer 2 tags, Layer 3 DiffServ/fragmentation bits, transport overrides, and nanosecond-to-minute `wait` timers to **any** statement:

| Layer | Modifier Syntax | Range / Format | Wire Effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **L2 VLAN** | `vlan <id> [pcp <0..7>] [dei <0..1>]` | VID `1..4094` | Inserts IEEE 802.1Q tag (`0x8100`) + CoS priority |
| **L2 QinQ** | `qinq <s_vid> inner_vlan <c_vid>` | VID `1..4094` | Inserts 802.1ad S-VLAN (`0x88a8`) + 802.1Q C-VLAN (`0x8100`) |
| **L2 MPLS** | `mpls <lbl> [exp <0..7>] [bos <0\|1>] [mpls_ttl <n>]` | Label `0..1048575` | Inserts RFC 3032 MPLS shim header (`0x8847`) |
| **L2 Ethernet** | `srcmac <mac>` / `dstmac <mac>` / `ethertype <u16>` | Any MAC / `0x88cc` | Overrides outer Ethernet MACs or EtherType |
| **L3 Hop & QoS** | `ttl <0..255>` / `dscp <0..63>` / `ecn <0..3>` | Unified IPv4 & IPv6 | Sets TTL/Hop Limit and TOS/Traffic Class (`dscp 46` = `EF`) |
| **L3 IPv6** | `flowlabel <0..1048575>` | `0..0xfffff` | Sets 20-bit IPv6 Flow Label (ignored on IPv4) |
| **L3 IPv4 Frag** | `ipid <u16>` / `df` / `mf` / `fragoffset <0..8191>` | 8-byte offset units | PMTUD Don't Fragment (`df`) or multi-fragment IPv4 reassembly |
| **L4 & Timing** | `srcport <p>` / `dstport <p>` / `transport tcp\|udp` / `wait <t>` | `ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m` | Overrides L4 ports/transport and advances PCAPNG timestamp |

```frameassembly
host branch_edge { ip 172.16.100.10 mac 00:1c:73:aa:00:10 }
host core_pe     { ip 172.16.100.1  mac 00:1c:73:aa:00:01 }

flow wan_encapsulation_showcase(edge, core) {
    edge -> core vlan 110 pcp 5 dei 0 ttl 64 dscp 46 ecn 2
        rtp pt 0 seq 1 timestamp 160 ssrc 0x10203040 payload "VOICE_FRAME" wait 5ms
    edge -> core qinq 2000 inner_vlan 110 dscp 26
        udp srcport 50000 dstport 9000 payload "METRO_ETHERNET_DATA" wait 5ms
    edge -> core mpls 16000 exp 5 bos 1 mpls_ttl 63 ttl 63 dscp 46
        icmp echo_request id 50 seq 1 payload "MPLS_L3VPN_PING" wait 5ms
    edge -> core df ipid 0x4400 ttl 64
        icmp echo_request id 51 seq 1 payload "PMTUD_DO_NOT_FRAGMENT" wait 5ms
    edge -> core ipid 0x7788 mf fragoffset 0
        icmp echo_request id 52 seq 1 payload "FIRST_8B_SECOND8" wait 1ms
    edge -> core ipid 0x7788 fragoffset 2
        icmp echo_request id 52 seq 1 payload "FINAL_FRAGMENT_B"
}

compile {
    wan_encapsulation_showcase(branch_edge, core_pe)
}
```

---

## Step 7 — Reusable Dual-Stack IPv4/IPv6 Flows & `loop` Bursts

Because a `flow(node, srv)` uses role labels instead of hardcoded IPs, you can write a packet sequence once and run it inside `compile` with IPv4 hosts, IPv6 hosts, or inside a `loop <count> { ... }` block to generate a multi-packet traffic burst. FrameAssembly automatically switches between IPv4 (`0x0800`) and IPv6 (`0x86dd`), recalculates pseudo-header checksums, and advances sequence numbers and timestamps on every pass:

```frameassembly
host sensor_v4    { ip 10.50.0.10 }
host collector_v4 { ip 10.50.0.100 }
host sensor_v6    { ip 2001:db8:50::10 }
host collector_v6 { ip 2001:db8:50::100 }

flow heartbeat_burst(node, srv) {
    node -> srv vlan 50 dscp 16 ttl 64 flowlabel 0x1a2b3
        icmp echo_request id 90 seq 1 payload "HEARTBEAT" wait 2ms
    node <- srv vlan 50 dscp 16 ttl 64 flowlabel 0x1a2b3
        icmp echo_reply id 90 seq 1 payload "HEARTBEAT" wait 5ms
    node -> srv vlan 50 dscp 16 ttl 64 flowlabel 0x1a2b3
        syslog facility 16 severity 6 hostname "edge-sensor" app "healthd" msg "Heartbeat OK" wait 10ms
}

compile {
    loop 4 {
        heartbeat_burst(sensor_v4, collector_v4)
        heartbeat_burst(sensor_v6, collector_v6)
    }
}
```

---

## Step 8 — Helpful Error Messages & Typo Hints

When a `.fasm` file has a typo—or if someone accidentally passes an x86 Flat Assembler or FPGA FASM file—FrameAssembly refuses to create a broken `.pcap` and prints a plain-English fix:

```text
frameassembly::parse_error

  × Failed to parse input: Syntax error: unexpected token 'sport', expected a valid statement
  │ or protocol modifier. Did you mean 'SRCPORT'?
   ╭─[my_test.fasm:6:16]
 5 │ flow test(c, s) {
 6 │     c -> s tcp sport 50000 dstport 80 syn
   ·                ──┬──
   ·                  ╰── Here
   ╰────
  help: Replace 'sport' with 'SRCPORT <port>' (for example: srcport 51234).
```

---

## Step 9 — Wireshark / `tcpdump` to `.fasm` Cheat Sheet

| Networking Concept | Wireshark Display Filter | `tcpdump` Expression | `.fasm` Syntax |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Host IP & MAC** | `ip.addr == 10.0.0.1 && eth.addr == ...` | `host 10.0.0.1 and ether host ...` | `host rtr { ip 10.0.0.1 mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e }` |
| **802.1Q VLAN & CoS** | `vlan.id == 100 && vlan.priority == 5` | `vlan 100` | `vlan 100 pcp 5 dei 0` |
| **802.1ad QinQ** | `vlan.id == 2000 && vlan.id == 100` | `vlan 2000 and vlan 100` | `qinq 2000 inner_vlan 100` |
| **MPLS Label & EXP** | `mpls.label == 16000 && mpls.exp == 5` | `mpls 16000` | `mpls 16000 exp 5 bos 1 mpls_ttl 64` |
| **DiffServ `DSCP` / `ECN`** | `ip.dsfield.dscp == 46` | `ip[1] & 0xfc == 0xb8` | `dscp 46 ecn 2` |
| **TTL / IPv6 Hop Limit** | `ip.ttl == 64` / `ipv6.hlim == 64` | `ip[8] == 64` / `ip6[7] == 64` | `ttl 64` |
| **IPv4 DF / Fragments** | `ip.flags.df == 1` / `ip.frag_offset` | `ip[6] & 0x40 != 0` | `df` or `ipid 0x1234 mf fragoffset 0` |
| **L4 Ports & TCP Flags** | `tcp.dstport == 443 && tcp.flags.syn == 1` | `dst port 443 and tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0` | `tcp syn srcport 52000 dstport 443` |
| **TCP Seq / Ack / Win** | `tcp.seq == 1000 && tcp.ack == 2000` | `tcp[4:4] == 1000` | `seq 1000 acknum 2000 win 65535` |
| **SNMP VarBinds** | `snmp.name == 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0` | `udp port 161 or udp port 162` | `varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "core-sw"` |

> **Tip — Using AI Coding Assistants with `.fasm`:**
> FrameAssembly ships a compact syntax sheet at [`llms.txt`](https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/blob/main/llms.txt) (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/llms.txt`). Point ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or Cursor at that URL when you want to scaffold a large multi-host topology from a plain-English description.

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/use_cases.md`

# Practical Use Cases & Cookbook for Network Engineers

Testing a new firewall ACL, an encrypted SNMPv3 trap alert, an 802.1ad QinQ / MPLS trunk, or a Suricata IDS rule usually means hours of lab cabling, MIB hunting, or fighting `root` raw-socket scripts. Every recipe in this cookbook replaces that setup with a **complete, ready-to-copy `.fasm` file** ("Packets as Code") built from three simple sections—no programming experience required:
- **`host` blocks** declare the devices on your network diagram (`ip` and optional `mac`).
- **`flow(a, b)` blocks** script the packet-by-packet sequence between role labels (`a -> b` sends forward; `a <- b` sends a reply from `b` back to `a`).
- **`compile` block** plugs your `host` devices into those flow roles in left-to-right order (or repeats them inside `loop <count> { ... }`) to emit the `.pcap`.

To run any recipe below:
1. Save the `.fasm` code to a file (for example, `scenario.fasm`) and compile it to `.pcap`: `frameassembly scenario.fasm -o scenario.pcap` (or preview in your terminal with `frameassembly show scenario.fasm`—no `sudo` required).
2. Replay or inspect `scenario.pcap` with **`tcpreplay`**, **Wireshark** / **`tshark`**, or **Suricata** / **Zeek**.

---

| I Need to Test or Troubleshoot... | Protocols & Header Features Used | Jump Directly to Recipe |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| **Encrypted SNMPv3 `authPriv` trap decryption (`SHA-256`/`SHA-512` + `AES-128` or legacy `MD5`/`DES`)** | `SNMP3` (`AUTH SHA256`/`SHA512`/`MD5`/`SHA`, `PRIV AES`/`DES`, `ENGINEID`) | [Recipe 1B — Encrypted SNMPv3 `authPriv` Traps & Informs](#recipe-1b--encrypted-snmpv3-authpriv-traps--informs-sha-256sha-512--aes-128--md5sha-1--des) |
| **DMZ / Perimeter firewall ACLs (permitted HTTPS vs. blocked port `TCP RST` vs. stealth scans)** | `TCP` (`SYN`, `RST ACK`, out-of-state `ACK`, `FIN PSH URG`), `VLAN`, `ICMP` (`CODE 13`) | [Recipe 2A — DMZ & Perimeter Firewall Policy Audit](#recipe-2a--dmz--perimeter-firewall-policy-audit-handshakes-rejections-out-of-state--stealth-probes) |
| **VPN / WAN blackhole MTU issues (`DF` bit), IPv4 fragment reassembly, or BCP 38 IP spoofing** | `DF`, `IPID`, `MF`, `FRAGOFFSET`, `ICMP` (`DEST_UNREACH CODE 4`), spoofed `HOST` | [Recipe 2B — Path MTU (`DF`), IPv4 Fragmentation & Anti-Spoofing](#recipe-2b--path-mtu-discovery-df-ipv4-fragmentation-mf--fragoffset--spoofed-source-egress-filtering) |

| **SIEM syslog parsers (`UDP`/`TCP 514`) or flow collectors (ElastiFlow, Akvorado, `nfdump`)** | `SYSLOG` (`TRANSPORT TCP`), `NETFLOW` (v5), `IPFIX` (v10), `SFLOW` (v5) | [Recipe 4A — SIEM & Flow Collector Ingest](#recipe-4a--siem--flow-collector-ingest-syslog-over-udptcp-netflow-v5-ipfix-v10--sflow-v5) |
| **Suricata / Zeek / Snort IDS rules, DNS sinkholes, TLS 1.3 `SNI` filtering, or WAF rules** | `DNS` (`RCODE 5`), `TLS` (`CLIENT_HELLO`, `SNI`, `ALPN`, `ALERT`), `HTTP` (`HEADER`, `BODY`) | [Recipe 4B — IDS/IPS & DPI Signature Validation](#recipe-4b--idsips--dpi-signature-validation-dns-sinkhole-tls-13-snialpn--custom-http-headers) |
| **Industrial OT firewall conduits & SCADA sensors (`READ` vs. `WRITE`/`OPERATE`) without PLCs** | `MODBUS`, `S7COMM`, `DNP3` (auto CRC-16), `BACNET`, `ETHERNETIP`, `OPCUA` | [Recipe 5 — Purdue Level 1–3.5 OT / SCADA Conduit Validation](#recipe-5--purdue-level-135-conduit-validation-modbus-s7comm-dnp3-bacnet-ethernetip--opcua) |
| **Application stalls caused by a full receive buffer (`TCP ZeroWindow` & Window Update)** | `TCP` (`WIN 0`, Keep-Alive probe, `WIN 32768`), `HTTP` (`POST`, `202 Accepted`) | [Recipe 6A — TCP Zero-Window Stall & Recovery Reproducer](#recipe-6a--application-troubleshooting-reproducer-tcp-zero-window-stall--window-update-recovery) |

## 1. Simulating SNMP Traps & Polls (`SNMPv1`, `SNMPv2c` & Encrypted `SNMPv3`)

When configuring an NMS or trap receiver (**Zabbix**, **LibreNMS**, **Checkmk**, **PRTG**, **Datadog**, **SolarWinds**, or **`snmptrapd`**), simulating SNMP traps manually is a pain:
* You cannot unplug production uplinks or overheat chassis power supplies just to trigger a `linkDown` or thermal trap.
* Running `snmptrap` from the CLI requires configuring agents, hunting down vendor MIB files, remembering arcane positional arguments, and fighting hex EngineID and SNMPv3 USM key-localization flags.

FrameAssembly solves it with a few lines of `.fasm` code and two CLI commands (`frameassembly` to compile + `tcpreplay` to inject)—encoding ASN.1 BER structures and computing RFC 3414 / 3826 / 7860 SNMPv3 key localization, HMAC authentication digests, and DES/AES payload encryption automatically.

### Recipe 1A — `SNMPv1` Generic/Enterprise Traps & `SNMPv2c` Polls, Traps, and Informs

Save as `snmp_v1_v2c_alerts.fasm`:

```frameassembly
host core_switch {
    ip 10.100.0.254
    mac 00:1c:73:a0:00:fe
}

host nms_collector {
    ip 10.100.0.10
    mac 00:50:56:a0:00:10
}

flow snmp_v1_and_v2c_verification(sw, nms) {
    // 1. SNMPv1 generic linkDown trap (gentrap 2, spectrap 0) for interface index 5
    sw -> nms snmp1 trap community "public" enterprise 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.1.1 agentip 10.100.0.254 gentrap 2 spectrap 0 sysuptime 125000 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1.5 int 5 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.5 string "GigabitEthernet0/5" wait 5ms

    // 2. SNMPv1 vendor enterprise-specific trap (gentrap 6, spectrap 1 = chassis temperature alarm)
    sw -> nms snmp1 trap community "public" enterprise 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.13.3 agentip 10.100.0.254 gentrap 6 spectrap 1 sysuptime 125100 varbind 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.13.1.3.1.3.1 gauge32 84 wait 10ms

    // 3. SNMPv2c GET poll from NMS and switch RESPONSE with sysName.0 and sysUpTime.0
    nms -> sw snmp2 get community "noc_ro" reqid 1001 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 null varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 null wait 2ms
    nms <- sw snmp2 response community "noc_ro" reqid 1001 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "core-sw-01.dc1.example.com" varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 timeticks 8640000 wait 10ms

    // 4. SNMPv2c linkUp trap (1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4) with 64-bit interface counter (Counter64)
    sw -> nms snmp2 trap community "noc_traps" reqid 2001 sysuptime 125500 oid 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.1.5 string "TenGigabitEthernet1/1/5" varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.6.5 counter64 9876543210 wait 10ms

    // 5. SNMPv2c acknowledged InformRequest and NMS Response from UDP port 162
    sw -> nms snmp2 inform community "noc_traps" reqid 2002 sysuptime 126000 oid 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.5 int 1 wait 2ms
    sw <- nms snmp2 response community "noc_traps" srcport 162 reqid 2002 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.5 int 1
}

compile {
    snmp_v1_and_v2c_verification(core_switch, nms_collector)
}
```

#### Compile, Inspect & Replay:
```bash
frameassembly snmp_v1_v2c_alerts.fasm -o snmp_v1_v2c_alerts.pcap

# Verify PDU types, community strings, and varbind OIDs in tshark
tshark -r snmp_v1_v2c_alerts.pcap -Y "snmp" -V

# Replay traps toward your monitoring server on eth0
sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 snmp_v1_v2c_alerts.pcap
```

### Recipe 1B — Encrypted `SNMPv3` `authPriv` Traps & Informs (`SHA-256`/`SHA-512` + `AES-128` & `MD5`/`SHA-1` + `DES`)

This recipe generates authenticated and encrypted **SNMPv3 USM (`authPriv`)** packets across modern **RFC 7860 SHA-2** (`SHA256`, `SHA512`) with **RFC 3826 `AES-128-CFB`** as well as legacy **RFC 3414 `MD5`/`SHA-1`** with **`DES-CBC`** for older UPS/PDU hardware.

Save as `snmp_v3_encrypted.fasm`:

```frameassembly
host dist_router {
    ip 10.100.0.250
    mac 00:1c:73:a0:00:fa
}

host trap_receiver {
    ip 10.100.0.10
    mac 00:50:56:a0:00:10
}

flow snmpv3_usm_authpriv_suite(rtr, nms) {
    // 1. Modern SNMPv3 authPriv TRAP: HMAC-SHA256 + AES-128-CFB
    rtr -> nms snmp3 trap user "ops_sha256_aes" engineid "80001f8880001c73a000fa" engineboots 14 enginetime 86400 contextname "dc1_vrf" auth sha256 "AuthSecret_SHA256_2026!" priv aes "PrivSecret_AES128_2026!" reqid 3001 oid 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.13.3.0.1 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "dist-rtr-01.dc1" varbind 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.13.1.3.1.3.1 gauge32 89 wait 10ms

    // 2. High-security SNMPv3 authPriv INFORM + NMS RESPONSE: HMAC-SHA512 + AES-128-CFB
    rtr -> nms snmp3 inform user "sec_sha512_aes" engineid "80001f8880001c73a000fa" engineboots 14 enginetime 86405 contextname "dc1_vrf" auth sha512 "HighSecAuth_SHA512_Key!" priv aes "HighSecPriv_AES128_Key!" reqid 3002 oid 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.5 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "dist-rtr-01.dc1" wait 2ms
    rtr <- nms snmp3 response srcport 162 user "sec_sha512_aes" engineid "80001f8880001c73a000fa" engineboots 14 enginetime 86405 contextname "dc1_vrf" auth sha512 "HighSecAuth_SHA512_Key!" priv aes "HighSecPriv_AES128_Key!" reqid 3002 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "dist-rtr-01.dc1" wait 10ms

    // 3. Legacy SNMPv3 authPriv TRAPs for older UPS/branch appliances: HMAC-MD5 + DES and HMAC-SHA1 + DES
    rtr -> nms snmp3 trap user "legacy_ups_md5" engineid "80001f8880001c73a000fa" engineboots 3 enginetime 43200 auth md5 "LegacyUpsAuthMD5!" priv des "LegacyUpsPrivDES!" reqid 3003 oid 1.3.6.1.2.1.33.2.0.1 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.33.1.2.1.0 int 3 wait 10ms
    rtr -> nms snmp3 trap user "legacy_rtr_sha1" engineid "80001f8880001c73a000fa" engineboots 3 enginetime 43210 auth sha "LegacyRtrAuthSHA1!" priv des "LegacyRtrPrivDES!" reqid 3004 oid 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1.2 int 2
}

compile {
    snmpv3_usm_authpriv_suite(dist_router, trap_receiver)
}
```

#### Compile, Decrypt in `tshark` / Wireshark & Replay:
```bash
frameassembly snmp_v3_encrypted.fasm -o snmp_v3_encrypted.pcap

# Inspect SNMPv3 USM header fields (EngineID, Boots, Time, User, Auth/Priv parameters)
tshark -r snmp_v3_encrypted.pcap -T fields -e frame.number -e snmp.msgUserName -e snmp.msgAuthoritativeEngineID -e snmp.msgAuthoritativeEngineBoots -e snmp.msgAuthoritativeEngineTime

# Decrypt the ScopedPDU in Wireshark GUI:
#   Edit -> Preferences -> Protocols -> SNMP -> Users Table -> Edit...
#   Add Engine ID: 80001f8880001c73a000fa, Username: ops_sha256_aes,
#   Auth model: SHA2-256, Auth password: AuthSecret_SHA256_2026!,
#   Priv protocol: AES, Priv password: PrivSecret_AES128_2026!
wireshark snmp_v3_encrypted.pcap &
```

## 2. Testing Firewall Rules, ACLs & Stateful Inspection

Standard Linux utilities (`ping`, `curl`, `nc`) go through the local kernel's TCP/IP stack, which means you cannot easily emit an out-of-state `ACK` packet without an existing socket, craft a single capture containing both a permitted handshake and a rejected `RST ACK`, or test how a firewall handles fragmented packets and spoofed source IPs.

### Recipe 2A — DMZ & Perimeter Firewall Policy Audit (Handshakes, Rejections, Out-of-State & Stealth Probes)

Save as `firewall_dmz_audit.fasm`:

```frameassembly
host untrusted_client {
    ip 198.51.100.42
    mac 00:0c:29:11:22:33
}

host dmz_reverse_proxy {
    ip 203.0.113.10
    mac 00:1b:21:aa:bb:cc
}

flow perimeter_acl_audit(ext, dmz) {
    // 1. Permitted TCP port 443 (HTTPS) 3-way handshake with modern TCP options
    ext -> dmz tcp syn srcport 51001 dstport 443 win 64240 mss 1460 wscale 7 sack_perm wait 1ms
    ext <- dmz tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wscale 7 sack_perm wait 1ms
    ext -> dmz tcp ack wait 5ms

    // 2. Blocked MySQL port 3306 connection attempt rejected immediately with TCP RST+ACK
    ext -> dmz tcp syn srcport 51002 dstport 3306 win 64240 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    ext <- dmz tcp rst ack wait 5ms

    // 3. Out-of-state TCP ACK scan on SSH port 22 (verifies stateful firewall drops unsolicited ACKs)
    ext -> dmz tcp ack srcport 51003 dstport 22 seq 85000 acknum 42000 win 1024 wait 5ms

    // 4. Christmas-tree stealth probe (FIN + PSH + URG) on SMB port 445
    ext -> dmz tcp fin psh urg srcport 51004 dstport 445 win 1024 urgent 1 wait 5ms

    // 5. Blocked ICMP ping across DMZ VLAN 40 answered with ICMP Destination Unreachable,
    //    Code 13 (Communication Administratively Prohibited by ACL)
    ext -> dmz vlan 40 ttl 64 icmp echo_request id 900 seq 1 payload "DMZ_PING_AUDIT" wait 1ms
    ext <- dmz vlan 40 ttl 64 icmp dest_unreach code 13
}

compile {
    perimeter_acl_audit(untrusted_client, dmz_reverse_proxy)
}
```

#### Compile, Inspect & Replay:
```bash
frameassembly firewall_dmz_audit.fasm -o firewall_dmz_audit.pcap

# Verify TCP flags, ports, and ICMP unreachable code
tshark -r firewall_dmz_audit.pcap

# Inject into firewall outside interface eth1
sudo tcpreplay -i eth1 firewall_dmz_audit.pcap
```

### Recipe 2B — Path MTU Discovery (`DF`), IPv4 Fragmentation (`MF` + `FRAGOFFSET`) & Spoofed Source Egress Filtering

When tuning IPSec/GRE/VXLAN tunnel overhead or auditing anti-spoofing (BCP 38 / uRPF) rules, you need to verify that:
1. Oversized packets with **Don't Fragment (`df`)** trigger **ICMP Destination Unreachable, Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed and DF Set)** instead of being silently blackholed.
2. Legitimate **IPv4 fragments (`mf` + `fragoffset`)** sharing an `ipid` are reassembled by stateful inspection.
3. Packets from a **spoofed RFC 1918 / external source IP** on an internal port are dropped by ingress/egress ACLs.

Save as `firewall_mtu_frag_spoof.fasm`:

```frameassembly
host branch_client {
    ip 10.40.10.25
    mac 00:1c:73:40:10:25
}

host wan_firewall {
    ip 10.40.10.1
    mac 00:1c:73:40:10:01
}

// Host representing a spoofed external source IP on the same physical LAN MAC
host spoofed_source {
    ip 198.51.100.250
    mac 00:1c:73:40:10:25
}

flow mtu_fragmentation_and_bcp38(client, fw, spoof) {
    // 1. Path MTU Discovery probe with Don't Fragment (DF) bit set
    //    Firewall responds with ICMP Type 3, Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed and DF Set)
    client -> fw df ipid 0x3100 ttl 64 udp srcport 55100 dstport 443 payload "PMTUD_PROBE_DO_NOT_FRAGMENT_PAYLOAD" wait 1ms
    client <- fw ttl 64 icmp dest_unreach code 4 wait 5ms

    // 2. IPv4 Fragmentation inspection test (both fragments share IPID 0x4242):
    //    Fragment 1: MF bit set, fragment offset 0 (first 16 bytes = 2 x 8-byte blocks)
    client -> fw ipid 0x4242 mf fragoffset 0 ttl 64 icmp echo_request id 77 seq 1 payload "FRAG_BLOCK_ONE_A" wait 1ms
    //    Fragment 2: MF bit cleared, fragment offset 2 (starts at byte 16)
    client -> fw ipid 0x4242 fragoffset 2 ttl 64 icmp echo_request id 77 seq 1 payload "FRAG_BLOCK_TWO_B" wait 2ms
    client <- fw ttl 64 icmp echo_reply id 77 seq 1 payload "FRAG_REASSEMBLED_OK" wait 5ms

    // 3. BCP 38 / uRPF anti-spoofing test: internal MAC attempting to send with an external source IP
    spoof -> fw ttl 64 udp srcport 59999 dstport 53 payload "SPOOFED_EGRESS_TEST"
}

compile {
    mtu_fragmentation_and_bcp38(branch_client, wan_firewall, spoofed_source)
}
```

#### Compile, Inspect & Replay:
```bash
frameassembly firewall_mtu_frag_spoof.fasm -o firewall_mtu_frag_spoof.pcap

# Check IPv4 DF/MF flags, fragment offsets, and IP IDs
tshark -r firewall_mtu_frag_spoof.pcap -T fields -e frame.number -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e ip.id -e ip.flags.df -e ip.flags.mf -e ip.frag_offset -e icmp.code

# Replay against the firewall inside test port
sudo tcpreplay -i eth2 firewall_mtu_frag_spoof.pcap
```
