# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md`

# Layer 7 Web, Cloud-Native, Transport Security, VoIP & Remote Access Reference

Testing a Web Application Firewall (WAF), verifying TLS 1.3 SNI/ALPN inspection or UDP `443` QUIC pinholes, auditing a VoIP Session Border Controller (SBC), or triggering IDS rules for legacy Telnet/FTP shouldn't require spinning up Docker containers, Nginx reverse proxies, throwaway certificate authorities, and Asterisk PBXs. FrameAssembly solves that with a few lines of `.fasm` code and two CLI commands:

```bash
# 1. Compile the .fasm code into a deterministic .pcap capture
frameassembly web.fasm -o web.pcap

# 2. Replay the capture onto the wire (or inspect web.pcap in Wireshark / Suricata)
sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 web.pcap
```

This guide covers **16 Layer 7 web, cloud-native, transport security, VoIP, and remote access protocols** across IPv4 and IPv6:
**`HTTP`**, **`HTTP2`**, **`GRPC`**, **`WEBSOCKET`**, **`TLS`**, **`QUIC`**, **`TFTP`**, **`FTP`**, **`SSH`**, **`TELNET`**, **`WHOIS`**, **`SIP`**, **`RTP`**, **`RTSP`**, **`STUN`**, and **`SSDP`**.

> **Where to Find IoT & Message Broker Protocols (`MQTT`, `COAP`, `AMQP`):**
> Those three protocols are documented in [**Layer 7 Mail, Directory, Storage, Databases & Message Brokers (`l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md`)**](l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md#5-message-brokers--iot-telemetry-mqtt-coap-amqp).

---

## Quick Protocol & Default Port Matrix

Every protocol below works with **zero mandatory modifiers** (emitting a complete, RFC-compliant default frame on its standard port) or with explicit header overrides.

| Protocol | Keyword | Default Transport & Port | Standard / RFC | Common Network & Security Testing Use Cases |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **HTTP/1.1** | `HTTP` | TCP `80` | RFC 9110 / RFC 9112 | WAF rule validation, reverse-proxy routing, REST API health checks |
| **HTTP/2** | `HTTP2` | TCP `443` | RFC 9113 / RFC 7541 | Multiplexed stream inspection, `GOAWAY` graceful drain, `SETTINGS` tuning |
| **gRPC** | `GRPC` | TCP `50051` | gRPC over HTTP/2 | Kubernetes service-mesh telemetry, Protobuf RPC status code testing |
| **WebSocket** | `WEBSOCKET` | TCP `80` | RFC 6455 | Full-duplex masked client frames, `PING`/`PONG` keepalives, proxy upgrades |
| **TLS 1.2 / 1.3** | `TLS` | TCP `443` | RFC 8446 / RFC 6066 | Firewall SNI/ALPN filtering, cipher-suite policy audits, TLS alert handling |
| **QUIC / HTTP/3** | `QUIC` | UDP `443` | RFC 9000 / RFC 9114 | UDP `443` firewall pinholes, Connection ID migration, Retry token validation |
| **SSH-2** | `SSH` | TCP `22` | RFC 4253 / RFC 4252 | Bastion access ACLs, SSH version banner audits, `KEXINIT` algorithm inspection |
| **Telnet** | `TELNET` | TCP `23` | RFC 854 / RFC 855 | Legacy out-of-band console detection, IDS cleartext management alerts |
| **TFTP** | `TFTP` | UDP `69` | RFC 1350 | PXE network boot, switch Zero-Touch Provisioning (ZTP), firmware transfers |
| **FTP** | `FTP` | TCP `21` | RFC 959 / RFC 2428 | Firewall FTP ALG / passive helper testing, cleartext credential detection |
| **WHOIS** | `WHOIS` | TCP `43` | RFC 3912 | SOC domain/IP enrichment lookups, RIR/registrar query simulation |
| **SIP** | `SIP` | UDP / TCP `5060` | RFC 3261 / RFC 4566 | VoIP Session Border Controller (SBC) call setup, SIP ALG inspection |
| **RTP** | `RTP` | UDP `5004` | RFC 3550 / RFC 3551 | DSCP `EF` (`46`) voice/video QoS queue verification, jitter/sequence tests |
| **RTSP** | `RTSP` | TCP `554` | RFC 7826 / RFC 2326 | IP security camera NVR streams, media transport port negotiation |
| **STUN** | `STUN` | UDP `3478` | RFC 8489 / RFC 5389 | WebRTC ICE NAT traversal, `XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS` reflexive IP discovery |
| **SSDP / UPnP** | `SSDP` | UDP `1900` | UPnP DA 1.1 / 2.0 | Multicast IoT/printer discovery (`239.255.255.250`), rogue UPnP auditing |

> **Shared 4-Tuple TCP State & Port Overrides:**
> All TCP-based Layer 7 statements automatically emit a `PSH ACK` segment on that protocol's default port and share sequence/acknowledgment numbers (`SEQ`/`ACKNUM`) with raw `TCP` statements between the same two hosts and ports. You can override source or destination ports on any statement using `srcport <0..65535>` and `dstport <0..65535>`, or add Layer 2/Layer 3 tags (`vlan <id>`, `qinq <s_vid> inner_vlan <c_vid>`, `mpls <label>`, `dscp <0..63>`, `ttl <0..255>`) anywhere on the line.

---

## 1. Web, API & Microservice Protocols (`HTTP`, `HTTP2`, `GRPC`, `WEBSOCKET`)

### 1.1 HTTP/1.1 (`HTTP` — Default: TCP Port `80`)

Testing WAF signatures, reverse-proxy header routing (`X-Forwarded-For`, `Host`), or Suricata HTTP rules with `curl` only captures traffic if you already have a live backend server listening and returning the exact status code and JSON body you need. In `.fasm` code, you script both the client request and server response directly—`HTTP` builds CRLF-delimited RFC 9112 HTTP/1.1 messages over TCP port `80`:
- **Request vs. Response:** If `STATUS` (or `REASON`) is specified, FrameAssembly emits an HTTP response (`HTTP/1.1 <status> <reason>\r\n...`). Otherwise, it emits an HTTP request (`<method> <uri> HTTP/<version>\r\n...`).
- **Automatic `Content-Length`:** Whenever you include `BODY "<text>"`, FrameAssembly automatically computes the exact byte length of the body and appends a matching `Content-Length: <n>\r\n` header before the blank `\r\n\r\n` separator.
- **Setting the HTTP `Host:` Header with `HOST_HDR`:** Because `HOST` is a top-level keyword used to declare network endpoints (`host web_srv { ip 10.0.0.10 }`), use `HOST_HDR "<hostname>"` inside `HTTP` statements to set the HTTP `Host:` header without ambiguity.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shorthand Verb** | `GET` \| `POST` \| `PUT` \| `DELETE` \| `HEAD` \| `OPTIONS` \| `PATCH` | `GET` | Standalone keyword setting the HTTP request method |
| **`METHOD`** | `METHOD "<verb>"` | `"GET"` | Explicit HTTP method string (e.g., `"POST"`, `"PROPFIND"`, `"TRACE"`) |
| **`URI`** | `URI "<path>"` | `"/"` | Request target path or query string (e.g., `"/api/v1/orders?limit=10"`) |
| **`VERSION`** | `VERSION "<ver>"` | `"1.1"` | HTTP protocol version string (`"1.1"` or `"1.0"`) |
| **`HOST_HDR`** | `HOST_HDR "<host>"` | `"localhost"` | Sets the HTTP `Host:` header (never write `HOST` inside an `HTTP` statement) |
| **`USER_AGENT`** | `USER_AGENT "<ua>"` | Omitted | Appends `User-Agent: <ua>\r\n` |
| **`CONTENT_TYPE`** | `CONTENT_TYPE "<mime>"` | Omitted | Appends `Content-Type: <mime>\r\n` (e.g., `"application/json"`) |
| **`HEADER`** | `HEADER "<Key>" "<Val>"` | None | Appends a custom `Key: Val\r\n` header; may be repeated multiple times |
| **`STATUS`** | `STATUS <100..599>` | `200` (if response) | Switches frame to an HTTP response with the given status code (`200`, `404`, `503`) |
| **`REASON`** | `REASON "<phrase>"` | Auto-derived | Response reason phrase (`"OK"`, `"Created"`, `"Forbidden"`) |
| **`BODY`** | `BODY "<text>"` | Empty | Appends message body and automatically adds `Content-Length: <len>` |

### 1.2 HTTP/2 (`HTTP2` — Default: TCP Port `443`)

Crafting binary HTTP/2 stream multiplexing, flow-control `WINDOW_UPDATE` frames, or graceful `GOAWAY` connection drains by hand is miserable because RFC 9113 packs length, type, flags, and stream IDs into a binary 9-byte header. `HTTP2` builds those RFC 9113 binary frames (24-bit length, 8-bit frame type, 8-bit flags, 1-bit reserved bit, and 31-bit stream ID) and the optional 24-byte client connection preface (`PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n`) straight from readable modifiers. Multiple frame type flags can be combined in a single packet (such as `preface settings`).

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`PREFACE`** | `PREFACE` | Off | Prepends the 24-byte RFC 9113 client connection preface string |
| **`SETTINGS`** | `SETTINGS` | Default if none set | Emits Frame Type `0x04` (`SETTINGS`, 6-byte parameter entry) |
| **`HEADERS`** | `HEADERS` | Off | Emits Frame Type `0x01` (`HEADERS` with `END_HEADERS = 0x04`) |
| **`DATA`** | `DATA` | Off | Emits Frame Type `0x00` (`DATA` with `END_STREAM = 0x01`) |
| **`WINDOW_UPDATE`** | `WINDOW_UPDATE` | Off | Emits Frame Type `0x08` (`WINDOW_UPDATE`, 4-byte window increment) |
| **`PING`** | `PING` | Off | Emits Frame Type `0x06` (`PING`, 8-byte opaque payload) |
| **`GOAWAY`** | `GOAWAY` | Off | Emits Frame Type `0x07` (`GOAWAY`, last stream ID + error code) |
| **`STREAM_ID`** | `STREAM_ID <number>` | `0` or `1` | 31-bit HTTP/2 Stream ID (`0` for connection control, odd `1, 3, 5` for client streams) |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Default per type | Custom frame payload bytes |

### 1.3 gRPC (`GRPC` — Default: TCP Port `50051`)

Reproducing a Kubernetes service-mesh RPC failure (like `grpc-status: 14 UNAVAILABLE` or `7 PERMISSION_DENIED`) normally requires compiling `.proto` files and running client/server stubs behind Envoy or Istio. Instead, `GRPC` builds HTTP/2 frames on TCP port `50051` carrying `/package.Service/Method` call paths, 5-byte length-prefixed Protocol Buffers envelopes (1-byte compression flag `0x00` + 32-bit big-endian message length), and `grpc-status` trailer codes directly from `.fasm` code.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`SERVICE`** | `SERVICE "<pkg.Svc>"` | `"grpc.health.v1.Health"` | Fully qualified Protobuf service name |
| **`METHOD`** | `METHOD "<Rpc>"` | `"Check"` | Target RPC method name (combined on wire as `/<SERVICE>/<METHOD>`) |
| **`GRPC_STATUS`** | `GRPC_STATUS <0..16>` | Omitted (Request) | Emits a gRPC response trailer (`0` `OK`, `1` `CANCELLED`, `3` `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `4` `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `5` `NOT_FOUND`, `7` `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `14` `UNAVAILABLE`, `16` `UNAUTHENTICATED`) |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Serialized Protobuf message body wrapped in the 5-byte gRPC length prefix |

### 1.4 WebSocket (`WEBSOCKET` — Default: TCP Port `80`)

RFC 6455 mandates that every client-to-server WebSocket frame be XOR-masked with a 32-bit key—which means a naive packet generator produces malformed frames that Wireshark and proxies reject. `WEBSOCKET` builds binary RFC 6455 frames with configurable opcodes, `FIN` bit fragmentation control, and automatic 32-bit XOR payload masking whenever `MASK_KEY` is provided.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shorthand Opcode** | `TEXT` \| `BINARY` \| `CLOSE` \| `PING` \| `PONG` | `TEXT` | Bare keyword setting the 4-bit WebSocket opcode (`0x1`, `0x2`, `0x8`, `0x9`, `0xA`) |
| **`OPCODE`** | `OPCODE "<name>"` | `"TEXT"` | Explicit opcode name (`"TEXT"`, `"BINARY"`, `"CLOSE"`, `"PING"`, `"PONG"`, `"CONTINUATION"`) |
| **`FIN_BIT`** | `FIN_BIT <0\|1>` | `1` | `1` = final fragment in message; `0` = more fragments follow |
| **`MASK_KEY`** | `MASK_KEY <32-bit_hex>` | Unmasked | Sets the `MASK` bit (`0x80`), writes the 4-byte key, and XOR-masks the payload on the wire |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | `"Hello WebSocket"` | Application text or binary payload (automatically XOR-masked if `MASK_KEY` is set) |

### Compilable Example: Web API Gateway, HTTP/2, gRPC & WebSocket Stream

```frameassembly
host api_gateway { ip 10.120.1.10 mac 00:1b:21:10:01:0a }
host app_service { ip 10.120.1.50 mac 00:1b:21:10:01:32 }

flow web_and_microservice_tier(gw, svc) {
    // 1. HTTP/1.1 POST request with custom headers and JSON body + 201 Created response
    gw -> svc http post uri "/v1/orders" version "1.1" host_hdr "api.corp.example.com" user_agent "Envoy/1.31" content_type "application/json" header "X-Request-Id" "req-4092" header "X-Forwarded-Proto" "https" body "{\"sku\":\"RTR-9000\",\"qty\":2}" wait 1ms
    gw <- svc http version "1.1" status 201 reason "Created" content_type "application/json" header "X-Request-Id" "req-4092" body "{\"order_id\":8801,\"status\":\"confirmed\"}" wait 2ms

    // 2. HTTP/2 connection preface, settings exchange, stream 1 request, and graceful GOAWAY
    gw -> svc http2 preface settings stream_id 0 wait 1ms
    gw <- svc http2 settings window_update stream_id 0 wait 1ms
    gw -> svc http2 headers stream_id 1 payload ":method GET :path /v2/inventory" wait 1ms
    gw <- svc http2 data stream_id 1 payload "{\"in_stock\":true}" wait 1ms
    gw -> svc http2 ping stream_id 0 wait 1ms
    gw <- svc http2 goaway stream_id 0 wait 2ms

    // 3. gRPC unary RPC call and OK response on TCP 50051
    gw -> svc grpc service "inventory.v1.StockService" method "ReserveItems" payload "PROTOBUF_RESERVE_REQ" wait 1ms
    gw <- svc grpc service "inventory.v1.StockService" method "ReserveItems" grpc_status 0 payload "PROTOBUF_RESERVE_OK" wait 2ms

    // 4. WebSocket client-masked TEXT frame, server unmasked reply, PING/PONG, and CLOSE
    gw -> svc websocket text fin_bit 1 mask_key 0x37fa213d payload "{\"subscribe\":\"order_events\"}" wait 1ms
    gw <- svc websocket opcode "TEXT" fin_bit 1 payload "{\"event\":\"ORDER_SHIPPED\",\"id\":8801}" wait 1ms
    gw -> svc websocket ping fin_bit 1 mask_key 0x11223344 payload "hb" wait 1ms
    gw <- svc websocket pong fin_bit 1 payload "hb" wait 1ms
    gw -> svc websocket close fin_bit 1 mask_key 0x37fa213d payload ""
}

compile {
    web_and_microservice_tier(api_gateway, app_service)
}
```

---

## 2. Transport Security & Next-Gen Web (`TLS`, `QUIC`)

### 2.1 Transport Layer Security (`TLS` — Default: TCP Port `443`)

Next-generation firewalls, egress proxies, and IDS sensors inspect the cleartext `ClientHello` for Server Name Indication (`SNI`), Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (`ALPN`), and weak cipher suites. Rather than generating throwaway OpenSSL certificates and running `openssl s_client` against a dummy server, you can declare the exact `SNI`, `ALPN`, and `CIPHERSUITE` in `.fasm` code. `TLS` builds RFC 5246 (TLS 1.2) and RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3) 5-byte Record Layer headers (`ContentType`, `RecordVersion`, `Length`) and Handshake messages (`ClientHello`, `ServerHello`, `Certificate`, `Finished`) complete with RFC 6066 `SNI` and RFC 7301 `ALPN` extensions.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`CLIENT_HELLO`** | `CLIENT_HELLO` | Default if none set | Handshake Type `1` (`ClientHello`) with 32-byte random, cipher suite, SNI, and ALPN |
| **`SERVER_HELLO`** | `SERVER_HELLO` | Off | Handshake Type `2` (`ServerHello`) selecting cipher suite and ALPN |
| **`CERTIFICATE`** | `CERTIFICATE` | Off | Handshake Type `11` (`Certificate`) carrying X.509 certificate payload |
| **`FINISHED`** | `FINISHED` | Off | Handshake Type `20` (`Finished`) carrying handshake verify data |
| **`APP_DATA`** | `APP_DATA` | Off | Record ContentType `23` (`ApplicationData`) carrying encrypted record bytes |
| **`ALERT`** | `ALERT` | Off | Record ContentType `21` (`Alert`, e.g., `close_notify` or `handshake_failure`) |
| **`RECORD_VERSION`** | `RECORD_VERSION <0..65535>` | `0x0303` | Outer 16-bit TLS record version (`0x0301` = TLS 1.0, `0x0303` = TLS 1.2) |
| **`HANDSHAKE_VERSION`**| `HANDSHAKE_VERSION <0..65535>`| `0x0303` | Inner 16-bit handshake client/server version (`0x0303` = TLS 1.2 / TLS 1.3 legacy) |
| **`SNI`** | `SNI "<hostname>"` | Omitted | Encodes TLS Extension `0x0000` (`server_name`) for firewall SNI inspection |
| **`CIPHERSUITE`** | `CIPHERSUITE <0..65535>` | `0x1301` (`4865`) | 16-bit IANA Cipher Suite (`4865`/`0x1301` = `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`, `4866`/`0x1302` = `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`, `4867`/`0x1303` = `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256`) |
| **`ALPN`** | `ALPN "<proto>"` | Omitted | Encodes TLS Extension `0x0010` (`"h2"`, `"http/1.1"`, `"grpc-exp"`) |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Default per type | Custom certificate, verify data, alert, or encrypted application payload |

### 2.2 QUIC & HTTP/3 Transport (`QUIC` — Default: UDP Port `443`)

Verifying how firewalls and middleboxes handle UDP port `443` HTTP/3 traffic—whether they allow QUIC `Initial` handshakes, validate `Retry` tokens, or force a fallback to TCP—is tricky without a full QUIC stack. `QUIC` builds RFC 9000 QUIC Long Header packets (`INITIAL`, `ZERO_RTT`, `HANDSHAKE`, `RETRY`) with RFC 9000 §16 2-byte variable-length integer payload lengths and 1-RTT `SHORT` Header packets over UDP port `443`.
- **Important Syntax Note on `DCID` and `SCID`:** Destination and Source Connection IDs (`DCID` and `SCID`) take **unquoted 64-bit integer or hexadecimal values** (for example `dcid 0x8394c8f03e515708`), never quoted strings.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`INITIAL`** | `INITIAL` | Default if none set | Long Header Type `0x00` (`Initial`, carries Token length + Token + Packet Number) |
| **`ZERO_RTT`** | `ZERO_RTT` | Off | Long Header Type `0x01` (`0-RTT` early data packet) |
| **`HANDSHAKE`** | `HANDSHAKE` | Off | Long Header Type `0x02` (`Handshake` cryptographic exchange) |
| **`RETRY`** | `RETRY` | Off | Long Header Type `0x03` (`Retry` address validation packet) |
| **`SHORT`** | `SHORT` | Off | 1-RTT Short Header (`Header Form = 0`, `Fixed Bit = 1`, `DCID` + `PKT_NUM`) |
| **`VERSION`** | `VERSION <number>` | `1` (`0x00000001`) | 32-bit QUIC version (`1` = RFC 9000 QUIC v1, `0x6b3343cf` = RFC 9369 QUIC v2) |
| **`DCID`** | `DCID <64-bit_id>` | `0x0102030405060708` | 64-bit Destination Connection ID (unquoted integer or `0x...` hex value) |
| **`SCID`** | `SCID <64-bit_id>` | `0x1112131415161718` | 64-bit Source Connection ID (unquoted integer or `0x...` hex value) |
| **`TOKEN`** | `TOKEN "<text>"` | Empty | Address validation token string included in `INITIAL` or `RETRY` packets |
| **`PKT_NUM`** | `PKT_NUM <number>` | `1` | Packet number encoded into `INITIAL`, `ZERO_RTT`, `HANDSHAKE`, or `SHORT` headers |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Default per type | Encrypted QUIC frames / HTTP/3 payload bytes |

### Compilable Example: TLS 1.3 Inspection & QUIC v1 / HTTP/3 Handshake over IPv6

```frameassembly
host client_v6   { ip 2001:db8:443::50 }
host cdn_edge_v6 { ip 2001:db8:443::1 }

flow tls13_and_quic_v1(c, s) {
    // 1. TLS 1.3 handshake with SNI and ALPN "h2", encrypted AppData, and close_notify Alert
    c -> s tls client_hello record_version 0x0301 handshake_version 0x0303 sni "edge.cdn.example.com" ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 1ms
    c <- s tls server_hello record_version 0x0303 handshake_version 0x0303 ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 1ms
    c <- s tls certificate record_version 0x0303 payload "X509_ECDSA_CERT_CHAIN" wait 1ms
    c <- s tls finished record_version 0x0303 payload "SERVER_HANDSHAKE_VERIFY" wait 1ms
    c -> s tls finished record_version 0x0303 payload "CLIENT_HANDSHAKE_VERIFY" wait 1ms
    c -> s tls app_data record_version 0x0303 payload "ENCRYPTED_HTTP2_GET_REQUEST" wait 1ms
    c <- s tls app_data record_version 0x0303 payload "ENCRYPTED_HTTP2_200_RESPONSE" wait 1ms
    c -> s tls alert record_version 0x0303 payload "CLOSE_NOTIFY" wait 5ms

    // 2. QUIC v1 Initial -> Retry with token -> Initial -> 0-RTT -> Handshake -> 1-RTT Short Header
    c -> s quic initial version 1 dcid 0x8394c8f03e515708 scid 0x1122334455667788 pkt_num 1 payload "CRYPTO_CLIENT_HELLO" wait 1ms
    c <- s quic retry version 1 dcid 0x1122334455667788 scid 0x9988776655443322 token "quic_retry_tok_v1" wait 1ms
    c -> s quic initial version 1 dcid 0x9988776655443322 scid 0x1122334455667788 token "quic_retry_tok_v1" pkt_num 2 payload "CRYPTO_CLIENT_HELLO_RETRY" wait 1ms
    c -> s quic zero_rtt version 1 dcid 0x9988776655443322 scid 0x1122334455667788 pkt_num 3 payload "HTTP3_0RTT_GET_INDEX" wait 1ms
    c <- s quic handshake version 1 dcid 0x1122334455667788 scid 0x9988776655443322 pkt_num 1 payload "CRYPTO_SERVER_FINISHED" wait 1ms
    c <- s quic short dcid 0x1122334455667788 pkt_num 2 payload "HTTP3_200_OK_HEADERS_AND_DATA"
}

compile {
    tls13_and_quic_v1(client_v6, cdn_edge_v6)
}
```

---

## 3. Remote Access, File Transfer & Domain Lookup (`SSH`, `TELNET`, `TFTP`, `FTP`, `WHOIS`)

### 3.1 Secure Shell (`SSH` — Default: TCP Port `22`)

Security teams frequently write IDS rules and bastion ACLs to flag outdated SSH client/server banners (like `OpenSSH_7.2`) or weak key-exchange algorithms during the cleartext handshake. `SSH` builds RFC 4253 version banners (`SSH-2.0-...`) and binary SSH packet framing (`packet_length`, `padding_length`, `msg_code`, 16-byte `KEXINIT` cookie + algorithm negotiation lists, `NEWKEYS`, and encrypted channel payloads) on TCP port `22`.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`BANNER`** | `BANNER "<text>"` | `"SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.3"` | Emits CRLF-terminated version exchange string (`SSH-2.0-...\r\n`) |
| **`KEXINIT`** | `KEXINIT` | Off | Emits `SSH_MSG_KEXINIT` (`msg_code = 20`) with 16-byte cookie and kex algorithm lists |
| **`NEWKEYS`** | `NEWKEYS` | Off | Emits `SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS` (`msg_code = 21`) signaling transition to encrypted keys |
| **`MSG_CODE`** | `MSG_CODE <0..255>` | `20` (if binary) | Explicit SSH message code (`5` Service Req, `50` UserAuth Req, `52` UserAuth Success, `90` Channel Open, `94` Channel Data) |
| **`COOKIE`** | `COOKIE "<hex_or_text>"` | 16-byte default | Custom 16-byte KEXINIT cookie value |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Additional SSH binary packet body or encrypted channel data |

### 3.2 Telnet (`TELNET` — Default: TCP Port `23`)

Every enterprise SOC has an alert rule for unauthorized Telnet login prompts on management VLANs, but nobody wants to enable `telnetd` on a core switch just to test the sensor. `TELNET` builds RFC 854 Interpret As Command (`IAC = 0xFF`) option negotiation sequences (`WILL = 0xFB`, `WONT = 0xFC`, `DO = 0xFD`, `DONT = 0xFE`) and NVT-ASCII terminal lines over TCP port `23`.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`WILL`** | `WILL [OPTION] <0..255>` | Omitted | Emits 3-byte `0xFF 0xFB <opt>` (`1` Echo, `3` Suppress Go Ahead, `24` TermType, `31` NAWS) |
| **`WONT`** | `WONT [OPTION] <0..255>` | Omitted | Emits 3-byte `0xFF 0xFC <opt>` refusing to perform option |
| **`DO`** | `DO [OPTION] <0..255>` | Omitted | Emits 3-byte `0xFF 0xFD <opt>` requesting peer to enable option |
| **`DONT`** | `DONT [OPTION] <0..255>` | Omitted | Emits 3-byte `0xFF 0xFE <opt>` requesting peer to disable option |
| **`OPTION`** | `OPTION <0..255>` | Omitted | Standalone option code when no negotiation verb is specified |
| **`DATA`** | `DATA "<text>"` | Omitted | Terminal text line or CLI command string (appended after any IAC bytes) |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Omitted | Additional raw terminal bytes |

### 3.3 Trivial File Transfer Protocol (`TFTP` — Default: UDP Port `69`)

Troubleshooting PXE network boot, switch Zero-Touch Provisioning (`ZTP`), or VoIP phone firmware downloads over UDP port `69` is straightforward when you can script the exact block-by-block transfer or `File not found` error in `.fasm` code. `TFTP` builds RFC 1350 UDP file transfer packets (`RRQ`, `WRQ`, `DATA`, `ACK`, `ERROR`) with 16-bit block counters and NUL-terminated filenames and transfer modes.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`RRQ`** | `RRQ` | Default if none set | Opcode `1` (Read Request: `0x0001` + `FILENAME` + `0x00` + `MODE` + `0x00`) |
| **`WRQ`** | `WRQ` | Off | Opcode `2` (Write Request: `0x0002` + `FILENAME` + `0x00` + `MODE` + `0x00`) |
| **`DATA`** | `DATA` | Off | Opcode `3` (Data block: `0x0003` + 16-bit `BLOCK` + `PAYLOAD` bytes) |
| **`ACK`** | `ACK` | Off | Opcode `4` (Acknowledgment: `0x0004` + 16-bit `BLOCK`) |
| **`ERROR`** | `ERROR` (or `ERR`) | Auto if `ERRCODE` set | Opcode `5` (Error: `0x0005` + 16-bit `ERRCODE` + `ERRMSG` + `0x00`) |
| **`FILENAME`** | `FILENAME "<text>"` | `"boot.bin"` | Target filename for `RRQ` and `WRQ` packets |
| **`MODE`** | `MODE "<text>"` | `"octet"` | Transfer mode string (`"octet"` for binary or `"netascii"` for text) |
| **`BLOCK`** | `BLOCK <0..65535>` | `1` | 16-bit block counter for `DATA` and `ACK` (`0` acknowledges a `WRQ`) |
| **`ERRCODE`** | `ERRCODE <0..65535>` | `1` | TFTP error code (`1` File not found, `2` Access violation, `3` Disk full, `4` Illegal op, `6` File exists) |
| **`ERRMSG`** | `ERRMSG "<text>"` | `"File not found"` | Human-readable NUL-terminated error string |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Block data content for `DATA` frames |

### 3.4 File Transfer Protocol (`FTP` — Default: TCP Port `21`)

Testing firewall FTP Application Layer Gateways (ALGs)—which inspect `227 Entering Passive Mode` or `229 Entering Extended Passive Mode` replies to open dynamic data-channel pinholes—or validating cleartext credential IDS alerts is much faster in `.fasm` code than configuring `vsftpd`. `FTP` builds RFC 959 / RFC 2428 control-channel commands and 3-digit server status replies (`<CODE> <REPLY>\r\n` or `<CMD> <ARG>\r\n`) on TCP port `21`.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`CMD`** | `CMD "<verb>"` | `"USER"` | FTP client command (`"USER"`, `"PASS"`, `"SYST"`, `"FEAT"`, `"PWD"`, `"TYPE"`, `"PASV"`, `"EPSV"`, `"RETR"`, `"STOR"`, `"QUIT"`) |
| **`ARG`** | `ARG "<text>"` | Omitted | Command argument (e.g., `"anonymous"`, `"I"`, `"/pub/firmware.bin"`) |
| **`CODE`** | `CODE <100..599>` | Omitted (Command) | Emits a 3-digit FTP server response (`220` Ready, `331` Password required, `230` Logged in, `227` Passive Mode, `229` Extended Passive, `150` Opening data, `226` Transfer complete, `530` Login incorrect) |
| **`REPLY`** | `REPLY "<text>"` | `"OK"` | Server response text following `CODE` |

### 3.5 WHOIS Registry Lookup (`WHOIS` — Default: TCP Port `43`)

Testing SOC threat-intelligence enrichment scripts or outbound TCP port `43` firewall rules against live public RIR WHOIS servers from an isolated lab either gets rate-limited or blocked at an air-gapped perimeter. In `.fasm` code, `WHOIS` synthesizes both the RFC 3912 domain/IPv4/IPv6 CIDR/ASN query and the formatted registry response offline.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`QUERY`** | `QUERY` | Default if no `REGISTRAR` | Emits `<DOMAIN>\r\n` client query on TCP port 43 |
| **`RESPONSE`** | `RESPONSE` | Auto if `REGISTRAR` set | Emits formatted multi-line WHOIS registry record (`Domain Name:`, `Registrar:`) |
| **`DOMAIN`** | `DOMAIN "<text>"` | `"example.com"` | Queried domain name, IP prefix, or ASN |
| **`REGISTRAR`** | `REGISTRAR "<text>"` | `"IANA"` | Sponsoring registrar name included in `RESPONSE` records |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Additional WHOIS response lines (e.g., `Name Server:` or `NetRange:` fields) |

### Compilable Example: Bastion SSH/Telnet Access, Switch ZTP TFTP/FTP & WHOIS Audit

```frameassembly
host admin_ws    { ip 10.50.1.100 }
host core_switch { ip 10.50.1.1 }

flow remote_admin_and_provisioning(ws, sw) {
    // 1. SSH-2 version banner exchange, KEXINIT with cookie, NEWKEYS, and encrypted channel data
    ws -> sw ssh banner "SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6" wait 1ms
    sw -> ws ssh banner "SSH-2.0-Cisco-2.0" wait 1ms
    ws -> sw ssh kexinit cookie "00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff" wait 1ms
    sw -> ws ssh kexinit cookie "ffeeddccbbaa99887766554433221100" wait 1ms
    ws -> sw ssh newkeys wait 1ms
    sw -> ws ssh newkeys wait 1ms
    ws -> sw ssh msg_code 94 payload "ENCRYPTED_SHOW_RUNNING_CONFIG" wait 2ms

    // 2. Legacy Telnet IAC option negotiation (Echo=1, SGA=3) and CLI prompt
    ws -> sw telnet do 1 will 3 wait 1ms
    sw -> ws telnet will 1 do 3 data "User Access Verification\r\nUsername: " wait 1ms
    ws -> sw telnet data "netadmin\r\n" wait 2ms

    // 3. TFTP switch configuration download (RRQ -> DATA Block 1 -> ACK Block 1)
    sw -> ws tftp rrq filename "leaf01-startup.cfg" mode "octet" wait 1ms
    ws -> sw tftp data block 1 payload "hostname leaf01\ninterface Eth1/1\n" wait 1ms
    sw -> ws tftp ack block 1 wait 2ms

    // 4. FTP firmware archive login and passive mode retrieval
    ws <- sw ftp code 220 reply "Switch FTP Server Ready" wait 1ms
    ws -> sw ftp cmd "USER" arg "admin" wait 1ms
    ws <- sw ftp code 331 reply "Password required for admin" wait 1ms
    ws -> sw ftp cmd "PASS" arg "SwitchPass!2026" wait 1ms
    ws <- sw ftp code 230 reply "User admin logged in" wait 1ms
    ws -> sw ftp cmd "EPSV" wait 1ms
    ws <- sw ftp code 229 reply "Entering Extended Passive Mode (|||62001|)" wait 1ms
    ws -> sw ftp cmd "RETR" arg "nos-v10.4.bin" wait 1ms
    ws <- sw ftp code 226 reply "Transfer complete" wait 2ms

    // 5. WHOIS domain registration lookup and response
    ws -> sw whois query domain "corp-network.example.net" wait 1ms
    ws <- sw whois response domain "corp-network.example.net" registrar "Example Enterprise Registrar LLC"
}

compile {
    remote_admin_and_provisioning(admin_ws, core_switch)
}
```

---

## 4. VoIP, Streaming Media, NAT Traversal & UPnP (`SIP`, `RTP`, `RTSP`, `STUN`, `SSDP`)

### 4.1 Session Initiation Protocol (`SIP` — Default: UDP / TCP Port `5060`)

Debugging a broken VoIP call through a firewall SIP ALG or Session Border Controller (SBC) usually means digging out two hardware desk phones or wrestling with `sipp` XML templates. In `.fasm` code, each step of the dialog (`INVITE` -> `100 Trying` -> `180 Ringing` -> `200 OK` -> `ACK` -> `BYE`) is a single readable line: `SIP` builds RFC 3261 VoIP call control signaling and status responses with automatic `Content-Length` calculation whenever an SDP `BODY` is attached.
- **UDP vs. TCP Transport:** `SIP` defaults to UDP port `5060`. Add `transport tcp` on the statement to emit SIP over TCP port `5060`.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shorthand Method** | `INVITE` \| `ACK` \| `BYE` \| `CANCEL` \| `REGISTER` \| `OPTIONS` | `INVITE` | Standalone keyword setting the SIP request method |
| **`METHOD`** | `METHOD "<verb>"` | `"INVITE"` | Explicit SIP method string (e.g., `"PRACK"`, `"SUBSCRIBE"`, `"NOTIFY"`, `"REFER"`) |
| **`URI`** | `URI "<sip_uri>"` | `"sip:bob@example.com"` | Request-URI in the SIP Request-Line |
| **`STATUS`** | `STATUS <100..699>` | Omitted (Request) | Emits a SIP response (`SIP/2.0 <STATUS> <REASON>`, e.g., `100`, `180`, `200`, `401`, `486`) |
| **`REASON`** | `REASON "<text>"` | Auto-derived | Response reason phrase (`"Trying"`, `"Ringing"`, `"OK"`, `"Busy Here"`) |
| **`FROM`** | `FROM "<uri>"` | `"sip:alice@example.com"`| Sets the `From:` header URI |
| **`TO`** | `TO "<uri>"` | `"sip:bob@example.com"` | Sets the `To:` header URI |
| **`CALL_ID`** | `CALL_ID "<id>"` | `"fasm-call-1"` | Sets the `Call-ID:` dialog identifier header |
| **`CSEQ`** | `CSEQ <number>` | `1` | Sequence number in `CSeq: <n> <METHOD>` |
| **`VIA`** | `VIA "<text>"` | Auto-generated | Custom `Via:` header (e.g., `"SIP/2.0/UDP 10.80.1.50:5060;branch=z9hG4bK776"`) |
| **`CONTACT`** | `CONTACT "<uri>"` | Omitted | Sets the `Contact:` header |
| **`CONTENT_TYPE`** | `CONTENT_TYPE "<mime>"` | `"application/sdp"` (if `BODY`) | Sets the `Content-Type:` header |
| **`BODY`** | `BODY "<sdp>"` | Empty | Attaches an SDP media description body and computes `Content-Length` |
| **`TRANSPORT`** | `TRANSPORT TCP` \| `UDP` | `UDP` | Switches SIP between UDP port `5060` and TCP port `5060` |

### 4.2 Real-Time Transport Protocol (`RTP` — Default: UDP Port `5004`)

Once SIP negotiates a call, network engineers need to verify that the media stream (`G.711 PCMU`/`PCMA`, `G.722`, `Opus`) actually lands in the router's low-latency priority queue (`DSCP EF` / `46`) without getting dropped. `RTP` builds RFC 3550 12-byte RTP headers (`Version = 2`, `Marker`, 7-bit `Payload Type`, 16-bit `Sequence Number`, 32-bit `Timestamp`, and 32-bit `SSRC`) over UDP port `5004`.
- **Canonical Syntax Note:** Always write `a -> b rtp ...` directly (never `a -> b udp rtp ...`). Override ports with `srcport <0..65535> dstport <0..65535>` if your SDP negotiated a custom UDP media port such as `16384`.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`PT`** | `PT <0..127>` | `0` (`PCMU`) | 7-bit RTP Payload Type (`0` = G.711 PCMU, `8` = G.711 PCMA, `9` = G.722, `18` = G.729, `96..127` = dynamic Opus / H.264 / VP9) |
| **`SEQ`** | `SEQ <0..65535>` | `1` | 16-bit RTP packet sequence counter |
| **`TIMESTAMP`** | `TIMESTAMP <number>` | `160` | 32-bit media sampling timestamp (e.g., `+160` per 20ms frame at 8 kHz) |
| **`SSRC`** | `SSRC <number>` | `0x12345678` | 32-bit Synchronization Source identifier |
| **`MARKER`** | `MARKER <0\|1>` | `0` | 1-bit Marker flag (`1` indicates start of talkspurt or end of video keyframe) |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | 160B silence | Encoded audio/video frame bytes (or `hexpayload "<hex>"`) |

### 4.3 Real-Time Streaming Protocol (`RTSP` — Default: TCP Port `554`)

Verifying physical-security VLAN ACLs between an NVR and IP cameras on TCP port `554` doesn't require climbing a ladder to reboot a camera. `RTSP` builds RFC 2326 / RFC 7826 media streaming control commands (`OPTIONS`, `DESCRIBE`, `SETUP`, `PLAY`, `TEARDOWN`) and status replies.
- **Setting the RTSP `Transport:` Header with `TRANSPORT_HDR`:** Because FrameAssembly reserves `TRANSPORT TCP` / `TRANSPORT UDP` to select the Layer 4 protocol, use `TRANSPORT_HDR "<spec>"` to set the RTSP `Transport: RTP/AVP;unicast;client_port=5004-5005` header.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shorthand Method** | `OPTIONS` \| `DESCRIBE` \| `SETUP` \| `PLAY` \| `TEARDOWN` | `OPTIONS` | Standalone keyword setting the RTSP request method |
| **`METHOD`** | `METHOD "<verb>"` | `"OPTIONS"` | Explicit RTSP method string (e.g., `"PAUSE"`, `"ANNOUNCE"`, `"RECORD"`, `"GET_PARAMETER"`) |
| **`URI`** | `URI "<rtsp_url>"` | `"rtsp://localhost/stream"` | Target RTSP stream URL |
| **`STATUS`** | `STATUS <100..599>` | Omitted (Request) | Emits an RTSP response (`RTSP/1.0 <STATUS> OK\r\n`, e.g., `200`, `401`, `454`) |
| **`CSEQ`** | `CSEQ <number>` | `1` | `CSeq:` request/response correlation counter |
| **`SESSION`** | `SESSION "<id>"` | Omitted | Sets the `Session:` header identifier |
| **`TRANSPORT_HDR`** | `TRANSPORT_HDR "<text>"` | Omitted | Sets the RTSP `Transport:` header (e.g., `"RTP/AVP;unicast;client_port=5004-5005"`) |

### 4.4 Session Traversal Utilities for NAT (`STUN` — Default: UDP Port `3478`)

When WebRTC video calls or remote-work softphones fail to establish direct media paths across NAT, the culprit is often a blocked UDP `3478` STUN binding or a mangled reflexive IP. `STUN` builds RFC 8489 / RFC 5389 20-byte STUN headers (with fixed magic cookie `0x2112A442` and 96-bit transaction ID) and padded TLV attributes (`0x0020` `XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS` and `0x8022` `SOFTWARE`).
- **Important Syntax Note on `XOR_MAPPED_ADDR`:** Pass an IPv4 or IPv6 address only (e.g., `xor_mapped_addr 203.0.113.50` or `xor_mapped_addr 2001:db8::50`), never an `ip:port` pair.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`BINDING_REQUEST`** | `BINDING_REQUEST` | Default if none set | Message Type `0x0001` (STUN Binding Request) |
| **`BINDING_RESPONSE`**| `BINDING_RESPONSE` | Auto if `XOR_MAPPED_ADDR` | Message Type `0x0101` (STUN Binding Success Response) |
| **`BINDING_ERROR`** | `BINDING_ERROR` | Off | Message Type `0x0111` (STUN Binding Error Response) |
| **`TXID`** | `TXID <number>` | `1` | Populates the lower 32 bits of the 96-bit STUN Transaction ID |
| **`XOR_MAPPED_ADDR`** | `XOR_MAPPED_ADDR <ip>` | Omitted | XORs the reflexive IPv4 or IPv6 address with the magic cookie (`0x2112A442`) per RFC 8489 |
| **`SOFTWARE`** | `SOFTWARE "<text>"` | Omitted | Appends 4-byte-aligned `SOFTWARE` (`0x8022`) TLV attribute |

### 4.5 Simple Service Discovery Protocol (`SSDP` — Default: UDP Port `1900`)

Auditing enterprise networks for rogue UPnP media servers or testing IoT segmentation rules on UDP port `1900` (`239.255.255.250`) takes two lines of `.fasm` code. `SSDP` builds UPnP HTTPU multicast discovery requests (`M-SEARCH * HTTP/1.1`) and presence advertisements (`NOTIFY * HTTP/1.1`) over UDP port `1900`.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`MSEARCH`** | `MSEARCH` | Default if none set | Emits `M-SEARCH * HTTP/1.1\r\n` active discovery query |
| **`NOTIFY`** | `NOTIFY` | Off | Emits `NOTIFY * HTTP/1.1\r\n` multicast device announcement |
| **`HOST_HDR`** | `HOST_HDR "<ip:port>"` | `"239.255.255.250:1900"` | Sets the HTTPU `HOST:` header |
| **`MAN`** | `MAN "<text>"` | `"\"ssdp:discover\""` | Sets the `MAN:` header for `MSEARCH` packets |
| **`MX`** | `MX <0..255>` | `3` | Maximum wait response delay in seconds (`MX:` header) |
| **`ST`** | `ST "<target>"` | `"ssdp:all"` | Search Target (`"upnp:rootdevice"`, `"urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:MediaServer:1"`) |
| **`NT`** | `NT "<type>"` | `"upnp:rootdevice"` | Notification Type header in `NOTIFY` advertisements |
| **`NTS`** | `NTS "<sub_type>"` | `"ssdp:alive"` | Notification Sub-Type (`"ssdp:alive"`, `"ssdp:byebye"`, `"ssdp:update"`) |
| **`USN`** | `USN "<uuid>"` | Default UUID | Unique Service Name identifier |
| **`LOCATION`** | `LOCATION "<url>"` | Omitted | URL to the XML UPnP device description document |

### Compilable Example: VoIP Call Setup (`STUN` + `SIP` + `RTP`), `RTSP` Camera & `SSDP` Discovery

```frameassembly
host voip_phone { ip 10.80.1.50 }
host sbc_media  { ip 10.80.1.10 }

flow voip_rtsp_and_upnp(phone, sbc) {
    // 1. WebRTC / VoIP STUN NAT binding discovery
    phone -> sbc stun binding_request txid 9001 software "Polycom-VVX/6.4" wait 1ms
    phone <- sbc stun binding_response txid 9001 xor_mapped_addr 203.0.113.50 software "Coturn-4.6" wait 2ms

    // 2. DSCP CS3 (24) SIP call setup + DSCP EF (46) G.711 PCMU RTP voice stream + SIP BYE
    phone -> sbc dscp 24 sip invite uri "sip:1002@pbx.example.com" from "sip:1001@pbx.example.com" to "sip:1002@pbx.example.com" call_id "call-7741@10.80.1.50" cseq 1 via "SIP/2.0/UDP 10.80.1.50:5060" contact "sip:1001@10.80.1.50" content_type "application/sdp" body "v=0\r\nm=audio 5004 RTP/AVP 0\r\n" wait 2ms
    phone <- sbc dscp 24 sip status 200 reason "OK" call_id "call-7741@10.80.1.50" cseq 1 wait 2ms
    phone -> sbc dscp 24 sip ack uri "sip:1002@pbx.example.com" call_id "call-7741@10.80.1.50" cseq 1 wait 1ms
    phone -> sbc dscp 46 rtp pt 0 seq 1001 timestamp 160 ssrc 0x11223344 marker 1 payload "G711_PCMU_FRAME_1" wait 20ms
    phone <- sbc dscp 46 rtp pt 0 seq 5001 timestamp 160 ssrc 0x99887766 marker 1 payload "G711_PCMU_REPLY_1" wait 20ms
    phone -> sbc dscp 24 sip bye uri "sip:1002@pbx.example.com" call_id "call-7741@10.80.1.50" cseq 2 wait 2ms
    phone <- sbc dscp 24 sip status 200 reason "OK" call_id "call-7741@10.80.1.50" cseq 2 wait 5ms

    // 3. RTSP security camera stream negotiation (DESCRIBE -> SETUP -> PLAY -> TEARDOWN)
    phone -> sbc rtsp describe uri "rtsp://10.80.1.10:554/cam01/main" cseq 1 wait 1ms
    phone <- sbc rtsp status 200 cseq 1 wait 1ms
    phone -> sbc rtsp setup uri "rtsp://10.80.1.10:554/cam01/main/track1" cseq 2 transport_hdr "RTP/AVP;unicast;client_port=5004-5005" wait 1ms
    phone <- sbc rtsp status 200 cseq 2 session "cam-sess-991" wait 1ms
    phone -> sbc rtsp play uri "rtsp://10.80.1.10:554/cam01/main" cseq 3 session "cam-sess-991" wait 5ms
    phone -> sbc rtsp teardown uri "rtsp://10.80.1.10:554/cam01/main" cseq 4 session "cam-sess-991" wait 2ms

    // 4. SSDP UPnP M-SEARCH query and NOTIFY alive response
    phone -> sbc ssdp msearch host_hdr "239.255.255.250:1900" man "\"ssdp:discover\"" mx 3 st "urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:MediaServer:1" wait 1ms
    phone <- sbc ssdp notify host_hdr "239.255.255.250:1900" nt "urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:MediaServer:1" nts "ssdp:alive" usn "uuid:media-sbc-01::upnp:rootdevice" location "http://10.80.1.10:8200/rootDesc.xml"
}

compile {
    voip_rtsp_and_upnp(voip_phone, sbc_media)
}
```

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md`

# Layer 7 Mail, Directory, Storage, Databases, Caches & Message Brokers Reference

Testing mail gateway DLP rules, Active Directory Kerberos/LDAP/SMB lateral-movement signatures, database activity monitors (`MySQL`/`PostgreSQL`/`Redis`/`Memcached`), or IoT message brokers (`MQTT`/`CoAP`/`AMQP`) usually means spinning up domain controllers, mail relays, NAS filers, or database clusters just to capture a few packets. FrameAssembly solves that with a few lines of `.fasm` code and two CLI commands:

```bash
# 1. Compile the .fasm code into a deterministic .pcap capture
frameassembly enterprise.fasm -o enterprise.pcap

# 2. Replay the capture onto the wire (or inspect enterprise.pcap in Wireshark / Suricata)
sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 enterprise.pcap
```

This guide covers **14 enterprise application, identity, storage, database, caching, and message-queuing protocols** across IPv4 and IPv6:
**`SMTP`**, **`IMAP`**, **`POP3`**, **`KERBEROS`**, **`LDAP`**, **`SMB`**, **`NFS`**, **`REDIS`**, **`MEMCACHED`**, **`MYSQL`**, **`POSTGRES`**, **`MQTT`**, **`COAP`**, and **`AMQP`**.

> **Where to Find Web, TLS/QUIC, Remote CLI (`SSH`/`TELNET`), File Transfer (`TFTP`/`FTP`), and VoIP (`SIP`/`RTP`):**
> Those 16 protocols are documented in [**Layer 7 Web, Cloud-Native, Transport Security, VoIP & Remote Access (`l7_web_and_cloud.md`)**](l7_web_and_cloud.md).

---

## Quick Protocol & Default Port Matrix

Every protocol below works with **zero mandatory modifiers** (emitting an RFC-compliant default frame on its standard port) or with explicit field overrides.

| Protocol | Keyword | Default Transport & Port | Standard / RFC | Common Network & Security Testing Use Cases |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SMTP** | `SMTP` | TCP `25` | RFC 5321 / RFC 6409 | Mail gateway relay filtering, DLP policy testing, ESMTP banner inspection |
| **IMAP4rev1/v2** | `IMAP` | TCP `143` | RFC 3501 / RFC 9051 | Mailbox access ACLs, tagged command/response parsing, cleartext auth alerts |
| **POP3** | `POP3` | TCP `110` | RFC 1939 | Legacy mail retrieval monitoring, `+OK`/`-ERR` authentication lockout tests |
| **Kerberos v5** | `KERBEROS` | UDP / TCP `88` | RFC 4120 / RFC 3961 | Active Directory KDC `AS-REQ`/`TGS-REQ` flows, encryption type (`ETYPE`) audits |
| **LDAPv3** | `LDAP` | TCP `389` | RFC 4511 | Directory `Bind`/`Search` inspection, LDAP filter & credential failure alerts |
| **SMB2 / SMB3** | `SMB` | TCP `445` | MS-SMB2 | Lateral-movement IDS rules, UNC share access control, ransomware simulation |
| **NFS v2/v3/v4** | `NFS` | TCP / UDP `2049` | RFC 7530 / RFC 5531 | NAS/HPC storage VLAN segmentation, ONC-RPC `COMPOUND` export mount verification |
| **Redis (RESP)** | `REDIS` | TCP `6379` | RESP2 / RESP3 | East-west cache tier ACLs, unauthenticated `SET`/`GET`/`EVAL` detection |
| **Memcached** | `MEMCACHED`| TCP / UDP `11211` | ASCII & Binary (`0x80`)| Cache key-value inspection, UDP `11211` reflection/amplification firewall blocks |
| **MySQL / MariaDB**| `MYSQL` | TCP `3306` | MySQL Wire v10 | Database activity monitoring (DAM), SQL query logging, error `1045`/`1062` alerts |
| **PostgreSQL** | `POSTGRES` | TCP `5432` | PostgreSQL Wire v3.0 | Startup role/database inspection, SQL transaction & error audit verification |
| **MQTT v3.1.1** | `MQTT` | TCP `1883` | OASIS MQTT v3.1.1 | IoT broker topic ACLs, QoS `0..2` delivery, `KEEPALIVE` and `RETAIN` policies |
| **CoAP** | `COAP` | UDP `5683` | RFC 7252 | Constrained IoT sensor REST calls (`CON`/`NON`/`ACK`/`RST`), CBOR/JSON payloads |
| **AMQP 0-9-1** | `AMQP` | TCP `5672` | AMQP 0-9-1 | RabbitMQ exchange/routing-key inspection, virtual channel and heartbeat traffic |

---

## 1. Electronic Mail Suite (`SMTP`, `IMAP`, `POP3`)

### 1.1 Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (`SMTP` — Default: TCP Port `25`)

Testing mail gateway relay filters, ESMTP banner rules, or DLP content inspection normally requires configuring Postfix or Exchange and sending test messages through a live relay. In `.fasm` code, `SMTP` scripts both the client and server sides directly—building RFC 5321 SMTP client commands (`EHLO`, `HELO`, `MAIL FROM`, `RCPT TO`, `DATA`, `QUIT`), 3-digit server status replies (`220`, `250`, `354`, `221`, `550`), and RFC 5322 MIME message bodies over TCP port `25`.
- **Passing Envelope Addresses (`MAIL_FROM` / `RCPT_TO`):** You can pass the address either directly after `MAIL_FROM "<addr>"` / `RCPT_TO "<addr>"` or via the `PARAM "<addr>"` modifier (`mail_from param "alice@corp.example.com"`).
- **Sending the `DATA` Command vs. Message Body:** Use `cmd "DATA"` to emit the `DATA\r\n` command line, and use `body "<mime_text>"` on the following packet after the server's `354` response to transmit the email headers/body and trailing `.\r\n` terminator.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`EHLO`** | `EHLO ["<domain>"]` | `"EHLO"` | Emits `EHLO <domain>\r\n` Extended SMTP client greeting |
| **`HELO`** | `HELO ["<domain>"]` | `"HELO"` | Emits `HELO <domain>\r\n` standard SMTP client greeting |
| **`MAIL_FROM`** | `MAIL_FROM ["<addr>"]` | Sets `CMD "MAIL FROM"` | Emits `MAIL FROM:<<addr>>\r\n` (address may also be passed via `PARAM "<addr>"`) |
| **`RCPT_TO`** | `RCPT_TO ["<addr>"]` | Sets `CMD "RCPT TO"` | Emits `RCPT TO:<<addr>>\r\n` (address may also be passed via `PARAM "<addr>"`) |
| **`QUIT`** | `QUIT` | Off | Emits `QUIT\r\n` session termination command |
| **`CMD`** | `CMD "<verb>"` | `"EHLO"` | Explicit SMTP verb (`"DATA"`, `"STARTTLS"`, `"AUTH"`, `"VRFY"`, `"RSET"`, `"NOOP"`) |
| **`PARAM`** | `PARAM "<arg>"` | `"example.com"` | Command parameter or envelope address when not specified inline |
| **`CODE`** | `CODE <200..599>` | Omitted (Command) | Emits a 3-digit server reply (`220` Banner, `250` OK, `354` Start mail input, `221` Bye, `550` Rejected) |
| **`REPLY`** | `REPLY "<text>"` | `"OK"` | Server reply text accompanying `CODE` |
| **`BODY`** | `BODY "<mime_msg>"` | Empty | Transmits RFC 5322 email headers/body and appends `\r\n.\r\n` |

### 1.2 Internet Message Access Protocol (`IMAP` — Default: TCP Port `143`)

Validating mailbox access ACLs, cleartext authentication alerts, or SIEM parsers for IMAP commands doesn't require standing up a Dovecot or Exchange mailbox server. `IMAP` builds RFC 3501 / RFC 9051 IMAP4rev1/v4rev2 client commands (`<TAG> <CMD> <ARG>\r\n`) and server completion or untagged responses (`<TAG> <STATUS> <RESPONSE>\r\n`) over TCP port `143`.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`TAG`** | `TAG "<text>"` | `"A001"` | Client command correlation tag (`"A001"`, `"A002"`) or untagged server prefix (`"*"`) |
| **`CMD`** | `CMD "<verb>"` | `"CAPABILITY"` | Client IMAP command (`"LOGIN"`, `"SELECT"`, `"EXAMINE"`, `"FETCH"`, `"SEARCH"`, `"STORE"`, `"IDLE"`, `"LOGOUT"`) |
| **`ARG`** | `ARG "<text>"` | Omitted | Command arguments (e.g., `"INBOX"`, `"1:* (FLAGS BODY.PEEK[HEADER])"`) |
| **`STATUS`** | `STATUS "<OK\|NO\|BAD>"`| Omitted (Command) | Emits a server completion line (`<TAG> <STATUS> <RESPONSE>\r\n`) |
| **`RESPONSE`** | `RESPONSE "<text>"` | `"Completed"` | Server response explanation text |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Raw untagged server response line or message body |

### 1.3 Post Office Protocol v3 (`POP3` — Default: TCP Port `110`)

Verifying that IDS sensors detect legacy cleartext mail retrieval or brute-force `-ERR` lockouts on TCP port `110` is straightforward with `POP3`, which builds RFC 1939 mailbox commands (`USER`, `PASS`, `STAT`, `LIST`, `UIDL`, `RETR`, `DELE`, `QUIT`) and `+OK` / `-ERR` server replies.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`CMD`** | `CMD "<verb>"` | `"STAT"` | Client POP3 command (`"USER"`, `"PASS"`, `"STAT"`, `"LIST"`, `"UIDL"`, `"RETR"`, `"DELE"`, `"QUIT"`) |
| **`ARG`** | `ARG "<text>"` | Omitted | Command argument (username, password, or message number `"1"`) |
| **`OK`** | `OK` | Off | Emits a positive `+OK <RESPONSE>\r\n` server status line |
| **`ERR`** | `ERR` | Off | Emits a negative `-ERR <RESPONSE>\r\n` server status line |
| **`RESPONSE`** | `RESPONSE "<text>"` | `"POP3 server ready"` | Status text following `+OK` or `-ERR` |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Additional multi-line message or mailbox drop listing |

### Compilable Example: Enterprise Email Submission (`SMTP`) & Mailbox Retrieval (`IMAP` / `POP3`)

```frameassembly
host mail_client { ip 10.30.1.50 }
host mail_server { ip 10.30.1.10 }

flow email_submission_and_sync(mua, mta) {
    // 1. SMTP message submission (TCP 25): Banner -> EHLO -> MAIL FROM -> RCPT TO -> DATA -> BODY -> QUIT
    mua <- mta smtp code 220 reply "mx01.corp.example.com ESMTP Postfix" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp ehlo "ws01.corp.example.com" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta smtp code 250 reply "mx01.corp.example.com PIPELINING SIZE 52428800" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp mail_from param "netops@corp.example.com" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta smtp code 250 reply "2.1.0 Ok" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp rcpt_to param "oncall@corp.example.com" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta smtp code 250 reply "2.1.5 Ok" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp cmd "DATA" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta smtp code 354 reply "End data with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp body "From: netops@corp.example.com\r\nTo: oncall@corp.example.com\r\nSubject: BGP Maintenance Window\r\n\r\nCore router upgrade scheduled at 02:00 UTC." wait 2ms
    mua <- mta smtp code 250 reply "2.0.0 Ok: queued as 4X9z2L01" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp quit wait 1ms
    mua <- mta smtp code 221 reply "2.0.0 Bye" wait 3ms

    // 2. IMAP4rev1 mailbox login, INBOX selection, and message flag fetch (TCP 143)
    mua -> mta imap tag "A001" cmd "LOGIN" arg "oncall@corp.example.com VaultPass!99" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta imap tag "A001" status "OK" response "LOGIN completed" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta imap tag "A002" cmd "SELECT" arg "INBOX" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta imap tag "A002" status "OK" response "[READ-WRITE] SELECT completed" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta imap tag "A003" cmd "FETCH" arg "1 (FLAGS BODY[HEADER.FIELDS (SUBJECT)])" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta imap tag "A003" status "OK" response "FETCH completed" wait 3ms

    // 3. POP3 mailbox status check and logout (TCP 110)
    mua -> mta pop3 cmd "USER" arg "oncall@corp.example.com" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta pop3 ok response "User accepted" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta pop3 cmd "STAT" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta pop3 ok response "4 18420" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta pop3 cmd "QUIT" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta pop3 ok response "Logging out"
}

compile {
    email_submission_and_sync(mail_client, mail_server)
}
```

---

## 2. Enterprise Identity & Directory (`KERBEROS`, `LDAP`)

### 2.1 Kerberos v5 (`KERBEROS` — Default: UDP / TCP Port `88`)

Reproducing Active Directory KDC ticket exchanges, Kerberoasting (`ETYPE 23` `rc4-hmac` downgrade) alerts, or `KRB-ERROR` pre-authentication failures normally requires a full Windows Server domain controller lab. Instead, `KERBEROS` builds RFC 4120 ASN.1 DER application-tagged Kerberos v5 Key Distribution Center (KDC) exchanges (`AS-REQ` tag `0x6A`, `AS-REP` tag `0x6B`, `TGS-REQ` tag `0x6C`, `TGS-REP` tag `0x6D`, and `KRB-ERROR` tag `0x7E`) directly from `.fasm` code.
- **Transport Selection:** Defaults to UDP port `88`; add `transport tcp` on the statement to emit TCP port `88` (with the 4-byte RFC 4120 §7.2.2 TCP record length prefix).

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`AS_REQ`** | `AS_REQ` | Default if none set | Authentication Service Request (`msg-type = 10`, ASN.1 tag `0x6A`) |
| **`AS_REP`** | `AS_REP` | Off | Authentication Service Reply (`msg-type = 11`, ASN.1 tag `0x6B`) |
| **`TGS_REQ`** | `TGS_REQ` | Off | Ticket-Granting Service Request (`msg-type = 12`, ASN.1 tag `0x6C`) |
| **`TGS_REP`** | `TGS_REP` | Off | Ticket-Granting Service Reply (`msg-type = 13`, ASN.1 tag `0x6D`) |
| **`KRB_ERROR`** | `KRB_ERROR` | Off | Kerberos Error PDU (`msg-type = 30`, ASN.1 tag `0x7E`) |
| **`REALM`** | `REALM "<REALM>"` | `"EXAMPLE.COM"` | Kerberos realm name (`GeneralString`) |
| **`CNAME`** | `CNAME "<principal>"` | `"alice"` | Client principal name (`PrincipalName`) |
| **`SNAME`** | `SNAME "<service>"` | `"krbtgt"` | Service principal name (e.g., `"krbtgt/CORP.EXAMPLE.COM"`, `"cifs/nas01.corp.example.com"`) |
| **`ETYPE`** | `ETYPE <code_id>` | `18` | RFC 3961/8009 encryption type (`18` = `aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96`, `17` = `aes128-cts-hmac-sha1-96`, `23` = `rc4-hmac`) |

### 2.2 Lightweight Directory Access Protocol v3 (`LDAP` — Default: TCP Port `389`)

Testing SIEM rules for Active Directory or OpenLDAP reconnaissance queries, group enumeration filters, and `invalidCredentials` (`49`) bind failures doesn't require querying a live directory server. `LDAP` builds RFC 4511 ASN.1 BER `LDAPMessage` envelopes (`SEQUENCE 0x30`) containing a `messageID` and protocol operation choice (`BindRequest`, `BindResponse`, `SearchRequest`, `SearchResultEntry`, `SearchResultDone`, or `UnbindRequest`) over TCP port `389`.
- **Complete RFC 4511 `SearchRequest` Encoding:** `SEARCH_REQ` encodes all 8 mandatory ASN.1 fields (`baseObject`, `scope`, `derefAliases`, `sizeLimit`, `timeLimit`, `typesOnly`, `filter`, and `attributes`) so Wireshark's BER dissector decodes every field without warnings.
- **Always write `BASE_DN`:** Use `BASE_DN "<dn>"` (never `DN`) to set the Distinguished Name on bind and search operations.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`BIND_REQ`** | `BIND_REQ` | Default if none set | `BindRequest` (ASN.1 tag `0x60`, LDAPv3, bind DN from `BASE_DN`, simple auth) |
| **`BIND_RES`** | `BIND_RES` | Off | `BindResponse` (ASN.1 tag `0x61`, carries `RESULT_CODE`) |
| **`SEARCH_REQ`** | `SEARCH_REQ` | Off | `SearchRequest` (ASN.1 tag `0x63`, carries `BASE_DN` and `FILTER`) |
| **`SEARCH_ENTRY`** | `SEARCH_ENTRY` | Off | `SearchResultEntry` (ASN.1 tag `0x64`, carries matched `BASE_DN` and attributes) |
| **`SEARCH_DONE`** | `SEARCH_DONE` | Off | `SearchResultDone` (ASN.1 tag `0x65`, carries completion `RESULT_CODE`) |
| **`UNBIND_REQ`** | `UNBIND_REQ` | Off | `UnbindRequest` (ASN.1 tag `0x42`, 0-length NULL body closing the session) |
| **`MSGID`** | `MSGID <number>` | `1` | LDAP message correlation ID |
| **`BASE_DN`** | `BASE_DN "<dn>"` | `"dc=example,dc=com"` | Distinguished Name for `BindRequest`, `SearchRequest`, or `SearchResultEntry` |
| **`FILTER`** | `FILTER "<expr>"` | `"(objectClass=*)"` | Search filter string for `SEARCH_REQ` |
| **`RESULT_CODE`** | `RESULT_CODE <number>` | `0` (`success`) | LDAP result code (`0` = `success`, `32` = `noSuchObject`, `49` = `invalidCredentials`) |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Attribute value string in `SEARCH_ENTRY` |

### Compilable Example: Active Directory Kerberos KDC Ticket Exchange & LDAPv3 Directory Query

```frameassembly
host ad_workstation { ip 10.45.1.100 }
host domain_ctrl    { ip 10.45.1.10 }

flow active_directory_auth_and_ldap(ws, dc) {
    // 1. Kerberos v5 AS-REQ / AS-REP (TGT acquisition) + TGS-REQ / TGS-REP (LDAP service ticket)
    ws -> dc kerberos as_req realm "CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" cname "jdoe" sname "krbtgt/CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" etype 18 wait 1ms
    ws <- dc kerberos as_rep realm "CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" cname "jdoe" sname "krbtgt/CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" etype 18 wait 1ms
    ws -> dc kerberos tgs_req realm "CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" cname "jdoe" sname "ldap/dc01.corp.example.com" etype 18 wait 1ms
    ws <- dc kerberos tgs_rep realm "CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" cname "jdoe" sname "ldap/dc01.corp.example.com" etype 18 wait 2ms

    // 2. LDAPv3 Bind -> Search group memberships -> Search Entry -> Search Done -> Unbind
    ws -> dc ldap bind_req msgid 1 base_dn "cn=jdoe,ou=Users,dc=corp,dc=example,dc=com" wait 1ms
    ws <- dc ldap bind_res msgid 1 result_code 0 wait 1ms
    ws -> dc ldap search_req msgid 2 base_dn "ou=Users,dc=corp,dc=example,dc=com" filter "(&(objectClass=user)(sAMAccountName=jdoe))" wait 1ms
    ws <- dc ldap search_entry msgid 2 base_dn "cn=jdoe,ou=Users,dc=corp,dc=example,dc=com" payload "memberOf: cn=NetAdmins,ou=Groups,dc=corp,dc=example,dc=com" wait 1ms
    ws <- dc ldap search_done msgid 2 result_code 0 wait 1ms
    ws -> dc ldap unbind_req msgid 3
}

compile {
    active_directory_auth_and_ldap(ad_workstation, domain_ctrl)
}
```

---

## 3. Network File Storage (`SMB`, `NFS`)

### 3.1 Server Message Block v2/v3 (`SMB` — Default: TCP Port `445`)

Validating east-west firewall segmentation, UNC share access controls, or lateral-movement IDS rules (`IPC$`, `ADMIN$`, `C$`) on TCP port `445` is much faster when you don't have to mount Windows file shares in a test VM. `SMB` builds Microsoft `[MS-SMB2]` packets prefixed with a 4-byte NetBIOS Session Service stream length header, a 64-byte SMB2 header (`\xFESMB` magic, 64-byte header length, `Status`, `Command`, `MessageId`, `TreeId`, `SessionId`, and 16-byte signature), and command-specific UTF-16LE share or file paths.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`COMMAND`** | `COMMAND "<name>"` | `"NEGOTIATE"` | SMB2 command (`"NEGOTIATE"` `0x00`, `"SESSION_SETUP"` `0x01`, `"LOGOFF"` `0x02`, `"TREE_CONNECT"` `0x03`, `"TREE_DISCONNECT"` `0x04`, `"CREATE"` `0x05`, `"CLOSE"` `0x06`, `"READ"` `0x08`, `"WRITE"` `0x09`) |
| **`STATUS`** | `STATUS <number>` | `0` (`STATUS_SUCCESS`) | 32-bit `NTSTATUS` code (`0` = `STATUS_SUCCESS`, `0xC0000016` = `MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED`, `0xC0000022` = `ACCESS_DENIED`, `0xC000006D` = `LOGON_FAILURE`) |
| **`SESSION_ID`** | `SESSION_ID <64-bit_id>` | `0` | 64-bit authenticated SMB2 `SessionId` |
| **`TREE_ID`** | `TREE_ID <number>` | `0` | 32-bit mounted share `TreeId` |
| **`MSGID`** | `MSGID <number>` | `0` | 64-bit monotonically increasing `MessageId` |
| **`SHARE`** | `SHARE "<unc_path>"` | `"\\\\localhost\\IPC$"`| UNC share path encoded as UTF-16LE in `TREE_CONNECT` requests |
| **`FILENAME`** | `FILENAME "<path>"` | `"file.txt"` | Target file or named pipe encoded as UTF-16LE in `CREATE` requests |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | File data payload for `READ` / `WRITE` operations |

### 3.2 Network File System (`NFS` — Default: TCP / UDP Port `2049`)

Verifying NAS/HPC storage VLAN ACLs or ONC-RPC export mount rules on port `2049` without provisioning an NFS filer is simple in `.fasm` code. `NFS` builds RFC 1813 (NFSv3) and RFC 7530 / RFC 8881 (NFSv4) calls encapsulated inside RFC 5531 ONC-RPC v2 messages (with the 4-byte RPC Record Marking fragment header `0x80000000 | len` on TCP and 4-byte XDR string padding).

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`VERS`** | `VERS <2\|3\|4>` | `4` | NFS version number (`2`, `3`, or `4`) in the ONC-RPC Call header (Program `100003`) |
| **`PROC`** | `PROC "<name>"` | `"COMPOUND"` | NFS procedure (`"NULL"`, `"COMPOUND"`, `"GETATTR"`, `"LOOKUP"`, `"READ"`, `"WRITE"`) |
| **`TAG`** | `TAG "<text>"` | `"fasm_nfs"` | NFSv4 `COMPOUND4args` UTF-8 tag string (XDR length-prefixed and 4-byte aligned) |
| **`PATH`** | `PATH "</export/...>"` | `"/export"` | Export or file path encoded into the XDR call body |
| **`XID`** | `XID <number>` | `0x12345678` | 32-bit ONC-RPC Transaction Identifier (`XID`) |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Additional XDR data or file read/write block bytes |

### Compilable Example: Enterprise NAS File Share Operations (`SMB` & `NFS`)

```frameassembly
host compute_node { ip 10.90.1.25 }
host nas_filer    { ip 10.90.1.10 }

flow nas_storage_operations(node, filer) {
    // 1. SMB2/3 dialect negotiate -> session setup -> tree connect -> file create & write
    node -> filer smb command "NEGOTIATE" msgid 0 wait 1ms
    node <- filer smb command "NEGOTIATE" status 0 msgid 0 wait 1ms
    node -> filer smb command "SESSION_SETUP" session_id 0x100001 msgid 1 wait 1ms
    node <- filer smb command "SESSION_SETUP" status 0 session_id 0x100001 msgid 1 wait 1ms
    node -> filer smb command "TREE_CONNECT" session_id 0x100001 msgid 2 share "\\\\nas01.corp\\vmstore" wait 1ms
    node <- filer smb command "TREE_CONNECT" status 0 session_id 0x100001 tree_id 10 msgid 2 wait 1ms
    node -> filer smb command "CREATE" session_id 0x100001 tree_id 10 msgid 3 filename "prod-db01.vhdx" wait 1ms
    node <- filer smb command "CREATE" status 0 session_id 0x100001 tree_id 10 msgid 3 wait 1ms
    node -> filer smb command "WRITE" session_id 0x100001 tree_id 10 msgid 4 payload "VHDX_HEADER_4096B" wait 1ms
    node <- filer smb command "WRITE" status 0 session_id 0x100001 tree_id 10 msgid 4 wait 2ms

    // 2. NFSv4 ONC-RPC NULL ping and COMPOUND read operation on TCP 2049
    node -> filer nfs vers 4 proc "NULL" xid 0x90010001 wait 1ms
    node <- filer nfs vers 4 proc "NULL" xid 0x90010001 wait 1ms
    node -> filer nfs vers 4 proc "COMPOUND" xid 0x90010002 tag "lookup_read" path "/exports/hpc/checkpoint.dat" wait 1ms
    node <- filer nfs vers 4 proc "COMPOUND" xid 0x90010002 tag "lookup_read" path "/exports/hpc/checkpoint.dat" payload "NFS4_CHECKPOINT_BLOCK"
}

compile {
    nas_storage_operations(compute_node, nas_filer)
}
```

---

## 4. In-Memory Caches & SQL Databases (`REDIS`, `MEMCACHED`, `MYSQL`, `POSTGRES`)

### 4.1 Redis (`REDIS` — Default: TCP Port `6379`)

Auditing east-west cache tier ACLs or testing IDS alerts for unauthenticated Redis commands on TCP port `6379` requires zero database setup. `REDIS` builds Redis Serialization Protocol (RESP2/RESP3) client command arrays (`*<n>\r\n$<len>\r\n<arg>\r\n...`) and server replies (`+OK\r\n`, `-ERR ...\r\n`, `:<int>\r\n`, `$<len>\r\n<val>\r\n`).

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shorthand Cmd** | `GET` \| `SET` | `"PING"` | Bare keyword setting `CMD "GET"` or `CMD "SET"` |
| **`CMD`** | `CMD "<verb>"` | `"PING"` | Explicit Redis command (`"PING"`, `"GET"`, `"SET"`, `"DEL"`, `"HSET"`, `"LPUSH"`, `"AUTH"`, `"INFO"`) |
| **`KEY`** | `KEY "<key>"` | Omitted | Appends the target key as the first command argument |
| **`ARGS`** | `ARGS "<space_sep>"` | Omitted | Splits space-separated arguments into individual RESP Bulk Strings |
| **`REPLY_TYPE`** | `REPLY_TYPE "<type>"` | Omitted (Command) | Emits a server reply (`"SIMPLE"` / `"STATUS"` `+`, `"ERROR"` / `"ERR"` `-`, `"INTEGER"` / `"INT"` `:`, `"BULK"` `$`, `"ARRAY"` `*`) |
| **`VALUE`** | `VALUE "<val>"` | `"OK"` | Reply value or second argument for `SET` commands |

### 4.2 Memcached (`MEMCACHED` — Default: TCP / UDP Port `11211`)

Verifying that perimeter firewalls block UDP `11211` DDoS reflection/amplification vectors or inspecting east-west cache traffic doesn't require spinning up a live Memcached daemon. In `.fasm` code, `MEMCACHED` builds both the Memcached ASCII protocol (`set <key> <flags> <exptime> <bytes>\r\n<value>\r\n`, `get <key>\r\n`) and the 24-byte Memcached Binary Protocol (`0x80` request / `0x81` response magic when `OPCODE` is specified).

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shorthand Cmd** | `GET` \| `SET` | `"get"` | Bare keyword setting `CMD "GET"` or `CMD "SET"` |
| **`CMD`** | `CMD "<verb>"` | `"get"` | ASCII command or reply (`"get"`, `"set"`, `"add"`, `"delete"`, `"stats"`, `"STORED"`, `"END"`) |
| **`KEY`** | `KEY "<key>"` | `"default_key"` | Cache item key |
| **`VALUE`** | `VALUE "<val>"` | `"default_val"` | Cache item data payload (automatically sets `<bytes>` in ASCII `set` commands) |
| **`FLAGS`** | `FLAGS <number>` | `0` | 32-bit client flags field for `set`/`add` operations |
| **`EXPTIME`** | `EXPTIME <seconds>` | `3600` | Expiration TTL in seconds |
| **`OPCODE`** | `OPCODE <0..255>` | Omitted (ASCII) | Switches packet to the 24-byte Binary Protocol (`0x00` Get, `0x01` Set, `0x04` Delete, `0x07` Quit) |
| **`OPAQUE`** | `OPAQUE <number>` | `0` | 32-bit correlation ID in the Binary Protocol header |
| **`CAS`** | `CAS <64-bit_id>` | `0` | 64-bit Compare-And-Swap version check |

### 4.3 MySQL / MariaDB (`MYSQL` — Default: TCP Port `3306`)

Testing Database Activity Monitoring (DAM) appliances, SQL query logging, or failed-login (`1045`) alerts on TCP port `3306` doesn't require running a live MySQL or MariaDB instance. `MYSQL` builds MySQL Client/Server Wire Protocol v10 packets with 3-byte little-endian payload length and 1-byte sequence ID headers.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`GREETING`** | `GREETING` | Default if `SERVER_VERSION` | Emits Server `HandshakeV10` (`0x0A`) with version string, thread ID, and auth-plugin salt |
| **`LOGIN`** | `LOGIN` | Auto if `USER` set | Emits Client `HandshakeResponse41` (`seq = 1`) with capability flags, `USER`, and `DB` |
| **`QUERY`** | `QUERY` | Default if `SQL` set | Emits Client `COM_QUERY` (`0x03`) carrying the `SQL` statement |
| **`OK`** | `OK` | Off | Emits Server `OK_Packet` (`0x00`, affected rows, last insert ID, status flags) |
| **`ERR`** | `ERR` | Auto if `ERRCODE` set | Emits Server `ERR_Packet` (`0xFF`, 16-bit `ERRCODE`, `#HY000` SQLSTATE, and error message) |
| **`EOF`** | `EOF` | Off | Emits Server `EOF_Packet` (`0xFE`, warning count and status flags) |
| **`SERVER_VERSION`**| `SERVER_VERSION "<ver>"`| `"8.0.35"` | Null-terminated version banner in `GREETING` packets |
| **`USER`** | `USER "<username>"` | `"root"` | Database login username in `LOGIN` packets |
| **`DB`** | `DB "<schema>"` | Omitted | Initial database schema name in `LOGIN` packets |
| **`SQL`** | `SQL "<statement>"` | `"SELECT 1"` | SQL statement string for `QUERY` (`COM_QUERY`) packets |
| **`ERRCODE`** | `ERRCODE <0..65535>` | `1045` | 16-bit MySQL error code (`1045` = Access denied, `1062` = Duplicate entry, `1146` = Table doesn't exist) |

### 4.4 PostgreSQL (`POSTGRES` — Default: TCP Port `5432`)

Validating PostgreSQL startup role/database policies, SQL transaction audit rules, or `ErrorResponse` handling on TCP port `5432` can be scripted directly in `.fasm` code. `POSTGRES` builds PostgreSQL Wire Protocol v3.0 (`0x00030000` / `196608`) `StartupMessage` frames and 1-byte tagged messages (`'Q'` Query, `'R'` AuthenticationOk, `'C'` CommandComplete, `'Z'` ReadyForQuery, `'E'` ErrorResponse). Multiple server response tags (such as `auth_ok ready_for_query` or `command_complete ready_for_query`) can be combined into a single TCP frame just like a real PostgreSQL server.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`STARTUP`** | `STARTUP` | Auto if `USER`/`DB` set | Emits untagged v3.0 `StartupMessage` (`0x00030000`) with `user` and `database` parameters |
| **`QUERY`** | `QUERY` | Default if `SQL` set | Emits Client `'Q'` (`Query`) message with NUL-terminated `SQL` string |
| **`AUTH_OK`** | `AUTH_OK` | Off | Emits Server `'R'` (`AuthenticationOk`, length `8`, auth code `0`) |
| **`COMMAND_COMPLETE`**| `COMMAND_COMPLETE` | Off | Emits Server `'C'` (`CommandComplete`, e.g., `"SELECT 1\0"` or `PAYLOAD` tag) |
| **`READY_FOR_QUERY`**| `READY_FOR_QUERY` | Off | Emits Server `'Z'` (`ReadyForQuery`, length `5`, idle status `'I'`) |
| **`ERROR_RESPONSE`**| `ERROR_RESPONSE` | Off | Emits Server `'E'` (`ErrorResponse` with severity `ERROR`, SQLSTATE `42601`, and message) |
| **`USER`** | `USER "<role>"` | `"postgres"` | Database role name in `STARTUP` packets |
| **`DB`** | `DB "<dbname>"` | `"postgres"` | Target database name in `STARTUP` packets |
| **`SQL`** | `SQL "<statement>"` | `"SELECT 1;"` | SQL query text in `QUERY` (`'Q'`) packets |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<tag>"` | `"SELECT 1"` | Custom command tag for `COMMAND_COMPLETE` or error text for `ERROR_RESPONSE` |

### Compilable Example: Cache & Relational Database Tier (`REDIS`, `MEMCACHED`, `MYSQL`, `POSTGRES`)

```frameassembly
host app_worker   { ip 10.110.1.50 }
host data_cluster { ip 10.110.1.10 }

flow cache_and_sql_tier(app, db) {
    // 1. Redis RESP2 SET and GET cache lookup (TCP 6379)
    app -> db redis cmd "SET" args "session:9042 active EX 300" wait 1ms
    app <- db redis reply_type "SIMPLE" value "OK" wait 1ms
    app -> db redis get key "session:9042" wait 1ms
    app <- db redis reply_type "BULK" value "active" wait 2ms

    // 2. Memcached ASCII set and Binary protocol (0x80) get (TCP 11211)
    app -> db memcached set key "ratelimit:198.51.100.9" flags 0 exptime 60 value "14" wait 1ms
    app <- db memcached cmd "STORED" wait 1ms
    app -> db memcached get key "ratelimit:198.51.100.9" opcode 0x00 opaque 701 cas 1001 wait 2ms

    // 3. MySQL v10 Greeting -> Login -> INSERT Query -> Duplicate Key Error 1062 (TCP 3306)
    app <- db mysql greeting server_version "8.4.2-Enterprise" wait 1ms
    app -> db mysql login user "orders_svc" db "commerce" wait 1ms
    app <- db mysql ok wait 1ms
    app -> db mysql query sql "INSERT INTO orders (id, total_cents) VALUES (9001, 14999);" wait 1ms
    app <- db mysql err errcode 1062 payload "Duplicate entry '9001' for key 'orders.PRIMARY'" wait 2ms

    // 4. PostgreSQL v3.0 Startup -> AuthOk + ReadyForQuery -> Transaction -> CommandComplete (TCP 5432)
    app -> db postgres startup user "ledger_svc" db "ledger" wait 1ms
    app <- db postgres auth_ok ready_for_query wait 1ms
    app -> db postgres query sql "BEGIN; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 14999 WHERE id = 42; COMMIT;" wait 1ms
    app <- db postgres command_complete ready_for_query payload "COMMIT"
}

compile {
    cache_and_sql_tier(app_worker, data_cluster)
}
```

---

## 5. Message Brokers & IoT Telemetry (`MQTT`, `COAP`, `AMQP`)

### 5.1 MQTT v3.1.1 (`MQTT` — Default: TCP Port `1883`)

Testing IoT broker topic ACLs, unauthorized `PUBLISH`/`SUBSCRIBE` alerts (`RETURN_CODE 5`), or `QoS 0..2` and `RETAIN` policies on TCP port `1883` doesn't require deploying Mosquitto or EMQX. `MQTT` builds OASIS MQTT v3.1.1 control packets with 1-byte Fixed Headers (4-bit packet type, `DUP`, 2-bit `QoS`, and `RETAIN` bit), RFC-compliant variable-length Remaining Length encoding, Variable Headers, and payloads.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Packet Type Flag** | `CONNECT` \| `CONNACK` \| `PUBLISH` \| `PUBACK` \| `SUBSCRIBE` \| `SUBACK` \| `PINGREQ` \| `PINGRESP` \| `DISCONNECT` | `PUBLISH` (or `CONNECT` if `CLIENT_ID` set) | Selects the 4-bit MQTT Control Packet Type (`1..14`) |
| **`CLIENT_ID`** | `CLIENT_ID "<id>"` | `"fasm-mqtt"` | UTF-8 length-prefixed Client Identifier in `CONNECT` packets |
| **`KEEPALIVE`** | `KEEPALIVE <seconds>` | `60` | 16-bit Keep Alive timer in seconds in `CONNECT` packets |
| **`RETURN_CODE`** | `RETURN_CODE <0..255>` | `0` (`Accepted`) | Connect Return Code in `CONNACK` (`0` = Accepted, `4` = Bad user/pass, `5` = Not authorized) or granted QoS in `SUBACK` |
| **`TOPIC`** | `TOPIC "<topic>"` | `"test/topic"` | Publication topic in `PUBLISH` or topic filter in `SUBSCRIBE` |
| **`QOS`** | `QOS <0\|1\|2>` | `0` | Quality of Service level (`0` At most once, `1` At least once, `2` Exactly once) |
| **`RETAIN`** | `RETAIN [0\|1]` | Off | Sets the Fixed Header `RETAIN` bit (`0x01`) on `PUBLISH` packets |
| **`PKT_ID`** | `PKT_ID <0..65535>` | `1` | 16-bit Packet Identifier for `PUBLISH` (`QoS > 0`), `PUBACK`, `SUBSCRIBE`, and `SUBACK` |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Message body published to `TOPIC` |

### 5.2 Constrained Application Protocol (`COAP` — Default: UDP Port `5683`)

Simulating constrained IoT sensor REST telemetry (`CON`/`NON`/`ACK`/`RST`) on UDP port `5683` without flashing embedded hardware is straightforward with `COAP`. It builds RFC 7252 4-byte binary CoAP headers (`Version = 1`, 2-bit Type, Token Length, 8-bit `c.dd` Code byte `(class << 5) | detail`, and 16-bit `Message ID`), variable-length Token, delta-encoded `Uri-Path` (Option `11`) and `Content-Format` (Option `12`) options, and the `0xFF` payload marker.

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Message Type** | `CON` \| `NON` \| `ACK` \| `RST` | `CON` | 2-bit CoAP Type (`0` Confirmable, `1` Non-confirmable, `2` Acknowledgment, `3` Reset) |
| **Shorthand Code** | `GET` \| `POST` \| `PUT` \| `DELETE` \| `CREATED` \| `CHANGED` \| `NOT_FOUND` | `GET` (`0.01`) | Sets the CoAP method/response code (`GET`=`0.01`, `POST`=`0.02`, `PUT`=`0.03`, `DELETE`=`0.04`, `CREATED`=`2.01`, `CHANGED`=`2.04`, `NOT_FOUND`=`4.04`) |
| **`CODE`** | `CODE "<c.dd>"` | `"0.01"` | Dotted CoAP code string (`"0.01"` GET, `"0.02"` POST, `"2.04"` Changed, `"2.05"` Content, `"4.04"` Not Found) |
| **`MSGID`** | `MSGID <0..65535>` | `1` | 16-bit Message ID used to match `CON` requests with `ACK`/`RST` replies |
| **`TOKEN`** | `TOKEN <number\|"<text>">` | Omitted (0-len) | Client/server correlation token (32-bit integer/hex value or text string) |
| **`URI_PATH`** | `URI_PATH "<path>"` | Omitted | Slash-separated path split into delta-encoded Option `11` (`Uri-Path`) segments |
| **`CONTENT_FORMAT`**| `CONTENT_FORMAT <0..65535>` | Omitted | CoAP Option `12` media type (`0` = `text/plain`, `40` = `application/link-format`, `50` = `application/json`, `60` = `application/cbor`) |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Prepends `0xFF` payload marker followed by payload bytes |

### 5.3 Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (`AMQP` — Default: TCP Port `5672`)

Verifying RabbitMQ exchange and routing-key firewall rules or message-broker dissectors on TCP port `5672` requires no broker cluster—`AMQP` builds AMQP 0-9-1 protocol handshake headers (`'AMQP\x00\x00\x09\x01'`) and general frames (1-byte Frame Type, 16-bit Channel, 32-bit Payload Size, Class/Method IDs, and trailing `0xCE` frame-end marker).

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`PROTOCOL_HEADER`** | `PROTOCOL_HEADER` | Off | Emits the 8-byte `'AMQP\x00\x00\x09\x01'` connection preface |
| **`CONNECTION_START`**| `CONNECTION_START` | Off | Method Frame (Class `10`, Method `10` `Connection.Start`, version `0.9`) |
| **`CHANNEL_OPEN`** | `CHANNEL_OPEN` | Off | Method Frame (Class `20`, Method `10` `Channel.Open`) |
| **`BASIC_PUBLISH`** | `BASIC_PUBLISH` | Default if none set | Method Frame (Class `60`, Method `40` `Basic.Publish`) with `EXCHANGE` and `ROUTING_KEY` |
| **`BASIC_DELIVER`** | `BASIC_DELIVER` | Off | Method Frame (Class `60`, Method `60` `Basic.Deliver`) |
| **`HEARTBEAT`** | `HEARTBEAT` | Off | Frame Type `8` (`Heartbeat` on Channel `0`, 0-byte body + `0xCE`) |
| **`CHANNEL`** | `CHANNEL <0..65535>` | `1` (`0` for conn/hb) | 16-bit AMQP virtual channel number |
| **`EXCHANGE`** | `EXCHANGE "<name>"` | `""` (Default exch) | Short-string Exchange name in `BASIC_PUBLISH` / `BASIC_DELIVER` |
| **`ROUTING_KEY`** | `ROUTING_KEY "<key>"` | `"default"` | Short-string Routing Key in `BASIC_PUBLISH` / `BASIC_DELIVER` |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | Appended message body bytes before the `0xCE` frame-end byte |

### Compilable Example: IoT Edge Gateway & Enterprise Message Broker Pipeline (`MQTT`, `COAP`, `AMQP`)

```frameassembly
host iot_gateway { ip 192.168.140.10 }
host msg_broker  { ip 192.168.140.1 }

flow messaging_and_iot_pipeline(edge, brk) {
    // 1. MQTT v3.1.1 Connect -> ConnAck -> Subscribe -> Publish QoS 1 Retain -> PubAck -> Ping -> Disconnect
    edge -> brk mqtt connect client_id "gw-floor2-01" keepalive 60 wait 1ms
    edge <- brk mqtt connack return_code 0 wait 1ms
    edge -> brk mqtt subscribe pkt_id 1 topic "plant/floor2/cmd/#" qos 1 wait 1ms
    edge <- brk mqtt suback pkt_id 1 return_code 1 wait 1ms
    edge -> brk mqtt publish pkt_id 10 topic "plant/floor2/temp" qos 1 retain payload "{\"sensor\":\"T-104\",\"temp_c\":23.8}" wait 1ms
    edge <- brk mqtt puback pkt_id 10 wait 1ms
    edge -> brk mqtt pingreq wait 1ms
    edge <- brk mqtt pingresp wait 1ms
    edge -> brk mqtt disconnect wait 2ms

    // 2. CoAP Confirmable POST sensor telemetry with JSON content-format (50) and 2.04 Changed ACK
    edge -> brk coap con code "0.02" msgid 401 token 0x99aabb01 uri_path "sensors/vibration" content_format 50 payload "{\"rms_mm_s\":1.42}" wait 1ms
    edge <- brk coap ack code "2.04" msgid 401 token 0x99aabb01 wait 2ms

    // 3. AMQP 0-9-1 Protocol Header -> Connection.Start -> Channel.Open -> Basic.Publish -> Heartbeat
    edge -> brk amqp protocol_header wait 1ms
    edge <- brk amqp connection_start channel 0 wait 1ms
    edge -> brk amqp channel_open channel 1 wait 1ms
    edge -> brk amqp basic_publish channel 1 exchange "ot.telemetry" routing_key "floor2.alerts" payload "{\"severity\":\"INFO\",\"msg\":\"Vibration normal\"}" wait 1ms
    edge <- brk amqp basic_deliver channel 1 exchange "ot.telemetry" routing_key "floor2.alerts" payload "{\"ack\":true}" wait 1ms
    edge -> brk amqp heartbeat channel 0
}

compile {
    messaging_and_iot_pipeline(iot_gateway, msg_broker)
}
```
