# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l7_industrial_ot.md`

# Layer 7 Industrial Control Systems (ICS), SCADA & OT Reference

Nobody in their right mind tests a new industrial firewall rule or OT intrusion detection sensor by firing write commands at a live spinning turbine or substation breaker relay—and building a physical lab rack of Rockwell, Siemens, and DNP3 outstations costs a small fortune. FrameAssembly solves that with a few lines of `.fasm` code and two CLI commands:

```bash
# 1. Compile the .fasm code into a deterministic, checksum-valid .pcap capture
frameassembly ot_conduit.fasm -o ot_conduit.pcap

# 2. Replay the capture onto the test interface (or inspect ot_conduit.pcap in Wireshark / Suricata / Zeek)
sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 ot_conduit.pcap
```

This guide covers all **6 built-in Industrial Control System (ICS), building-automation, electrical substation, and factory PLC protocols**:
**`MODBUS`**, **`BACNET`**, **`DNP3`**, **`S7COMM`**, **`ETHERNETIP`**, and **`OPCUA`**.

OT security engineers, industrial firewall administrators, and SCADA system integrators use these protocols to validate:
- **Purdue Model (ISA-95 / IEC 62443) Zone & Conduit Firewalls:** Verify that deep packet inspection (DPI) policies between Level 3 (Site Operations / Historian), Level 2 (Supervisory HMI), and Level 1 (PLCs / RTUs / IEDs) allow read-only polling while blocking unauthorized register/coil writes or PLC STOP commands.
- **OT Intrusion Detection & Asset Discovery Sensors:** Validate dissectors and alert rules in Dragos, Claroty, Nozomi Networks, Cisco Cyber Vision, Palo Alto App-ID, Fortinet OT Security, Zeek, and Suricata—without risking live factory controllers or physical substation relays.

---

## Quick ICS / OT Protocol & Purdue Zone Matrix

Every protocol below works with **zero mandatory modifiers** (emitting a complete, standards-compliant default frame on its IANA port) or with explicit field overrides.

| Protocol | Keyword | Default Port | Standard | Typical Purdue Levels | Primary OT Firewall & IDS Inspection Fields |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Modbus TCP** | `MODBUS` | TCP `502` | Modbus v1.1b3 | Level 2 HMI $\leftrightarrow$ Level 1 PLC | `UNITID`, Function Code (`0x01..0x04` Read vs. `0x05/0x06/0x10` Write), Register `ADDR` & `COUNT` |
| **BACnet/IP** | `BACNET` | UDP `47808` (`0xBAC0`) | ANSI/ASHRAE 135 | BMS Server $\leftrightarrow$ HVAC / Chiller | BVLC Unicast/Broadcast, `WHO_IS`/`I_AM`, `READ_PROPERTY` vs. `WRITE_PROPERTY`, `OBJECT_TYPE` |
| **DNP3** | `DNP3` | TCP / UDP `20000` | IEEE 1815-2012 | Utility DMS $\leftrightarrow$ Substation RTU | Data Link `SRC`/`DST`, Function (`READ` vs. `SELECT`/`OPERATE`/`DIRECT_OPERATE`), `GROUP`/`VARIATION`, CRC-16 |
| **Siemens S7comm**| `S7COMM` | TCP `102` | RFC 1006 / ISO 8073| Eng. Workstation $\leftrightarrow$ S7 PLC | `ROSCTR` (`JOB` vs. `ACK_DATA`), `FUNC` (`READ_VAR` vs. `WRITE_VAR`/`PLC_CONTROL`), `AREA`, `DB_NUM` |
| **EtherNet/IP** | `ETHERNETIP`| TCP `44818` | ODVA CIP | Cell Controller $\leftrightarrow$ Logix PLC | Encapsulation `CMD` (`REGISTER_SESSION`, `SEND_RR_DATA`), `CIP_SERVICE`, `CIP_CLASS`/`INSTANCE`/`ATTR` |
| **OPC UA Binary**| `OPCUA` | TCP `4840` | IEC 62541-6 | Level 3.5 IDMZ Historian $\leftrightarrow$ Server| UACP `MSG_TYPE` (`HEL`, `ACK`, `OPN`, `MSG`, `CLO`), `SECURE_CHANNEL_ID`, `ENDPOINT_URL`, `NODE_ID` |

---

## 1. Modbus TCP (`MODBUS` — Default: TCP Port `502`)

A classic Purdue Level 2-to-Level 1 conduit policy permits HMI read polling (Function Codes `0x01..0x04`) on TCP port `502` while blocking unauthorized coil or holding-register writes (`0x05`, `0x06`, `0x10`). Instead of wiring up a Modbus simulator and a physical PLC, you can script both read polls and write attempts in `.fasm` code. On the wire, `MODBUS` wraps a Modbus Protocol Data Unit (PDU: 1-byte Function Code + register address/count/value fields) inside a 7-byte **MBAP (Modbus Application Protocol) header**:
- Bytes `0..2`: 16-bit big-endian Transaction Identifier (`TXID`)
- Bytes `2..4`: 16-bit Protocol Identifier (`PROTO_ID`, `0x0000` for standard Modbus)
- Bytes `4..6`: 16-bit computed byte `Length` (Unit ID byte + PDU length)
- Byte `6`: 8-bit Slave Unit Identifier (`UNITID`)

### 1.1 `MODBUS` Modifiers

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shorthand Func** | `READ_COILS` \| `READ_DISCRETE_INPUTS` \| `READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS` \| `READ_INPUT_REGISTERS` \| `WRITE_SINGLE_COIL` \| `WRITE_SINGLE_REGISTER` \| `WRITE_MULTIPLE_REGISTERS` | `READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS` | Bare keyword setting the 1-byte Modbus Function Code |
| **`FUNC`** | `FUNC "<name>"` | `"READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS"`| Explicit function name string (same 7 values as above) |
| **`TXID`** | `TXID <0..65535>` | `1` | 16-bit MBAP Transaction Identifier correlating master requests and slave replies |
| **`PROTO_ID`** | `PROTO_ID <0..65535>` | `0` (`0x0000`) | 16-bit MBAP Protocol Identifier (`0` = standard Modbus TCP) |
| **`UNITID`** | `UNITID <0..255>` | `1` | 8-bit Unit Identifier (slave station address behind a Modbus TCP-to-RTU gateway) |
| **`ADDR`** | `ADDR <0..65535>` | `0` | 16-bit starting coil or register reference address |
| **`COUNT`** | `COUNT <0..65535>` | `1` | Quantity of coils or 16-bit registers to read/write |
| **`VALUE`** | `VALUE <0..65535>` | `0` | 16-bit coil/register value written in requests or returned in `IS_RESPONSE` frames |
| **`IS_RESPONSE`** | `IS_RESPONSE` | Off (Master Request) | Formats the PDU as a PLC Slave response (encoding `ByteCount = COUNT * 2` followed by `COUNT` big-endian `VALUE` words) |

### 1.2 Supported Modbus Function Codes

| Function Name / Keyword | Hex / Dec Code | Access Type | Typical OT Firewall Policy |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `READ_COILS` | `0x01` (`1`) | Read (1-bit Coils) | Permitted from HMI / Historian |
| `READ_DISCRETE_INPUTS` | `0x02` (`2`) | Read (1-bit Contacts) | Permitted from HMI / Historian |
| `READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS` | `0x03` (`3`) | Read (16-bit R/W Regs) | Permitted from HMI / Historian (Default) |
| `READ_INPUT_REGISTERS` | `0x04` (`4`) | Read (16-bit Analog In) | Permitted from HMI / Historian |
| `WRITE_SINGLE_COIL` | `0x05` (`5`) | Write (1-bit Actuator) | Restricted to authorized Level 2 Operator HMI |
| `WRITE_SINGLE_REGISTER` | `0x06` (`6`) | Write (16-bit Setpoint) | Restricted to authorized Level 2 Operator HMI |
| `WRITE_MULTIPLE_REGISTERS`| `0x10` (`16`) | Bulk Write (16-bit Regs)| Blocked from Level 3/IDMZ; audited on Level 2 |

### Compilable Example: Modbus TCP HMI Polling & Setpoint Write Cycle

```frameassembly
host scada_hmi   { ip 192.168.100.10 mac 00:1b:21:64:00:0a }
host turbine_plc { ip 192.168.100.50 mac 00:80:f4:64:00:32 }

flow modbus_hmi_to_plc(hmi, plc) {
    // 1. Read 4 Holding Registers (0x03) starting at address 40001
    hmi -> plc modbus read_holding_registers txid 101 unitid 1 addr 40001 count 4 wait 2ms
    hmi <- plc modbus read_holding_registers txid 101 unitid 1 count 4 value 1480 is_response wait 5ms

    // 2. Read 2 Analog Input Registers (0x04) at address 30010
    hmi -> plc modbus func "READ_INPUT_REGISTERS" txid 102 unitid 1 addr 30010 count 2 wait 2ms
    hmi <- plc modbus func "READ_INPUT_REGISTERS" txid 102 unitid 1 count 2 value 725 is_response wait 5ms

    // 3. Write Single Holding Register (0x06) to update governor RPM setpoint
    hmi -> plc modbus write_single_register txid 103 unitid 1 addr 40010 value 1500 wait 2ms
    hmi <- plc modbus write_single_register txid 103 unitid 1 addr 40010 value 1500 is_response
}

compile {
    modbus_hmi_to_plc(scada_hmi, turbine_plc)
}
```

---

## 2. BACnet/IP (`BACNET` — Default: UDP Port `47808` / `0xBAC0`)

Building Management Systems (BMS), data-center chillers, and HVAC controllers speak BACnet/IP over UDP port `47808` (`0xBAC0`). To test campus segmentation between BMS workstations and field controllers without touching the building's air conditioning, write the discovery and property exchange in `.fasm` code. `BACNET` builds ANSI/ASHRAE 135 Building Automation and Control Networks frames over UDP port `47808` (`0xBAC0`), packing:
1. **4-byte BVLC (BACnet Virtual Link Control) Header:** Type `0x81` (`BACnet/IP`), Function `0x0B` (`Original-Broadcast-NPDU` for `WHO_IS`) or `0x0A` (`Original-Unicast-NPDU` for `I_AM`, `READ_PROPERTY`, and `WRITE_PROPERTY`), and 16-bit total length.
2. **2-byte NPDU (Network Layer) Header:** Protocol Version `0x01`, Control `0x00`.
3. **APDU (Application Layer):** Encodes unconfirmed discovery (`Who-Is` / `I-Am`) or confirmed property access (`ReadProperty` / `WriteProperty`) with a packed 32-bit `ObjectIdentifier` (`(object_type << 22) | (object_instance & 0x3FFFFF)`), context-tagged `PropertyIdentifier`, and application-tagged unsigned integer `PropertyValue`.

### 2.1 `BACNET` Modifiers

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`WHO_IS`** | `WHO_IS` | Default if none set | Unconfirmed-Request APDU (`0x10`, Service `0x08` `Who-Is`) over BVLC Broadcast (`0x0B`) |
| **`I_AM`** | `I_AM` | Off | Unconfirmed-Request APDU (`0x10`, Service `0x00` `I-Am`) announcing Device Object ID |
| **`READ_PROPERTY`** | `READ_PROPERTY` | Off | Confirmed-Request APDU (`0x00`, Service `0x0C` `ReadProperty`) over BVLC Unicast (`0x0A`) |
| **`WRITE_PROPERTY`** | `WRITE_PROPERTY` | Auto if `VALUE` set | Confirmed-Request APDU (`0x00`, Service `0x0F` `WriteProperty`) writing `VALUE` |
| **`INVOKE_ID`** | `INVOKE_ID <0..255>` | `1` | 8-bit APDU correlation Invoke ID for `READ_PROPERTY` and `WRITE_PROPERTY` |
| **`OBJECT_TYPE`** | `OBJECT_TYPE <0..1023>` | `8` (`Device`) | 10-bit BACnet Object Type (`0` = Analog Input, `1` = Analog Output, `2` = Analog Value, `3` = Binary Input, `4` = Binary Output, `5` = Binary Value, `8` = Device) |
| **`OBJECT_INSTANCE`**| `OBJECT_INSTANCE <0..4194303>` | `1234` | 22-bit BACnet Object Instance number (`0..4194303`) |
| **`PROPERTY_ID`** | `PROPERTY_ID <number>` | `85` (`Present_Value`)| BACnet Property Identifier (`85` = `Present_Value`, `77` = `Object_Name`, `111` = `Status_Flags`, `28` = `Description`) |
| **`VALUE`** | `VALUE <number>` | Omitted | Application-tagged 32-bit unsigned integer property value |

### Compilable Example: BACnet/IP BMS Discovery, Sensor Read & Chiller Setpoint Write

```frameassembly
host bms_workstation { ip 10.120.1.10 }
host hvac_controller { ip 10.120.1.50 }

flow bacnet_building_automation(bms, ahu) {
    // 1. Broadcast Who-Is discovery and unicast I-Am reply for Device #1010
    bms -> ahu bacnet who_is wait 2ms
    bms <- ahu bacnet i_am object_type 8 object_instance 1010 wait 5ms

    // 2. Read Present_Value (85) of Analog Input #1 (Supply Air Temp)
    bms -> ahu bacnet read_property invoke_id 10 object_type 0 object_instance 1 property_id 85 wait 2ms
    bms <- ahu bacnet read_property invoke_id 10 object_type 0 object_instance 1 property_id 85 value 58 wait 5ms

    // 3. Write Present_Value (85) = 72 to Analog Value #2 (Zone Temp Setpoint)
    bms -> ahu bacnet write_property invoke_id 11 object_type 2 object_instance 2 property_id 85 value 72
}

compile {
    bacnet_building_automation(bms_workstation, hvac_controller)
}
```

---

## 3. Distributed Network Protocol v3 (`DNP3` — Default: TCP / UDP Port `20000`)

Crafting IEEE 1815 DNP3 packets by hand is notoriously painful because DNP3 requires a reflected CRC-16 (`0xA653`) on the 10-byte Data Link header *and* a separate CRC-16 after every 16-byte chunk of application data—get one bit wrong and Wireshark or your substation firewall drops the frame as corrupted. FrameAssembly computes every DNP3 CRC-16 automatically from `.fasm` code, letting you simulate Class 0 integrity polls (`READ`) and Control Relay Output Block (`CROB` Group `12`) `SELECT` / `OPERATE` breaker sequences for electrical substations, water treatment plants, and oil/gas RTUs:
1. **10-byte Data Link Layer Header:** Start bytes `0x0564`, `Length`, Control byte `0xC4`, 16-bit little-endian `DST` and `SRC` outstation addresses, and a 16-bit little-endian **IEEE 1815 DNP3 CRC-16** (reflected polynomial `0xA653`, initial `0x0000`, inverted remainder).
2. **1-byte Transport Header (`0xC0`):** `FIN = 1`, `FIR = 1`, `SEQ = 0`.
3. **Application Layer & Object Header:** Application Control (`0xC0`), 1-byte Function Code, Object `GROUP` and `VARIATION`, Qualifier `0x06` (all objects), and automatic 16-bit DNP3 CRC-16 appended after every 16-byte user data block.

### 3.1 `DNP3` Modifiers

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shorthand Func** | `CONFIRM` \| `READ` \| `WRITE` \| `SELECT` \| `OPERATE` \| `DIRECT_OPERATE` \| `UNSOLICITED_RESPONSE` | `READ` | Bare keyword setting the DNP3 Application Function Code |
| **`FUNC`** | `FUNC "<name>"` | `"READ"` | Explicit function string (`"CONFIRM"` `0`, `"READ"` `1`, `"WRITE"` `2`, `"SELECT"` `3`, `"OPERATE"` `4`, `"DIRECT_OPERATE"` `5`, `"RESPONSE"` `129`, `"UNSOLICITED_RESPONSE"` `130`) |
| **`SRC`** | `SRC <0..65535>` | `100` | 16-bit little-endian Data Link source address (Master or Outstation ID) |
| **`DST`** | `DST <0..65535>` | `1` | 16-bit little-endian Data Link destination address |
| **`GROUP`** | `GROUP <0..255>` | `60` (if set) | DNP3 Object Group (`1` Binary Input, `10` Binary Output, `12` CROB Control Relay, `30` Analog Input, `40` Analog Output, `60` Class 0/1/2/3 Data) |
| **`VARIATION`** | `VARIATION <0..255>` | `1` (if set) | DNP3 Object Variation (`1` = Class 0 / 32-bit with flags, `2` = Class 1, `3` = Class 2, `4` = Class 3) |
| **`CRC`** | `CRC <0..65535>` | Auto-computed | Overrides the 16-bit Data Link header CRC (useful for testing IDS checksum-anomaly rules) |

### Compilable Example: Substation Class 0 Poll & Select-Before-Operate Breaker Trip

```frameassembly
host dms_master     { ip 10.200.1.1  mac 00:1b:21:c8:01:01 }
host substation_rtu { ip 10.200.1.50 mac 00:a0:c9:c8:01:32 }

flow dnp3_substation_control(master, rtu) {
    // 1. Class 0 Integrity Poll (Group 60 Variation 1) and Analog Input Response (Group 30 Variation 1)
    master -> rtu dnp3 read src 1 dst 50 group 60 variation 1 wait 3ms
    master <- rtu dnp3 func "RESPONSE" src 50 dst 1 group 30 variation 1 wait 5ms

    // 2. Control Relay Output Block (CROB Group 12 Variation 1) Select-Before-Operate sequence
    master -> rtu dnp3 select src 1 dst 50 group 12 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master <- rtu dnp3 func "RESPONSE" src 50 dst 1 group 12 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master -> rtu dnp3 operate src 1 dst 50 group 12 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master <- rtu dnp3 func "RESPONSE" src 50 dst 1 group 12 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master -> rtu dnp3 confirm src 1 dst 50
}

compile {
    dnp3_substation_control(dms_master, substation_rtu)
}
```

---

## 4. Siemens SIMATIC S7comm (`S7COMM` — Default: TCP Port `102`)

Validating deep packet inspection rules for Siemens SIMATIC S7-300/400/1200/1500 PLCs—such as allowing `READ_VAR` (`0x04`) on Data Blocks while alerting on `WRITE_VAR` (`0x05`) or `PLC_CONTROL` (`0x28`) over TCP port `102`—normally requires Siemens TIA Portal and hardware controllers. In `.fasm` code, `S7COMM` builds complete Siemens SIMATIC PLC communication frames over ISO-on-TCP (RFC 1006, TCP port `102`):
1. **4-byte TPKT Header:** Version `3`, Reserved `0`, 16-bit big-endian total packet length.
2. **3-byte ISO 8073 COTP Header:** `0x02 0xF0 0x80` (`DT Data` TPDU with `EOT = 1`).
3. **10-byte / 12-byte S7 Header:** Magic byte `0x32`, `ROSCTR` (`0x01` `JOB`, `0x02` `ACK`, `0x03` `ACK_DATA`, `0x07` `USERDATA`), 16-bit `PDU_REF`, parameter/data lengths, and a 2-byte error class/code field on `ACK`/`ACK_DATA` replies.
4. **S7 Parameter Block:** Encodes `SETUP_COMM` (`0xF0`, 480-byte PDU size negotiation), `READ_VAR` (`0x04`) / `WRITE_VAR` (`0x05`) with a 10-byte `S7ANY` memory pointer (`AREA`, `DB_NUM`, bit-shifted `OFFSET << 3`, and `COUNT`), or `PLC_CONTROL` (`0x28`).

### 4.1 `S7COMM` Modifiers

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shorthand Func** | `SETUP_COMM` \| `READ_VAR` \| `WRITE_VAR` \| `PLC_CONTROL` | `SETUP_COMM` | Bare keyword setting the S7 Parameter Function Code |
| **`FUNC`** | `FUNC "<name>"` | `"SETUP_COMM"` | Explicit S7 function string (`"SETUP_COMM"` `0xF0`, `"READ_VAR"` `0x04`, `"WRITE_VAR"` `0x05`, `"PLC_CONTROL"` `0x28`) |
| **`ROSCTR`** | `ROSCTR "<type>"` | `"JOB"` | Remote Operating Service Control (`"JOB"` `0x01` request, `"ACK"` `0x02`, `"ACK_DATA"` `0x03` response, `"USERDATA"` `0x07`) |
| **`PDU_REF`** | `PDU_REF <0..65535>` | `1` | 16-bit PDU Reference number matching `JOB` requests with `ACK_DATA` replies |
| **`AREA`** | `AREA <0..255\|"<name>">` | `0x84` (`DB`) | PLC memory area (`0x84` / `"DB"` Data Blocks, `0x83` / `"MK"` Merker flags, `0x81` / `"PE"` Process Inputs, `0x82` / `"PA"` Process Outputs) |
| **`DB_NUM`** | `DB_NUM <0..65535>` | `1` | Data Block number (`DB1`, `DB10`, etc.) when `AREA` is `0x84` |
| **`OFFSET`** | `OFFSET <number>` | `0` | Byte offset within the memory area (automatically multiplied by 8 into a 24-bit S7 bit address) |
| **`COUNT`** | `COUNT <0..65535>` | `1` | Number of bytes to read or write |
| **`PAYLOAD`** | `PAYLOAD "<text>"` | Empty | S7 data block payload for `WRITE_VAR` or `ACK_DATA` frames |

### Compilable Example: Siemens S7comm Session Setup, Data Block Read & Write

```frameassembly
host tia_portal { ip 10.80.10.5  mac 00:1b:21:50:0a:05 }
host s7_1500    { ip 10.80.10.20 mac 00:0e:8c:50:0a:14 }

flow siemens_s7_plc_polling(eng, plc) {
    // 1. Negotiate S7 communication PDU size (SETUP_COMM 0xF0)
    eng -> plc s7comm rosctr "JOB" setup_comm pdu_ref 100 wait 2ms
    eng <- plc s7comm rosctr "ACK_DATA" setup_comm pdu_ref 100 wait 2ms

    // 2. Read 16 bytes from Data Block DB1 starting at byte offset 0
    eng -> plc s7comm rosctr "JOB" read_var pdu_ref 101 area 0x84 db_num 1 offset 0 count 16 wait 2ms
    eng <- plc s7comm rosctr "ACK_DATA" read_var pdu_ref 101 count 16 payload "S7_DB1_TELEMETRY" wait 5ms

    // 3. Write 4 bytes to Data Block DB10 at byte offset 8
    eng -> plc s7comm rosctr "JOB" write_var pdu_ref 102 area 0x84 db_num 10 offset 8 count 4 payload "VAL1" wait 2ms
    eng <- plc s7comm rosctr "ACK_DATA" write_var pdu_ref 102
}

compile {
    siemens_s7_plc_polling(tia_portal, s7_1500)
}
```

---

## 5. ODVA EtherNet/IP & CIP (`ETHERNETIP` — Default: TCP Port `44818`)

Rockwell Automation / Allen-Bradley ControlLogix and CompactLogix environments use ODVA EtherNet/IP over TCP port `44818` to discover assets (`ListIdentity`), register sessions, and read/write Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) objects. Rather than capturing live Studio 5000 traffic on the plant floor, you can express the encapsulation command and CIP EPATH (`Class` / `Instance` / `Attribute`) in `.fasm` code. `ETHERNETIP` builds ODVA EtherNet/IP frames with:
1. **24-byte Little-Endian Encapsulation Header:** 16-bit `Command`, 16-bit `Length`, 32-bit `SessionHandle`, 32-bit `Status`, 64-bit `SenderContext`, and 32-bit `Options`.
2. **Common Packet Format (CPF) & CIP EPATH:** For `SEND_RR_DATA` (`0x006F`) and `SEND_UNIT_DATA` (`0x0070`) packets (or whenever any `CIP_*` modifier is specified), FrameAssembly automatically constructs a 2-item CPF body (`Null Address Item 0x0000` + `Unconnected Data Item 0x00B2`) containing the CIP Service code and logical EPATH segments (`0x20 <Class>`, `0x24 <Instance>`, and optional `0x30 <Attribute>`).

### 5.1 `ETHERNETIP` Modifiers

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shorthand Cmd** | `LIST_IDENTITY` \| `LIST_SERVICES` \| `LIST_INTERFACES` \| `REGISTER_SESSION` \| `UNREGISTER_SESSION` \| `SEND_RR_DATA` \| `SEND_UNIT_DATA` | `LIST_IDENTITY` (or `SEND_RR_DATA` if `CIP_*` set) | Bare keyword setting the 16-bit little-endian Encapsulation Command |
| **`CMD`** | `CMD "<name>"` | Auto-selected | Explicit command string (`"NOP"` `0x0000`, `"LIST_SERVICES"` `0x0004`, `"LIST_IDENTITY"` `0x0063`, `"LIST_INTERFACES"` `0x0064`, `"REGISTER_SESSION"` `0x0065`, `"UNREGISTER_SESSION"` `0x0066`, `"SEND_RR_DATA"` `0x006F`, `"SEND_UNIT_DATA"` `0x0070`) |
| **`SESSION_HANDLE`** | `SESSION_HANDLE <number>` | `0` | 32-bit little-endian session handle assigned by `REGISTER_SESSION` |
| **`STATUS`** | `STATUS <number>` | `0` (`Success`) | 32-bit encapsulation status (`0x0000` Success, `0x0001` Invalid command, `0x0064` Invalid session handle) |
| **`CONTEXT`** | `CONTEXT <64-bit_id>` | `0` | 64-bit little-endian `SenderContext` correlation value |
| **`CIP_SERVICE`** | `CIP_SERVICE <0..255>` | `0x0E` (`Get_Attr_Single`) | 8-bit CIP service code (`0x01` `Get_Attributes_All`, `0x0E` `Get_Attribute_Single`, `0x10` `Set_Attribute_Single`, `0x4C` `Read_Tag`, `0x4D` `Write_Tag`) |
| **`CIP_CLASS`** | `CIP_CLASS <0..65535>` | `1` (`Identity`) | CIP Object Class ID (`0x01` Identity, `0x02` Message Router, `0x04` Assembly, `0x06` Connection Manager, `0x6B` Symbol) |
| **`CIP_INSTANCE`** | `CIP_INSTANCE <0..65535>` | `1` | CIP Object Instance ID (e.g., Assembly Instance `100` or `150`) |
| **`CIP_ATTR`** | `CIP_ATTR <0..65535>` | Omitted | Optional 3rd logical EPATH segment (`0x30 <attr>`, e.g., `3` for Assembly Data attribute) |

### Compilable Example: EtherNet/IP Device Discovery, Session Registration & CIP Assembly Read

```frameassembly
host factory_scada { ip 10.80.20.5  }
host logix_plc     { ip 10.80.20.30 }

flow ethernetip_cip_session(scada, plc) {
    // 1. Asset discovery via ListIdentity (0x0063)
    scada -> plc ethernetip list_identity context 0x0001000200030004 wait 1ms
    scada <- plc ethernetip list_identity status 0 context 0x0001000200030004 wait 2ms

    // 2. Register an explicit messaging session (0x0065)
    scada -> plc ethernetip register_session context 100 wait 1ms
    scada <- plc ethernetip register_session session_handle 0x0001a2b3 status 0 context 100 wait 2ms

    // 3. Read CIP Assembly Object (Class 0x04, Instance 100, Attribute 3) via SendRRData (0x006F)
    scada -> plc ethernetip send_rr_data session_handle 0x0001a2b3 context 101 cip_service 0x0e cip_class 0x04 cip_instance 100 cip_attr 3 wait 2ms
    scada <- plc ethernetip send_rr_data session_handle 0x0001a2b3 status 0 context 101 payload "CIP_ASSEMBLY_100_DATA" wait 5ms

    // 4. Cleanly unregister session (0x0066)
    scada -> plc ethernetip unregister_session session_handle 0x0001a2b3 context 102
}

compile {
    ethernetip_cip_session(factory_scada, logix_plc)
}
```

---

## 6. OPC Unified Architecture Binary (`OPCUA` — Default: TCP Port `4840`)

In IEC 62443 architectures, the conduit across the Level 3.5 Industrial DMZ (IDMZ) between plant-floor servers and enterprise historians almost always runs OPC UA Binary (`opc.tcp`) on TCP port `4840`. To test IDMZ firewall conduits and `NodeId` inspection rules without standing up an OPC UA server/client pair, `OPCUA` builds IEC 62541-6 OPC UA Connection Protocol (`UACP`) binary messages over TCP port `4840`:
- **8-byte UACP Header:** 3-byte ASCII `MessageType` (`HEL`, `ACK`, `ERR`, `OPN`, `CLO`, `MSG`), 1-byte `ChunkType` (`'F'` Final, `'C'` Intermediate, `'A'` Aborted), and 32-bit little-endian `MessageSize`.
- **Connection & SecureChannel Bodies:** `HEL` and `ACK` frames automatically populate the 20-byte receive/send buffer negotiation fields (64 KB buffers, 16 MB max message, 5,000 max chunks) plus length-prefixed `ENDPOINT_URL`. `OPN`, `MSG`, and `CLO` frames encode 32-bit little-endian `SECURE_CHANNEL_ID`, `TOKEN_ID`, `SEQ_NUM`, `REQID`, and string `NODE_ID` descriptors.

### 6.1 `OPCUA` Modifiers

| Modifier | Syntax | Default | Wire Behavior & Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`MSG_TYPE`** | `MSG_TYPE "<HEL\|ACK\|OPN\|MSG\|CLO\|ERR>"` | `"HEL"` (or `"MSG"` if `NODE_ID` set) | 3-byte ASCII UACP message type |
| **`CHUNK_TYPE`** | `CHUNK_TYPE "<F\|C\|A>"` | `"F"` (`Final`) | 1-byte chunk indicator (`"F"` Final chunk, `"C"` Continuation chunk, `"A"` Abort) |
| **`ENDPOINT_URL`** | `ENDPOINT_URL "<url>"` | Omitted | Length-prefixed discovery URL in `HEL` messages (e.g., `"opc.tcp://10.80.30.20:4840/freeopcua"`) |
| **`SECURE_CHANNEL_ID`**| `SECURE_CHANNEL_ID <number>`| `1` | 32-bit little-endian SecureChannel ID in `OPN`, `MSG`, and `CLO` frames |
| **`TOKEN_ID`** | `TOKEN_ID <number>` | `1` | 32-bit little-endian Security Token ID |
| **`SEQ_NUM`** | `SEQ_NUM <number>` | `1` | 32-bit little-endian chunk Sequence Number |
| **`REQID`** | `REQID <number>` | `1` | 32-bit little-endian client Request ID |
| **`NODE_ID`** | `NODE_ID "<text>"` | Omitted | Encodes a String NodeId (`0x03` mask) in `MSG` service calls (e.g., `"ns=2;s=Boiler1.Pressure"`) |

### Compilable Example: OPC UA Binary Lifecycle (`HEL` $\rightarrow$ `ACK` $\rightarrow$ `OPN` $\rightarrow$ `MSG` $\rightarrow$ `CLO`)

```frameassembly
host idmz_historian { ip 10.80.30.5  }
host opcua_server   { ip 10.80.30.20 }

flow opcua_historian_collection(hist, srv) {
    // 1. UACP Hello (HEL) and Acknowledge (ACK) buffer size negotiation
    hist -> srv opcua msg_type "HEL" chunk_type "F" endpoint_url "opc.tcp://10.80.30.20:4840/plant/server" wait 2ms
    hist <- srv opcua msg_type "ACK" chunk_type "F" wait 2ms

    // 2. OpenSecureChannel (OPN) request and response
    hist -> srv opcua msg_type "OPN" chunk_type "F" secure_channel_id 10 token_id 1 seq_num 1 reqid 1 wait 2ms
    hist <- srv opcua msg_type "OPN" chunk_type "F" secure_channel_id 10 token_id 1 seq_num 1 reqid 1 wait 2ms

    // 3. Read NodeId telemetry via MSG chunks
    hist -> srv opcua msg_type "MSG" chunk_type "F" secure_channel_id 10 token_id 1 seq_num 2 reqid 2 node_id "ns=2;s=Line01.ExtruderTempC" wait 2ms
    hist <- srv opcua msg_type "MSG" chunk_type "F" secure_channel_id 10 token_id 1 seq_num 2 reqid 2 node_id "ns=2;s=Line01.ExtruderTempC" payload "OPCUA_DATA_VALUE_215.4C" wait 5ms

    // 4. CloseSecureChannel (CLO)
    hist -> srv opcua msg_type "CLO" chunk_type "F" secure_channel_id 10 token_id 1 seq_num 3 reqid 3
}

compile {
    opcua_historian_collection(idmz_historian, opcua_server)
}
```

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md`

# Multi-Host Network Topologies & Dual-Stack Scenarios

Real production incidents rarely happen between just two hosts speaking a single protocol. A single user login, WAN failover, or microservice call typically crosses Layer 2 switching, Layer 3 routing or tunneling, Layer 4 transport handshakes, and three or four Layer 7 services across 4 to 8 devices.

Reproducing that kind of multi-hop sequence in a physical lab or a virtual network emulator (GNS3, EVE-NG, Containerlab) just to get a clean test capture takes hours: you have to boot half a dozen router and server images, wire up VLAN trunks and VRFs, configure routing protocols and AAA daemons, and then coordinate `tcpdump` across multiple interfaces while manually triggering the event.

FrameAssembly lets you express the entire multi-device conversation in a single `.fasm` file ("Packets as Code") and run it with two CLI commands (`frameassembly topology.fasm -o topology.pcap` to compile + `tcpreplay`, **Wireshark**, or **Suricata** to replay or inspect) using three core capabilities:

1. **Multi-Host Flows:** Pass 3, 4, or 8+ endpoints into a single `flow(client, switch, radius, firewall, server, siem)` to interleave north-south client traffic, east-west service calls, and out-of-band telemetry in exact chronological order.
2. **Reusable Dual-Stack IPv4 & IPv6 Flows:** Write a `flow` once and run it inside `compile` first with IPv4 `host` definitions and then with IPv6 `host` definitions—automatically switching between IPv4 (`EtherType 0x0800`) and IPv6 (`EtherType 0x86DD`), recomputing IPv4/IPv6 pseudo-header checksums, and deriving multicast MAC addresses per RFC 1112 (`01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx`) and RFC 2464 (`33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx`).
3. **Deterministic `wait` Timers & `loop` Traffic Bursts:** Combine nanosecond-to-minute inter-packet delays (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`) with `loop <count> { ... }` blocks inside `compile` to generate realistic keepalive cadences, VXLAN/IPsec bursts, and RTP media streams.

> **104 Ready-to-Compile Topologies in `examples/topologies/`:**
> In addition to the 5 reference architectures below, you can browse **104 full-stack `.fasm` scenarios** in [`examples/topologies/`](../examples/topologies/).

---

## Core Architectural Building Blocks

### 1. Multi-Host Flows Across 3 to 8+ Devices

A `flow` header can accept any number of host endpoints. Inside the flow body, every statement specifies which two endpoints are communicating on that line (`ws -> sw`, `sw -> aaa`, `aaa -> siem`):

```text
flow branch_transaction(client, edge_fw, app_srv, siem) {
    client  -> app_srv tcp syn dstport 443 wait 1ms
    edge_fw -> siem    syslog facility 4 severity 6 msg "Permit TCP 443" wait 1ms
    client  <- app_srv tcp syn ack
}
```

When you run `branch_transaction(workstation, perimeter_fw, web_srv, splunk_siem)` inside `compile { ... }`, FrameAssembly plugs those four `host` definitions into `(client, edge_fw, app_srv, siem)` in matching left-to-right order.

### 2. Dual-Stack IPv4 / IPv6 Reuse & Multicast MAC Derivation

FrameAssembly enforces strict Layer 3 address-family consistency per statement (mixing an IPv4 host and an IPv6 host on the same arrow is rejected with a clear validation error), while allowing the exact same `flow` block to run unmodified over both IPv4 and IPv6:

| Feature | IPv4 Execution (`host { ip 10.x.x.x }`) | IPv6 Execution (`host { ip 2001:db8::x }`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ethernet EtherType** | `0x0800` (or `0x8100` / `0x88A8` / `0x8847` when tagged) | `0x86DD` (or `0x8100` / `0x88A8` / `0x8847` when tagged) |
| **L3 `ttl <0..255>` & `dscp <0..63>`** | Maps to IPv4 `TTL` and `TOS/DSCP` | Maps to IPv6 `Hop Limit` and `Traffic Class` |
| **L3 `flowlabel <0..1048575>`** | Silently ignored on IPv4 statements | Encoded into the 20-bit IPv6 `Flow Label` field |
| **Multicast Destination MAC** | Auto-derived as `01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx` (RFC 1112) when `mac` is omitted on a `224.0.0.0/4` host | Auto-derived as `33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx` (RFC 2464) when `mac` is omitted on an `ff00::/8` host |
| **UDP Checksum `0x0000` Guard** | RFC 768 checksum | RFC 8200 §8.1 mandatory pseudo-header checksum (`0x0000` mapped to `0xFFFF`) |

### 3. `loop <count> { ... }` Bursts in `compile`

Inside `compile { ... }`, wrap one or more flow calls in `loop <count> { ... }` to repeat traffic bursts while automatically advancing TCP sequence numbers and packet timestamps across iterations:

```text
compile {
    underlay_bringup(spine_01, leaf_01)
    loop 10 {
        vxlan_east_west_burst(leaf_01, leaf_02)
    }
}
```

---

## 1. EVPN-VXLAN Leaf-Spine Data Center Fabric (`LLDP` + `BFD` + `BGP` + `VXLAN` + `IPFIX`)

**Scenario:** Models a data center fabric link bring-up between a Spine switch (`spine_01`) and two ToR Leaf VTEPs (`leaf_01`, `leaf_02`), followed by an East-West VXLAN tenant burst and an IPFIX flow telemetry export to a fabric collector:
1. **Layer 2 Link Discovery (`LLDP`):** Spine and Leaf exchange chassis/port capabilities and system names.
2. **Sub-Second Failure Detection (`BFD`):** 50ms (`50000` $\mu\text{s}$) BFD Control sessions reach State `3` (`Up`) with `TTL 255` GTSM protection.
3. **Underlay Routing (`BGP`):** eBGP `OPEN` (`ASN 65101` $\leftrightarrow$ `ASN 65000`), `KEEPALIVE`, and `/32` VTEP loopback `UPDATE` advertisement.
4. **Overlay Data Plane (`VXLAN`):** A 4-packet `loop` burst encapsulating tenant traffic in `VNI 10100` with `DSCP 26` (`AF31`) and the IPv4 Don't Fragment (`DF`) bit set for Path MTU validation.
5. **Fabric Visibility (`IPFIX`):** `leaf_01` exports a CFlow/IPFIX v10 accounting record summarizing the 4-packet VXLAN burst to `collector` on UDP port `4739`.

```frameassembly
host spine_01  { ip 10.255.0.1    mac 00:1c:73:00:00:01 }
host leaf_01   { ip 10.255.0.11   mac 00:1c:73:00:01:01 }
host leaf_02   { ip 10.255.0.12   mac 00:1c:73:00:01:02 }
host collector { ip 10.255.100.50 mac 00:1c:73:00:99:50 }

flow underlay_bringup(spine, leaf) {
    // 1. IEEE 802.1AB LLDP neighbor discovery on point-to-point fabric link
    spine -> leaf lldp chassis_id "spine-01.dc1" port_id "Ethernet1/1" ttl 120 sysname "spine-01" sysdesc "Arista EOS 4.32" wait 1ms
    spine <- leaf lldp chassis_id "leaf-01.dc1" port_id "Ethernet49/1" ttl 120 sysname "leaf-01" sysdesc "Arista EOS 4.32" wait 2ms

    // 2. RFC 5880 BFD 50ms timers (State 3 = Up, Multiplier = 3, TTL = 255)
    spine <- leaf bfd state 3 my_disc 101 your_disc 1 min_tx 50000 min_rx 50000 mult 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine -> leaf bfd state 3 my_disc 1 your_disc 101 min_tx 50000 min_rx 50000 mult 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms

    // 3. RFC 4271 eBGP peering and VTEP loopback /32 route advertisement
    spine <- leaf bgp open asn 65101 holdtime 90 bgpid 10.255.0.11 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine -> leaf bgp open asn 65000 holdtime 90 bgpid 10.255.0.1 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine <- leaf bgp keepalive ttl 255 wait 1ms
    spine -> leaf bgp keepalive ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine <- leaf bgp update asn 65101 prefix "10.254.1.11/32" nexthop 10.255.0.11 ttl 255 wait 5ms
}

flow vxlan_east_west(vtep1, vtep2) {
    // RFC 7348 VXLAN UDP 4789 overlay frame (VNI 10100, DSCP AF31 = 26, Don't Fragment)
    vtep1 -> vtep2 vxlan vni 10100 dscp 26 df payload "EAST_WEST_TENANT_RPC_FRAME" wait 2ms
}

flow export_fabric_telemetry(leaf, col) {
    // RFC 7011 IPFIX v10 flow record reporting the 4 VXLAN packets (512 octets)
    leaf -> col ipfix seq 1 domain_id 100 srcip 10.255.0.11 dstip 10.255.0.12 proto 17 srcport 49152 dstport 4789 packets 4 octets 512
}

compile {
    underlay_bringup(spine_01, leaf_01)
    loop 4 {
        vxlan_east_west(leaf_01, leaf_02)
    }
    export_fabric_telemetry(leaf_01, collector)
}
```

---

## 2. Campus Zero-Trust 802.1X NAC Port Onboarding (`EAPOL` + `RADIUS` + `DHCP` + `ARP` + `SNMP3`)

**Scenario:** Captures the complete lifecycle of an employee workstation plugging into a Zero-Trust campus switch port across 4 network tiers (`workstation`, `access_sw`, `radius_srv`, and `nms_srv`):
1. **802.1X Supplicant Handshake (`EAPOL`):** The laptop sends `EAPOL-Start`, responds to the switch's `EAP-Request/Identity` (`eap_code 1, eap_method 1`), and awaits port authorization.
2. **AAA Policy Verification (`RADIUS`):** The switch relays the identity to the RADIUS server (`Access-Request` on UDP `1812`) and receives `Access-Accept` with the assigned `Framed-IP-Address`, then sends `EAP-Success` (`eap_code 3`) to open the switch port.
3. **IPv4 Address Assignment (`DHCP`):** Full 4-packet `DORA` exchange (`Discover` $\rightarrow$ `Offer` $\rightarrow$ `Request` $\rightarrow$ `Ack`) assigning `10.10.50.100/24`.
4. **Duplicate Address Detection (`ARP`):** The workstation broadcasts a Gratuitous ARP (`senderip` and `targetip` both set to `10.10.50.100`).
5. **Encrypted NMS Audit (`SNMP3`):** The switch sends an authenticated and AES-128-CFB encrypted `SNMPv3 InformRequest` (`SHA256` + `AES`) to the NMS reporting `ifOperStatus = up(1)` on port 12.

```frameassembly
host workstation { ip 10.10.50.100 mac 00:22:44:66:88:aa }
host access_sw   { ip 10.10.50.1   mac 00:11:22:33:44:01 }
host radius_srv  { ip 10.10.1.10   mac 00:11:22:33:44:10 }
host nms_srv     { ip 10.10.1.20   mac 00:11:22:33:44:20 }

flow campus_dot1x_onboarding(ws, sw, aaa, nms) {
    // 1. IEEE 802.1X EAPOL Start and EAP-Identity exchange
    ws -> sw eapol version 2 type start wait 2ms
    ws <- sw eapol version 2 type eap_packet eap_code 1 eap_id 1 eap_method 1 wait 2ms
    ws -> sw eapol version 2 type eap_packet eap_code 2 eap_id 1 eap_method 1 identity "eng-laptop-42" wait 2ms

    // 2. RADIUS Access-Request / Access-Accept and EAP-Success (eap_code 3)
    sw -> aaa radius access_request id 42 user "eng-laptop-42" nas_ip 10.10.50.1 wait 5ms
    sw <- aaa radius access_accept id 42 framed_ip 10.10.50.100 wait 2ms
    ws <- sw eapol version 2 type eap_packet eap_code 3 eap_id 1 wait 5ms

    // 3. DHCPv4 DORA lease acquisition (Discover -> Offer -> Request -> Ack)
    ws -> sw dhcp discover txid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa wait 5ms
    ws <- sw dhcp offer txid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa yiaddr 10.10.50.100 router 10.10.50.1 dns_server 10.10.1.53 subnet_mask 255.255.255.0 lease_time 43200 wait 5ms
    ws -> sw dhcp request txid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa yiaddr 10.10.50.100 wait 5ms
    ws <- sw dhcp ack txid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa yiaddr 10.10.50.100 router 10.10.50.1 dns_server 10.10.1.53 subnet_mask 255.255.255.0 lease_time 43200 wait 5ms

    // 4. RFC 5227 Gratuitous ARP announcement
    ws -> sw arp gratuitous sha 00:22:44:66:88:aa spa 10.10.50.100 tpa 10.10.50.100 wait 2ms

    // 5. SNMPv3 USM authPriv (HMAC-SHA-256 + AES-128) Inform to NMS
    sw -> nms snmp3 inform user "nac_auditor" engineid "80001f88801122334455" engineboots 5 enginetime 3600 auth sha256 "AuditAuthKey2026!" priv aes "AuditPrivKey2026!" reqid 500 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "access-sw-floor2" varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.12 int 1
}

compile {
    campus_dot1x_onboarding(workstation, access_sw, radius_srv, nms_srv)
}
```

---

## 3. Dual-Stack IPv4 & IPv6 Cloud Service Mesh (`DNS` + `TCP` + `TLS` + `GRPC` + `REDIS` + `POSTGRES`)

**Scenario:** Demonstrates **reusable dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 flow generation**. A single 4-tier Kubernetes service-mesh flow (`service_mesh_checkout`) models:
1. CoreDNS service discovery (`DNS`)
2. Explicit 3-way TCP handshake (`SYN` $\rightarrow$ `SYN ACK` $\rightarrow$ `ACK`) on port `50051`
3. mTLS 1.3 negotiation with SNI and ALPN `"h2"` (`TLS`)
4. Unary gRPC `CreateOrder` call (`GRPC`)
5. East-west Redis inventory cache lookup (`REDIS`) and PostgreSQL SQL order insert (`POSTGRES`)

In `compile`, calling `service_mesh_checkout` first with the `_v4` hosts and then with the `_v6` hosts generates both the complete IPv4 cluster trace and the complete IPv6 cluster trace in one PCAPNG file.

```frameassembly
// IPv4 Kubernetes Pod & Service Endpoints
host ingress_v4 { ip 10.244.1.10 }
host coredns_v4 { ip 10.96.0.10 }
host orders_v4  { ip 10.244.2.20 }
host storage_v4 { ip 10.244.3.30 }

// IPv6 Kubernetes Pod & Service Endpoints
host ingress_v6 { ip fd00:10:244:1::10 }
host coredns_v6 { ip fd00:10:96::10 }
host orders_v6  { ip fd00:10:244:2::20 }
host storage_v6 { ip fd00:10:244:3::30 }

flow service_mesh_checkout(gw, dns, svc, db) {
    // 1. Internal service discovery via CoreDNS
    gw -> dns dns query txid 901 qname "orders.prod.svc.cluster.local" qtype "A" wait 1ms
    gw <- dns dns response txid 901 qname "orders.prod.svc.cluster.local" qtype "A" rdata "10.244.2.20" wait 1ms

    // 2. TCP 3-way handshake + TLS 1.3 ALPN "h2" + gRPC request on port 50051
    gw -> svc tcp syn srcport 51051 dstport 50051 mss 1460 wscale 7 sack_perm wait 1ms
    gw <- svc tcp syn ack mss 1460 wscale 7 sack_perm wait 1ms
    gw -> svc tcp ack wait 1ms
    gw -> svc tls client_hello sni "orders.prod.svc.cluster.local" ciphersuite 4865 alpn "h2" wait 1ms
    gw <- svc tls server_hello ciphersuite 4865 alpn "h2" wait 1ms
    gw -> svc grpc service "commerce.OrderService" method "CreateOrder" payload "sku=NVME-4TB&qty=2" wait 2ms

    // 3. Server-side Redis cache check (TCP 6379) & PostgreSQL transaction (TCP 5432)
    svc -> db redis get key "inventory:NVME-4TB" wait 1ms
    svc <- db redis reply_type "BULK" value "42" wait 1ms
    svc -> db postgres startup user "orders_app" db "commerce" wait 1ms
    svc <- db postgres auth_ok ready_for_query wait 1ms
    svc -> db postgres query sql "INSERT INTO orders (sku, qty) VALUES ('NVME-4TB', 2);" wait 2ms
    svc <- db postgres command_complete ready_for_query payload "INSERT 0 1" wait 2ms

    // 4. gRPC OK response returned to the ingress gateway
    gw <- svc grpc service "commerce.OrderService" method "CreateOrder" grpc_status 0 payload "order_id=90042" wait 5ms
}

compile {
    // Execute over IPv4 cluster network
    service_mesh_checkout(ingress_v4, coredns_v4, orders_v4, storage_v4)
    // Execute the exact same flow over IPv6 cluster network
    service_mesh_checkout(ingress_v6, coredns_v6, orders_v6, storage_v6)
}
```

---

## 4. WAN Branch Failover & IPsec/MPLS Backhaul (`BFD` + `OSPF` + `VRRP` + `IKEV2`/`ESP` + `QINQ`/`MPLS`)

**Scenario:** Models an enterprise branch office with redundant WAN edge routers (`branch_r1`, `branch_r2`) failing over to an IPsec-over-Metro-Ethernet/MPLS backhaul connected to `hq_hub`:
1. **LAN First-Hop Redundancy (`VRRP`):** `branch_r1` advertises VRRPv3 Group `10` Master ownership (`priority 200`, `vip 10.250.10.1`).
2. **WAN Link Failure & IGP Convergence (`BFD` + `OSPF`):** `branch_r1` signals a BFD `Down` state (`state 1, diag 1`), then floods an Area `0` OSPF Link State Update (`LSU`) to `branch_r2` and receives an `LSACK`.
3. **Carrier QinQ IPsec Tunnel Bring-Up (`QINQ` + `IKEV2`):** `branch_r2` negotiates an IKEv2 Security Association (`SA_INIT` and `AUTH`) with `hq_hub` across a Metro Ethernet IEEE 802.1ad QinQ trunk (`S-VLAN 2100`, `C-VLAN 100`).
4. **MPLS Core Encrypted Data Plane (`MPLS` + `ESP`):** `branch_r2` and `hq_hub` exchange MPLS-labeled (`Label 32100`, `EXP 5`) IPsec `ESP` tunnel packets with explicit Initialization Vectors (`IV`) and Integrity Check Values (`ICV`).

```frameassembly
host branch_r1 { ip 10.250.10.2  mac 00:00:5e:00:01:0a }
host branch_r2 { ip 10.250.10.3  mac 00:1e:be:25:10:03 }
host hq_hub    { ip 172.31.250.1 mac 00:1e:be:31:fa:01 }

flow wan_failover_and_ipsec_mpls(r1, r2, hub) {
    // 1. VRRPv3 LAN gateway advertisement and preemptive priority takeover on VRID 10
    r1 -> r2 vrrp vrid 10 priority 200 adv_int 100 vip 10.250.10.1 version 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms

    // 2. BFD Down notification (state 1, diag 1) triggers OSPF Area 0 LSA flooding
    r1 -> r2 bfd state 1 diag 1 my_disc 501 your_disc 502 min_tx 100000 min_rx 100000 mult 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    r2 -> r1 vrrp vrid 10 priority 220 adv_int 100 vip 10.250.10.1 version 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    r1 -> r2 ospf hello router_id 10.250.0.1 area_id 0 hello_interval 10 dead_interval 40 priority 100 ttl 1 wait 1ms
    r1 -> r2 ospf lsu router_id 10.250.0.1 area_id 0 ttl 1 wait 1ms
    r1 <- r2 ospf lsack router_id 10.250.0.2 area_id 0 ttl 1 wait 3ms

    // 3. IKEv2 SA_INIT and AUTH negotiation over IEEE 802.1ad QinQ (S-VLAN 2100, C-VLAN 100)
    r2 -> hub qinq 2100 inner_vlan 100 dscp 48 ikev2 exchange sa_init initiator_spi 0x1122334455667788 responder_spi 0 msgid 0 flags 0x08 wait 2ms
    r2 <- hub qinq 2100 inner_vlan 100 dscp 48 ikev2 exchange sa_init initiator_spi 0x1122334455667788 responder_spi 0x99aabbccddeeff00 msgid 0 flags 0x20 wait 2ms
    r2 -> hub qinq 2100 inner_vlan 100 dscp 48 ikev2 exchange auth initiator_spi 0x1122334455667788 responder_spi 0x99aabbccddeeff00 msgid 1 flags 0x08 wait 2ms
    r2 <- hub qinq 2100 inner_vlan 100 dscp 48 ikev2 exchange auth initiator_spi 0x1122334455667788 responder_spi 0x99aabbccddeeff00 msgid 1 flags 0x20 wait 3ms

    // 4. Encrypted IPsec ESP tunnel traffic over MPLS Label 32100 (EXP 5 EF)
    r2 -> hub mpls 32100 exp 5 bos 1 mpls_ttl 60 dscp 46 esp spi 0x00102030 seq 1 iv "1122334455667788" icv "aabbccddeeff001122334455" next_header 4 payload "ENCRYPTED_BRANCH_VOICE_FRAME_1" wait 2ms
    r2 <- hub mpls 32200 exp 5 bos 1 mpls_ttl 60 dscp 46 esp spi 0x00102031 seq 1 iv "8877665544332211" icv "554433221100ffeeddccbbaa" next_header 4 payload "ENCRYPTED_HQ_VOICE_REPLY_1"
}

compile {
    wan_failover_and_ipsec_mpls(branch_r1, branch_r2, hq_hub)
}
```

---

## 5. IEC 62443 Industrial Substation & IDMZ Conduit (`MODBUS` + `DNP3` + `S7COMM` + `OPCUA` + `SYSLOG`)

**Scenario:** Validates a segmented **IEC 62443 / Purdue Model** industrial architecture spanning Level 2 Supervisory HMI (`substation_hmi`), Level 1 Field Controllers (`bay_rtu`, `s7_plc`), and a Level 3.5 Industrial DMZ Historian & SIEM (`idmz_historian`):
1. **Level 1–2 Process VLAN (`VLAN 110, PCP 6`):** The supervisory HMI polls holding registers from `bay_rtu` via `MODBUS` (TCP `502`), executes an IEEE 1815 `DNP3` Class 0 integrity poll (TCP `20000`), and reads Data Block `DB1` from a Siemens PLC via `S7COMM` (TCP `102`).
2. **Level 2–3.5 IDMZ Conduit (`VLAN 120, PCP 4`):** The HMI forwards aggregated telemetry upstream to `idmz_historian` over an `OPCUA` binary session (TCP `4840`) and emits an RFC 5424 `SYSLOG` compliance audit message (UDP `514`).

```frameassembly
host substation_hmi { ip 172.22.10.5   mac 00:1b:21:22:0a:05 }
host bay_rtu        { ip 172.22.10.50  mac 00:a0:c9:22:0a:32 }
host s7_plc         { ip 172.22.10.60  mac 00:0e:8c:22:0a:3c }
host idmz_historian { ip 172.22.20.100 mac 00:50:56:22:14:64 }

flow substation_conduit_telemetry(hmi, rtu, plc, idmz) {
    // 1. Level 1-2 Process VLAN 110 (802.1p PCP 6): Modbus TCP register poll
    hmi -> rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 modbus read_holding_registers txid 1 unitid 1 addr 40001 count 8 wait 1ms
    hmi <- rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 modbus read_holding_registers txid 1 unitid 1 count 8 value 13800 is_response wait 2ms

    // 2. Level 1-2 Process VLAN 110: IEEE 1815 DNP3 Class 0 read & analog input response
    hmi -> rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 dnp3 read src 1 dst 10 group 60 variation 1 wait 2ms
    hmi <- rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 dnp3 func "RESPONSE" src 10 dst 1 group 30 variation 1 wait 2ms

    // 3. Level 1-2 Process VLAN 110: Siemens S7comm DB1 variable read
    hmi -> plc vlan 110 pcp 6 s7comm rosctr "JOB" read_var pdu_ref 10 area 0x84 db_num 1 offset 0 count 4 wait 2ms
    hmi <- plc vlan 110 pcp 6 s7comm rosctr "ACK_DATA" read_var pdu_ref 10 count 4 payload "DB1_OK" wait 2ms

    // 4. Level 3.5 IDMZ VLAN 120 (802.1p PCP 4): OPC UA Historian push & Syslog SIEM audit
    hmi -> idmz vlan 120 pcp 4 opcua msg_type "HEL" chunk_type "F" endpoint_url "opc.tcp://172.22.20.100:4840/historian" wait 1ms
    hmi <- idmz vlan 120 pcp 4 opcua msg_type "ACK" chunk_type "F" wait 1ms
    hmi -> idmz vlan 120 pcp 4 opcua msg_type "MSG" chunk_type "F" secure_channel_id 10 token_id 1 seq_num 1 reqid 1 node_id "ns=3;s=Feeder01.BusVoltageKV" payload "138.0" wait 2ms
    hmi -> idmz vlan 120 pcp 4 syslog facility 4 severity 5 hostname "sub-hmi-01" app "scada-poller" msg "IEC62443-Conduit: Authorized Level 1 poll & IDMZ push completed"
}

compile {
    substation_conduit_telemetry(substation_hmi, bay_rtu, s7_plc, idmz_historian)
}
```

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/fasm-specification.md`

# FrameAssembly (`.fasm`) File Format & Media Type Specification (`text/vnd.frameassembly`)

* **Canonical Media Type:** `text/vnd.frameassembly`
* **File Extension:** `.fasm`
* **Uniform Type Identifier (UTI):** `io.github.stevewinschel.frameassembly` (conforms to `public.source-code`, `public.text`)
* **Freedesktop Shared MIME Info:** [`contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`](../contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml) (`sub-class-of` `text/plain`, glob `*.fasm`) • [`contrib/mime/README.md`](../contrib/mime/README.md)
* **Unix `file(1)` / `libmagic` Rule:** [`contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic`](../contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic)
* **IANA Vendor Tree Registration Template:** [`contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md`](../contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md)
* **GitHub Linguist Grammar & Heuristics:** [`contrib/linguist/languages.yml`](../contrib/linguist/languages.yml), [`contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml`](../contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml) • [`contrib/linguist/README.md`](../contrib/linguist/README.md)
* **Formal Context-Free Grammars:** [`grammar.ebnf`](../grammar.ebnf) (ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF), [`frameassembly.gbnf`](../frameassembly.gbnf) (`llama.cpp` / `XGrammar` GBNF), [`frameassembly.lark`](../frameassembly.lark) (Earley/LALR Lark)
* **Reference Compiler & Repository:** `frameassembly` v1.4.4 • [https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly](https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly) • [crates.io/crates/frameassembly](https://crates.io/crates/frameassembly) • [docs.rs/frameassembly](https://docs.rs/frameassembly)

---

## 1. Abstract & Scope

The **FrameAssembly** file format (`.fasm`, media type `text/vnd.frameassembly`) is a declarative, human-readable Domain-Specific Language (DSL) for specifying deterministic network packet captures ("Packets as Code" / "PCAP as Code").

A `.fasm` document declares network endpoints (`HOST`), parameterized multi-packet traffic sequences (`FLOW`), and compilation targets (`COMPILE`). The `frameassembly` reference compiler translates `.fasm` source files entirely offline in unprivileged user space—requiring no root privileges (`CAP_NET_RAW`), no live network sockets, and no `libpcap` library—into deterministic, nanosecond-resolution `.pcap` / `.pcapng` packet capture files across **81 native Layer 2 through Layer 7 network protocols**.

Generated captures are designed for downstream inspection in **Wireshark** and **`tshark`**, wire-speed packet injection via **`tcpreplay`**, and automated rule validation in intrusion detection systems (**Suricata**, **Zeek**, **Snort**), firewalls, network management systems, and CI/CD pipelines.

---

## 2. Media Type & File Identification (RFC 6838 & RFC 6657)

This section defines the formal media type registration parameters for `text/vnd.frameassembly` in accordance with [RFC 6838](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6838) (Media Type Specifications and Registration Procedures) and [RFC 6657](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6657) (Update to MIME regarding "charset" Parameter Handling in Textual Media Types).

| RFC 6838 §5.6 Field | Normative Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Type name** | `text` |
| **Subtype name** | `vnd.frameassembly` |
| **Required parameters** | None. |
| **Optional parameters** | `charset`: Per RFC 6657 §3, the default charset is `UTF-8`. Implementations MUST support `UTF-8` without a Byte Order Mark (BOM). |
| **Encoding considerations** | `8bit` (UTF-8 source code). Documents containing only ASCII characters in comments and string literals are valid `7bit` US-ASCII. |
| **File extension(s)** | `.fasm` |
| **Macintosh file type code(s)** | `TEXT` |
| **Uniform Type Identifier (UTI)** | `io.github.stevewinschel.frameassembly` (`public.source-code`, `public.text`) |
| **Object Identifiers (OIDs)** | None. |
| **Fragment identifier considerations** | Supports [RFC 5147](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5147) `text/plain` character and line fragment identifiers (for example, `#line=10,25`). |
| **Published specification** | `https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/blob/main/docs/fasm-specification.md` |

---

## 3. Character Encoding, Line Endings & Binary Safety

1. **Character Encoding (`UTF-8`)**:
   - All `.fasm` files MUST be encoded in valid UTF-8 (RFC 3629).
   - All language keywords, protocol names, header modifiers, identifiers, numeric literals, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, MAC addresses, and ASN.1 Object Identifiers (OIDs) belong to the 7-bit US-ASCII character set (`0x20..0x7E`).
   - Non-ASCII UTF-8 code points MAY appear inside single-line comments (`// ...`) and double-quoted payload strings (`"..."`).
2. **Line Endings & Whitespace**:
   - The canonical line ending for `.fasm` files in version control is LF (`0x0A`, `\n`).
   - Compliant parsers MUST accept both LF (`\n`) and CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings, as well as horizontal tabs (`\t`), form feeds (`\f`), and spaces (`0x20`) as token delimiters (`[ \t\r\n\f]+`).
3. **Prohibition of Literal NUL Bytes (`0x00`)**:
   - A valid `.fasm` file MUST NOT contain literal NUL bytes (`0x00`).
   - Arbitrary binary wire payloads (including NUL bytes) are represented safely in `.fasm` source code using hexadecimal escape sequences inside `PAYLOAD "<string>"` (such as `\x00\x09\x01`) or hexadecimal byte strings inside `HEXPAYLOAD "<hex>"` (such as `HEXPAYLOAD "000102ff"`).

---

## 4. Document Structure & Lexical Grammar

### 4.1 Comments & Case-Insensitivity

- **Single-Line Comments**: Comments begin with `//` and extend to the end of the line. Neither `#` nor `/* ... */` are valid comment delimiters in `.fasm`.
- **ASCII Case-Insensitivity**: All structural keywords (`HOST`, `FLOW`, `COMPILE`, `LOOP`), all 81 protocol keywords, all Layer 2–Layer 7 modifiers, all time unit suffixes (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`), and all user-defined host, flow, and parameter identifiers are ASCII case-insensitive (`host` and `HOST` are identical). String literals (`"..."`) preserve exact case on the wire.

### 4.2 Three-Block Program Model

Every compilable `.fasm` specification consists of three top-level block types:

1. **Endpoint Declarations (`HOST`)**:
   ```text
   HOST <identifier> {
       IP <ipv4-or-ipv6-address>
       [MAC <mac-address>]
   }
   ```
   - `IP`: Standard IPv4 dotted-quad (`10.0.0.1`) or IPv6 address (`2001:db8::1`, `fe80::1`, `ff02::fb`).
   - `MAC` *(optional)*: 48-bit Ethernet MAC address in IEEE colon notation (`00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e`), hyphen notation (`00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E`), or Cisco dotted-quad notation (`001a.2b3c.4d5e`). When omitted, FrameAssembly derives a deterministic unicast MAC or the standard multicast MAC per RFC 1112 (`01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx` for IPv4 `224.0.0.0/4`) and RFC 2464 (`33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx` for IPv6 `ff00::/8`).

2. **Parameterized Traffic Flows (`FLOW`)**:
   ```text
   FLOW <identifier>(<param1>, <param2>, ...) {
       <endpoint_a> -> <endpoint_b> [modifiers...] <PROTOCOL> [protocol_fields...] [WAIT <duration>]
       <endpoint_a> <- <endpoint_b> [modifiers...] <PROTOCOL> [protocol_fields...] [WAIT <duration>]
   }
   ```
   - **1 Statement = 1 Frame**: Each statement inside a `FLOW` block emits exactly one Ethernet frame.
   - **Directional Arrows**: `a -> b` transmits from `a` (source) to `b` (destination); `a <- b` transmits from `b` (source) back to `a` (destination), automatically reversing source and destination ports on reply packets.
   - **Shared 4-Tuple TCP State**: TCP-based Layer 7 statements automatically emit a `PSH ACK` segment on that protocol's default port and share sequence (`SEQ`) and acknowledgment (`ACKNUM`) counters with raw `TCP` statements on the same 4-tuple connection.
   - **Dual-Stack Polymorphism**: A `FLOW` definition is protocol-version agnostic and executes over both IPv4 host pairs and IPv6 host pairs. Mixing an IPv4 endpoint and an IPv6 endpoint in the same statement is rejected at semantic validation time.

3. **Compilation & Loop Execution (`COMPILE`)**:
   ```text
   COMPILE {
       <flow_identifier>(<host1>, <host2>, ...)
       LOOP <positive_integer> {
           <flow_identifier>(<host1>, <host2>, ...)
       }
   }
   ```
   - Exactly one `COMPILE` block defines the ordered sequence of flow invocations and bounded `LOOP` repetitions written to the output capture.

### 4.3 Lexical Token Classes

The reference lexer (`src/lexer/mod.rs`) partitions input text into the following token classes:

| Token Class | Lexical Pattern / Rule | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Structural Keywords** | `HOST`, `IP`, `MAC`, `FLOW`, `COMPILE`, `LOOP`, `WAIT` (ASCII case-insensitive) | `HOST`, `flow`, `Compile`, `WAIT` |
| **Directional Operators** | `->` (forward frame), `<-` (reverse frame) | `client -> server`, `client <- server` |
| **Delimiters** | `{`, `}`, `(`, `)`, `,` | `FLOW web(c, s) { ... }` |
| **Time Unit Suffixes** | `ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m` (attached to or following `WAIT <int>`) | `WAIT 500ns`, `WAIT 10ms`, `WAIT 2s` |
| **MAC Address Literal** | `([0-9a-fA-F]{2}:){5}[0-9a-fA-F]{2}` \| `([0-9a-fA-F]{2}-){5}[0-9a-fA-F]{2}` \| `[0-9a-fA-F]{4}\.[0-9a-fA-F]{4}\.[0-9a-fA-F]{4}` | `00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e`, `00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E`, `001a.2b3c.4d5e` |
| **IPv4 / IPv6 Literal** | `[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+` \| `::[0-9a-fA-F:.]*\|[0-9a-fA-F]{1,4}(:[0-9a-fA-F:.]*)+` | `192.168.1.10`, `2001:db8::1`, `ff02::1:ff00:1` |
| **Numeric Literal** | `-?[0-9]+\|0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+` | `443`, `0x88cc`, `65535` |
| **ASN.1 OID Literal** | `\.?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*` (3 or more arcs for OID context) | `1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0`, `1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3` |
| **String Literal** | `"([^"\\]\|\\.)*"` (supports `\"`, `\\`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\xHH`) | `"example.com"`, `"AMQP\x00\x00\x09\x01"` |
| **Identifier** | `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*` | `core_switch`, `web_session`, `client_v6` |

### 4.4 Complete 81 Native Protocol Keywords

Every protocol keyword below compiles with zero mandatory sub-keywords (emitting RFC-compliant default headers and ports) and accepts protocol-specific field overrides:

| OSI Layer | Count | Canonical `.fasm` Protocol Keywords |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Layer 2 (Switching & Data-Link)** | 8 | `ARP`, `VLAN`, `QINQ`, `LLDP`, `STP`, `LACP`, `EAPOL`, `MPLS` |
| **Layer 3 (Control, Tunnel, VPN, Routing)** | 20 | `ICMP`, `NDP`, `IGMP`, `MLD`, `GRE`, `VXLAN`, `GENEVE`, `IPSEC`, `ESP`, `AH`, `IKEV2`, `WIREGUARD`, `OSPF`, `BGP`, `RIP`, `VRRP`, `HSRP`, `PIM`, `BFD`, `OPENFLOW` |
| **Layer 4 (Transport)** | 3 | `TCP`, `UDP`, `SCTP` |
| **Layer 7 (SNMP, Infra, Time, AAA, Telemetry)** | 14 | `SNMP1`, `SNMP2`, `SNMP3`, `DNS`, `MDNS`, `DHCP`, `NTP`, `PTP`, `RADIUS`, `TACACS`, `SYSLOG`, `NETFLOW`, `IPFIX`, `SFLOW` |
| **Layer 7 (Web, Security, VoIP, Access)** | 16 | `HTTP`, `HTTP2`, `GRPC`, `WEBSOCKET`, `TLS`, `QUIC`, `TFTP`, `FTP`, `SSH`, `TELNET`, `WHOIS`, `SIP`, `RTP`, `RTSP`, `STUN`, `SSDP` |
| **Layer 7 (Mail, Auth, Storage, DB, Brokers)** | 14 | `SMTP`, `IMAP`, `POP3`, `KERBEROS`, `LDAP`, `SMB`, `NFS`, `REDIS`, `MEMCACHED`, `MYSQL`, `POSTGRES`, `MQTT`, `COAP`, `AMQP` |
| **Layer 7 (Industrial ICS / SCADA / OT)** | 6 | `MODBUS`, `BACNET`, `DNP3`, `S7COMM`, `ETHERNETIP`, `OPCUA` |

---

## 5. Lexical Magic, Content Sniffing & `.fasm` Extension Disambiguation

### 5.1 Authoritative Three-Way Format Disambiguation

The `.fasm` file extension is historically associated with three completely distinct formats across software engineering, compiler design, and hardware synthesis. Because neither Flat Assembler nor FPGA FASM has registered a formal media type with IANA or Freedesktop.org, naive extension-only associations can cause misclassification.

The table below provides the authoritative technical disambiguation across all eleven architectural dimensions:

| Architectural Dimension | **FrameAssembly (`.fasm`)** | **Flat Assembler x86 (`.asm`, `.fasm`)** | **FPGA Bitstream Assembly (`FASM`, `.fasm`)** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Domain** | Declarative network packet capture specification ("Packets as Code" / "PCAP as Code") | Low-level x86 / x86-64 machine assembly language | FPGA hardware tile and interconnect feature configuration (SymbiFlow / F4PGA) |
| **Canonical Media Type** | `text/vnd.frameassembly` (RFC 6838 Vendor Tree candidate) | Unregistered (`text/x-asm`) | Unregistered (`text/plain`) |
| **Comment Delimiters** | `// single-line comment` (C/C++/Rust style) | `; single-line comment` (standard assembly style) | `# single-line comment` (Python/Tcl/sh style) |
| **Top-Level Block Syntax** | `HOST <id> { IP ... }`<br>`FLOW <id>(...) { ... }`<br>`COMPILE { ... }` | Directives: `format PE/ELF`, `section '.text'`, `segment`, `org`, `use32`/`use64` | Hierarchical dot-separated hardware tile paths: `CLBLL_L_X10Y100.SLICEL_X0...` |
| **Statement Syntax & Operators** | Directional arrows `->` and `<-` paired with Layer 2–7 protocol keywords (`TCP`, `HTTP`, `SNMP3`) | x86 CPU mnemonics: `mov`, `eax`, `xor`, `call`, `int 80h`, `push`, `pop`, `db`, `dd` | Bit-slice assignments (`ALUT.INIT[63:0] = 64'h...`) or bare feature strings |
| **Target Output Artifact** | Deterministic `.pcap` / `.pcapng` packet capture file | Native machine code binary (`.bin`, `.obj`, `.o`, `.exe`, `.elf`) | FPGA configuration bitstream (`.bit`, `.frames`) |
| **Reference Tool / Compiler** | `frameassembly` compiler & CLI (offline userspace, rootless, zero raw sockets) | Flat Assembler (`fasm`) assembler & linker | `fasm2frames` / `xc7frames2bit` (SymbiFlow / F4PGA architecture tooling) |
| **Downstream Consumers** | **Wireshark**, **`tshark`**, **`tcpreplay`**, **Suricata**, **Zeek**, Snort, test harnesses | Operating system loader, CPU execution, static linkers (`ld`, `link.exe`) | Xilinx 7-Series / Lattice iCE40 FPGA programming hardware |
| **Registry Authority** | Candidate IANA Vendor Tree (`text/vnd.frameassembly`), Freedesktop XML, Wikidata | Unregistered informal convention (`.asm` primary, `.fasm` secondary) | Unregistered informal convention (`.fasm` tile configuration) |
| **Text Encoding & Line Endings** | UTF-8 without BOM (RFC 6657), LF / CRLF accepted, literal NUL (`0x00`) prohibited | ASCII or regional 8-bit code pages, CR+LF or LF | US-ASCII, LF or CRLF |
| **Syntax Highlighting Scopes** | `source.frameassembly` (TextMate), `FrameAssembly` (Linguist) | `source.assembly` or `source.x86` | Generic text or hardware configuration |

### 5.2 Explicit Syntactic Distinguishing Marks & Zero False-Positive Proof

Because each format operates in a distinct technological problem domain, their lexical token sets and grammars are strictly disjoint:

1. **Comment Syntax Discrimination**:
   - FrameAssembly exclusively accepts single-line comments introduced by `//`. Semicolons (`;`) and hash marks (`#`) are lexical errors outside quoted strings.
   - Flat Assembler exclusively uses semicolons (`;`) for comments.
   - FPGA FASM exclusively uses hash characters (`#`) for comments.
2. **Top-Level Structural Blocks**:
   - Every compilable FrameAssembly file contains mandatory structural keywords: `HOST`, `FLOW`, and `COMPILE`.
   - Flat Assembler source files never declare `HOST`, `FLOW`, or `COMPILE`; they declare `format`, `section`, `segment`, `org`, or raw assembly labels.
   - FPGA FASM files never declare blocks or braces; they consist of newline-separated feature lines with dot-separated tile identifiers.
3. **Directional Flow Statements vs Machine Mnemonics vs Tile Paths**:
   - FrameAssembly packet statements always utilize directional operators (`client -> server` or `client <- server`) followed by OSI layer protocol tokens (`TCP`, `UDP`, `VLAN`, `HTTP`, `SNMP3`).
   - Flat Assembler statements consist of x86 opcodes and registers (`mov eax, 1`).
   - FPGA FASM statements consist of tile coordinates and bit-slices (`HCLK_L_X0Y130.ENABLE_BUFFER`).

### 5.3 Deterministic Content-Sniffing & Linguist Heuristics

GitHub Linguist, `bat`, `Chroma`, and Pygments identify FrameAssembly `.fasm` documents with zero false positives using the regular expression heuristics published in [`contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml`](../contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml):

- **Positive FrameAssembly Anchors**:
  - `(?i)^\s*HOST\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\{\s*(?:IP|MAC)\b`
  - `(?i)^\s*FLOW\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\([A-Za-z0-9_,\s]*\)\s*\{`
  - `(?i)^\s*COMPILE\s*\{\s*(?:LOOP\s+[0-9]+\s*\{|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\()`
  - Directional packet statement: `(?i)\b[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*(?:->|<-)\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s+(?:...protocol tokens...)\b`
- **Negative / Competing Format Anchors**:
  - Flat Assembler: `(?i)^\s*(?:format\s+(?:PE|PE64|ELF|ELF64|MZ|COFF|binary)|section\b|segment\b|use16\b|use32\b|use64\b|org\b)` or lines beginning with `;`.
  - FPGA FASM: Lines beginning with `#` or matching tile patterns `^[A-Z0-9_]+(?:\.[A-Z0-9_]+){2,}`.

### 5.4 Freedesktop `shared-mime-info` Magic Signatures & Desktop Integration

The Freedesktop MIME package in [`contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`](../contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml) (documentation in [`contrib/mime/README.md`](../contrib/mime/README.md)) registers `text/vnd.frameassembly` as a subclass of `text/plain` with glob `*.fasm` (`weight="60"`) and `<magic priority="60">` rules matching:
- `HOST ` / `HOST\t` / `host ` / `host\t` within bytes `0..1024` AND `IP ` / `ip ` within bytes `0..1536` AND `COMPILE` / `compile` within bytes `0..8192`, or
- `FLOW ` / `flow ` within bytes `0..2048` AND `COMPILE` / `compile` within bytes `0..8192`.

Priority `60` ensures that FrameAssembly specifications take precedence over generic text handlers on Linux and BSD desktops while preventing collisions with Flat Assembler and FPGA FASM.

### 5.5 Unix `file(1)` / `libmagic` Content Sniffing

Unix systems and command-line utilities using `libmagic` identify FrameAssembly `.fasm` files via [`contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic`](../contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic):

```magic
0	search/2048/cC	HOST
>0	search/1024/cC	IP
>>0	search/4096/cC	FLOW
>>>0	search/8192/cC	COMPILE	FrameAssembly network packet specification
!:mime	text/vnd.frameassembly
!:ext	fasm

0	search/2048/cC	FLOW
>0	search/4096/cC	HOST
>>0	search/1024/cC	IP
>>>0	search/8192/cC	COMPILE	FrameAssembly network packet specification
!:mime	text/vnd.frameassembly
!:ext	fasm
```

Running `file -i <file.fasm>` returns `text/vnd.frameassembly; charset=us-ascii` or `utf-8`.

### 5.6 FAQ: What is a `.fasm` File? (FrameAssembly vs. Flat Assembler vs. FPGA FASM)

#### Q1: What is a `.fasm` file in FrameAssembly?
A `.fasm` file is a declarative network traffic specification written in the FrameAssembly Domain-Specific Language ("Packets as Code"). It defines network endpoints (`HOST`), directional packet exchanges across OSI Layers 2 through 7 (`FLOW`), and execution schedules (`COMPILE`). The `frameassembly` compiler compiles `.fasm` specifications offline into deterministic `.pcap` or `.pcapng` capture files for Wireshark, `tshark`, `tcpreplay`, Suricata, and Zeek.

#### Q2: How does a FrameAssembly `.fasm` file differ from an x86 Flat Assembler file?
Flat Assembler (traditionally abbreviated FASM) is a machine-code assembler that translates low-level x86/x86-64 assembly instructions into binary executables (`.exe`, `.elf`, `.bin`). Flat Assembler files use semicolon (`;`) comments, format directives (`format PE`, `section '.text'`), and CPU mnemonics (`mov`, `jmp`, `xor`). In contrast, FrameAssembly files use slash (`//`) comments, structural blocks (`HOST`, `FLOW`, `COMPILE`), and networking directives (`client -> server TCP SYN`).

#### Q3: How does a FrameAssembly `.fasm` file differ from an FPGA FASM file?
In open-source FPGA toolchains (SymbiFlow / F4PGA), FASM stands for FPGA Assembly. It describes low-level FPGA configuration bitstreams using hash (`#`) comments and dot-separated hardware tile feature paths (such as `CLBLL_L_X10Y100.SLICEL_X0.ALUT.INIT[63:0]`). It has no network endpoints, protocols, or flow logic.

#### Q4: How do tools, operating systems, and code editors disambiguate `.fasm` files?
Multi-tier content sniffing eliminates false positive collisions:
1. **GitHub**: `.gitattributes` (`linguist-language=FrameAssembly`) and Linguist `heuristics.yml` detect `HOST`, `FLOW`, `COMPILE`, and directional arrows (`->` and `<-`).
2. **Linux & BSD Desktops**: Freedesktop `shared-mime-info` (`contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`) and `libmagic` (`contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic`) inspect file bytes for `HOST ... IP ... FLOW ... COMPILE` magic tokens, reporting `text/vnd.frameassembly`.
3. **VS Code & IDEs**: The FrameAssembly extension registers the `source.frameassembly` TextMate scope and `text/vnd.frameassembly` MIME type.

#### Q5: Can I compile an x86 Flat Assembler or FPGA FASM file with the `frameassembly` compiler?
No. FrameAssembly is specifically a network packet capture compiler. If you accidentally pass an x86 Flat Assembler or FPGA FASM file to `frameassembly`, the parser immediately recognizes foreign syntax (such as `;` or `#` comments, `format PE`, or tile paths) and displays a plain-English remediation error explaining that FrameAssembly `.fasm` specifications require `HOST`, `FLOW`, and `COMPILE` blocks.

### 5.7 Registry Status Across Standards Bodies & Public Databases

The `.fasm` file extension and `text/vnd.frameassembly` media type maintain active registration entries and assets across all major registries:

1. **IANA Media Type Registry**: RFC 6838 Vendor Tree candidate registration application in [`contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md`](../contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md).
2. **Freedesktop `shared-mime-info`**: XML package definition in [`contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml`](../contrib/mime/text-vnd.frameassembly.xml) and upstream merge request guide in [`contrib/mime/README.md`](../contrib/mime/README.md).
3. **Unix `file(1)` / `libmagic`**: Magic rule definition in [`contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic`](../contrib/magic/frameassembly.magic).
4. **GitHub Linguist**: Language definition in [`contrib/linguist/languages.yml`](../contrib/linguist/languages.yml), disambiguation heuristics in [`contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml`](../contrib/linguist/heuristics.yml), TextMate grammar in [`frameassembly-vscode/syntaxes/frameassembly.tmLanguage.json`](../frameassembly-vscode/syntaxes/frameassembly.tmLanguage.json), and upstream PR guide in [`contrib/linguist/README.md`](../contrib/linguist/README.md).

6. **Public File Extension Databases, Preservation & Web Ecosystem**: Submission templates for `file-extensions.org`, `FileInfo.com`, `FILExt.com`, UK National Archives PRONOM (`digital-preservation/PRONOM_Research`), and Node.js `jshttp/mime-db` in [`contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md`](../contrib/iana/text-vnd.frameassembly.md).

## 6. Security Considerations (RFC 6838 §4.6 & RFC 3552)

1. **Declarative, Non-Executable Format**:
   - A `.fasm` file is a passive, declarative data specification describing network endpoints and packet header fields. It contains no executable code, macros, shell invocations, or system calls.
2. **Bounded, Side-Effect-Free Compilation**:
   - The `frameassembly` language is intentionally non-Turing-complete: there is no unbounded recursion, dynamic memory allocation expression, or conditional branching. `LOOP <count> { ... }` blocks require a compile-time positive integer literal.
   - The language includes no file-inclusion directives (`include` or `import`) and performs no network I/O or DNS resolution during compilation, eliminating Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and local file inclusion vectors when compiling untrusted `.fasm` inputs.
   - The compiler executes entirely in unprivileged user space without `CAP_NET_RAW`, raw sockets, or external C packet libraries (`libpcap`).
3. **Downstream Packet Capture Considerations**:
   - Compiling a `.fasm` specification produces a passive `.pcap` / `.pcapng` packet capture file.
   - Because FrameAssembly is designed for firewall, IDS/IPS (**Suricata**, **Zeek**, **Snort**), and protocol dissector (**Wireshark** / `tshark`) testing, generated `.pcap` files may intentionally contain malformed header combinations, fragmentation overlaps (`MF` + `FRAGOFFSET`), out-of-window TCP sequence numbers, or intrusion-detection test signatures.
   - Replaying a generated `.pcap` file onto a live network interface requires explicit administrator invocation of an external replay tool (such as `tcpreplay`) with host network privileges.

## 8. Validated `.fasm` Specification Examples

Every example below is a complete, standards-compliant `text/vnd.frameassembly` document verified by the `frameassembly` compiler.

### Example 1: Stateful TCP Handshake, HTTP/1.1 Transaction & Encrypted SNMPv3 USM Trap

```frameassembly
// Define IPv4 network endpoints
HOST web_client { IP 10.10.1.10 MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:10 }
HOST app_server { IP 10.10.1.80 MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:80 }
HOST nms_collector { IP 10.10.1.250 MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:fa }

// Stateful HTTP health check followed by an RFC 7860 SNMPv3 SHA-256 + AES-128 trap
FLOW service_check_and_alert(client, srv, nms) {
    client -> srv TCP SYN SRCPORT 51400 DSTPORT 80 WIN 65535 MSS 1460 WAIT 1ms
    client <- srv TCP SYN ACK WIN 65535 MSS 1460 WAIT 1ms
    client -> srv TCP ACK WAIT 1ms
    client -> srv HTTP GET URI "/healthz" HOST_HDR "app.internal" WAIT 4ms
    client <- srv HTTP STATUS 200 REASON "OK" BODY "{\"status\":\"healthy\"}" WAIT 2ms
    srv -> nms VLAN 100 SNMP3 TRAP USER "secops" ENGINEID "80001f888001020304" ENGINEBOOTS 3 ENGINETIME 1200 AUTH SHA256 "AuthSecret2026!" PRIV AES "PrivSecret2026!" OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "app-srv-01" WAIT 5ms
}

COMPILE {
    service_check_and_alert(web_client, app_server, nms_collector)
}
```

### Example 2: Dual-Stack IPv4/IPv6 Flow Reuse with Carrier 802.1ad QinQ & MPLS Tagging

```frameassembly
// IPv4 and IPv6 endpoint pairs
HOST edge_v4 { IP 172.16.10.1 MAC 00-50-56-C0-00-01 }
HOST core_v4 { IP 172.16.10.2 MAC 00-50-56-C0-00-02 }
HOST edge_v6 { IP 2001:db8:10::1 MAC 0050.56c0.0011 }
HOST core_v6 { IP 2001:db8:10::2 MAC 0050.56c0.0012 }

// Reusable TLS 1.3 handshake over 802.1ad QinQ (S-VLAN 2000 / C-VLAN 100) and MPLS label 32000
FLOW carrier_tls_probe(pe_a, pe_b) {
    pe_a -> pe_b QINQ 2000 INNER_VLAN 100 PCP 5 MPLS 32000 EXP 5 BOS 1 MPLS_TTL 64 DSCP 46 TTL 64 TLS CLIENT_HELLO SNI "api.carrier.example" CIPHERSUITE 4865 ALPN "h2" WAIT 2ms
    pe_a <- pe_b QINQ 2000 INNER_VLAN 100 PCP 5 MPLS 32000 EXP 5 BOS 1 MPLS_TTL 63 DSCP 46 TTL 63 TLS SERVER_HELLO CIPHERSUITE 4865 ALPN "h2" WAIT 2ms
}

COMPILE {
    carrier_tls_probe(edge_v4, core_v4)
    carrier_tls_probe(edge_v6, core_v6)
}
```

### Example 3: Industrial OT / SCADA Modbus TCP & IEEE 1815 DNP3 Conduit Verification

```frameassembly
HOST scada_master { IP 192.168.50.10 MAC 00:1b:21:50:00:10 }
HOST substation_rtu { IP 192.168.50.20 MAC 00:0e:8c:50:00:20 }

FLOW substation_poll(master, rtu) {
    master -> rtu VLAN 50 MODBUS READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS TXID 10 UNITID 1 ADDR 40001 COUNT 4 WAIT 2ms
    master <- rtu VLAN 50 MODBUS READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS TXID 10 UNITID 1 COUNT 4 VALUE 1200 IS_RESPONSE WAIT 2ms
    master -> rtu VLAN 50 DNP3 READ SRC 1 DST 10 SEQ 1 GROUP 60 VARIATION 1 WAIT 5ms
}

COMPILE {
    substation_poll(scada_master, substation_rtu)
}
```
