```gbnf
# 12. Lexical Terminals
str-or-ident ::= string-lit | ident
ident ::= [a-zA-Z_] [a-zA-Z0-9_]*
uint-lit ::= [0-9]+ | "0" [xX] [0-9a-fA-F]+
int-lit ::= "-"? [0-9]+ | "0" [xX] [0-9a-fA-F]+
duration-lit ::= uint-lit ("ns" | "us" | "ms" | "s" | "m")
string-lit ::= "\"" ([^"\\] | "\\" (["\\/bfnrt'] | "x" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} | "u" [0-9a-fA-F]{4}))* "\""
hex-string-lit ::= "\"" [0-9a-fA-F: ]* "\""
mac-addr ::= ([0-9a-fA-F]{2} ":" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} ":" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} ":" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} ":" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} ":" [0-9a-fA-F]{2}) | ([0-9a-fA-F]{2} "-" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} "-" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} "-" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} "-" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} "-" [0-9a-fA-F]{2}) | ([0-9a-fA-F]{4} "." [0-9a-fA-F]{4} "." [0-9a-fA-F]{4})
ip-addr ::= ipv4-addr | ipv6-addr
ipv4-addr ::= [0-9]+ "." [0-9]+ "." [0-9]+ "." [0-9]+
ipv6-addr ::= "::" [0-9a-fA-F:.]* | [0-9a-fA-F]{1,4} (":" [0-9a-fA-F:.]*)+
oid-lit ::= "."? [0-9]+ ("." [0-9]+)* | string-lit
```

---

# Formal Lark Earley/LALR Constrained Decoding Grammar (`frameassembly.lark`)

```lark
// ============================================================================
// FrameAssembly Lark Grammar (Outlines / vLLM / Guidance / XGrammar / llguidance)
// Synchronized with src/lexer/mod.rs, grammar.ebnf, and frameassembly.gbnf.
// Covers all 81 native protocols, L2-L4 modifiers, SNMPv1/v2c/v3 USM, and L7.
// Note: The FrameAssembly compiler accepts all keywords, protocols, modifiers,
// time units, and identifiers case-insensitively; canonical uppercase tokens
// are used here for deterministic LLM constrained decoding.
// ============================================================================

start: top_level_decl* compile_block top_level_decl*

top_level_decl: host_decl
              | flow_decl

// 1. Host Declarations
host_decl: "HOST" IDENT "{" host_prop* "}"
host_prop: "IP" ip_addr
         | "MAC" MAC_ADDR

// 2. Flow Declarations & Statements
flow_decl: "FLOW" IDENT "(" param_list? ")" "{" frame_stmt* "}"
param_list: IDENT ("," IDENT)*

frame_stmt: IDENT direction IDENT frame_field*
direction: "->" | "<-"

// 3. Compile Block & Loops
compile_block: "COMPILE" "{" run_stmt* "}"
run_stmt: loop_block
        | flow_call
loop_block: "LOOP" UINT_LIT "{" flow_call* "}"
flow_call: IDENT "(" param_list? ")"

// 4. Frame Fields (Protocols, Modifiers & Protocol Attributes)
frame_field: protocol_kw
           | universal_mod
           | l2_mod
           | l3_mod
           | l4_mod
           | l2_proto_field
           | l3_proto_field
           | l4_proto_field
           | snmp_proto_field
           | l7_proto_field

// 5. All 81 Native Protocol Keywords
protocol_kw: l2_proto
           | l3_proto
           | l4_proto
           | snmp_proto
           | l7_infra_proto
           | l7_app_proto
           | l7_ot_proto

l2_proto: "ARP" | "VLAN" | "QINQ" | "LLDP" | "STP" | "LACP" | "EAPOL" | "MPLS"

l3_proto: "ICMP" | "NDP" | "IGMP" | "MLD" | "GRE" | "VXLAN" | "GENEVE"
        | "IPSEC" | "ESP" | "AH" | "IKEV2" | "WIREGUARD"
        | "OSPF" | "BGP" | "RIP" | "VRRP" | "HSRP" | "PIM" | "BFD" | "OPENFLOW"

l4_proto: "TCP" | "UDP" | "SCTP"

snmp_proto: "SNMP1" | "SNMP2" | "SNMP3"

l7_infra_proto: "DNS" | "MDNS" | "DHCP" | "NTP" | "PTP" | "RADIUS"
              | "TACACS" | "SYSLOG" | "NETFLOW" | "IPFIX" | "SFLOW"

l7_app_proto: "TFTP" | "FTP" | "SSH" | "TELNET" | "HTTP" | "HTTP2" | "GRPC"
            | "WEBSOCKET" | "TLS" | "QUIC" | "STUN" | "SIP" | "RTP" | "RTSP"
            | "SMTP" | "IMAP" | "POP3" | "KERBEROS" | "LDAP" | "SMB" | "NFS"
            | "REDIS" | "MEMCACHED" | "MYSQL" | "POSTGRES" | "MQTT" | "COAP"
            | "AMQP" | "SSDP" | "WHOIS"

l7_ot_proto: "MODBUS" | "BACNET" | "DNP3" | "S7COMM" | "ETHERNETIP" | "OPCUA"

// 6. Universal & Layer 2-4 Modifiers
universal_mod: "WAIT" DURATION_LIT
             | "PAYLOAD" STRING_LIT
             | "HEXPAYLOAD" HEX_STRING_LIT

l2_mod: "SRCMAC" MAC_ADDR
      | "DSTMAC" MAC_ADDR
      | "ETHERTYPE" UINT_LIT
      | "VLAN" UINT_LIT?
      | "PCP" UINT_LIT
      | "DEI" UINT_LIT
      | "QINQ" UINT_LIT?
      | "INNER_VLAN" UINT_LIT
      | "MPLS" UINT_LIT?
      | "LABEL" UINT_LIT
      | ("EXP" | "TC") UINT_LIT
      | "BOS" UINT_LIT
      | "MPLS_TTL" UINT_LIT

l3_mod: "TTL" UINT_LIT
      | "DSCP" UINT_LIT
      | "ECN" UINT_LIT
      | "FLOWLABEL" UINT_LIT
      | "IPID" UINT_LIT
      | "DF"
      | "MF"
      | "FRAGOFFSET" UINT_LIT
      | "NEXT_HEADER" UINT_LIT

l4_mod: "SRCPORT" UINT_LIT
      | "DSTPORT" UINT_LIT
      | "TRANSPORT" ("TCP" | "UDP")
      | tcp_flag
      | "SEQ" UINT_LIT
      | "ACKNUM" UINT_LIT
      | ("WIN" | "WINDOW") UINT_LIT
      | "URGENT" UINT_LIT
      | "MSS" UINT_LIT
      | "WSCALE" UINT_LIT
      | "SACK_PERM" | "SACKPERM"
      | "TSVAL" UINT_LIT
      | "TSECR" UINT_LIT

tcp_flag: "SYN" | "ACK" | "FIN" | "RST" | "PSH" | "URG" | "ECE" | "CWR"

// 7. Layer 2 Protocol Sub-Keywords
l2_proto_field: "REQUEST"
              | "REPLY" STRING_LIT?
              | "GRATUITOUS" | "GARP"
              | ("SHA" | "SENDERMAC") MAC_ADDR
              | ("SPA" | "SENDERIP") ip_addr
              | ("THA" | "TARGETMAC") MAC_ADDR
              | ("TPA" | "TARGETIP") ip_addr
              | "CHASSIS_ID" str_or_ident
              | "PORT_ID" (UINT_LIT | str_or_ident)
              | "SYSNAME" str_or_ident
              | "SYSDESC" str_or_ident
              | "ROOT_ID" str_or_ident
              | "BRIDGE_ID" str_or_ident
              | "COST" UINT_LIT
              | "MAX_AGE" UINT_LIT
              | "HELLO_TIME" UINT_LIT
              | "FORWARD_DELAY" UINT_LIT
              | "RSTP"
              | "FLAGS" UINT_LIT
              | "ACTOR_SYS" (MAC_ADDR | STRING_LIT)
              | "ACTOR_KEY" UINT_LIT
              | "ACTOR_PORT" UINT_LIT
              | "PARTNER_SYS" (MAC_ADDR | STRING_LIT)
              | "PARTNER_KEY" UINT_LIT
              | "PARTNER_PORT" UINT_LIT
              | "ACTOR_STATE" UINT_LIT
              | "PARTNER_STATE" UINT_LIT
              | "VERSION" (UINT_LIT | str_or_ident)
              | "TYPE" (UINT_LIT | "START" | "LOGOFF" | "KEY" | "EAP_PACKET" | "INITIATION" | "RESPONSE" | "COOKIE" | "DATA"
              | "HELLO" | "FEATURES_REQ" | "FEATURES_REPLY" | "PACKET_IN" | "PACKET_OUT" | "FLOW_MOD" | "ECHO_REQ" | "ECHO_REQUEST" | "ECHO_REPLY"
              | "AUTHEN" | "AUTHOR" | "ACCT" | str_or_ident)
              | "START" | "LOGOFF" | "KEY" | "EAP_PACKET"
              | "EAP_CODE" UINT_LIT
              | "EAP_ID" UINT_LIT
              | "EAP_METHOD" UINT_LIT
              | "IDENTITY" str_or_ident

// 8. Layer 3 Protocol Sub-Keywords
l3_proto_field: "ECHO_REQUEST" | "ECHO_REPLY" | "DEST_UNREACH" | "TIME_EXCEEDED" | "REDIRECT"
              | "CODE" (UINT_LIT | str_or_ident)
              | "ID" UINT_LIT
              | "GATEWAY" ip_addr
              | "ROUTER_SOLICIT" | "ROUTER_ADVERT" | "NEIGHBOR_SOLICIT" | "NEIGHBOR_ADVERT"
              | "TARGET" (ip_addr | MAC_ADDR)
              | "SLLA" MAC_ADDR
              | "TLLA" MAC_ADDR
              | "ROUTER_LIFETIME" UINT_LIT
              | "QUERY" | "REPORT" | "LEAVE" | "DONE" | "V1" | "V2" | "V3"
              | "GROUP" (ip_addr | UINT_LIT)
              | "MAX_RESP" UINT_LIT
              | "MULTICAST_ADDR" ip_addr
              | "MAX_RESP_DELAY" UINT_LIT
              | "CHECKSUM"
              | "GRE_KEY" UINT_LIT
              | "GRE_SEQ" UINT_LIT
              | "GRE_PROTO" UINT_LIT
              | ("VNI" | "VNID") UINT_LIT
              | "OPT_CLASS" UINT_LIT
              | "OPT_TYPE" UINT_LIT
              | "PROTOCOL_TYPE" UINT_LIT
              | "SPI" UINT_LIT
              | "IV" (HEX_STRING_LIT | UINT_LIT)
              | "ICV" (HEX_STRING_LIT | UINT_LIT)
              | "INITIATOR_SPI" (UINT_LIT | HEX_STRING_LIT)
              | "RESPONDER_SPI" (UINT_LIT | HEX_STRING_LIT)
              | "EXCHANGE" (UINT_LIT | "SA_INIT" | "CREATE_CHILD_SA" | "INFORMATIONAL" | str_or_ident)
              | "SA_INIT" | "CREATE_CHILD_SA" | "INFORMATIONAL"
              | "MSGID" (UINT_LIT | str_or_ident)
              | "NEXT_PAYLOAD" UINT_LIT
              | "INITIATION" | "COOKIE" str_or_ident? | "DATA" str_or_ident?
              | "SENDER" UINT_LIT
              | "RECEIVER" UINT_LIT
              | "COUNTER" UINT_LIT
              | "HELLO" | "DBD" | "LSR" | "LSU" | "LSACK"
              | "ROUTER_ID" ip_addr
              | "AREA_ID" (UINT_LIT | ip_addr)
              | "HELLO_INTERVAL" UINT_LIT
              | "DEAD_INTERVAL" UINT_LIT
              | "PRIORITY" UINT_LIT
              | "OPEN" | "UPDATE" | "NOTIFICATION" | "KEEPALIVE" UINT_LIT?
              | "ASN" UINT_LIT
              | "HOLDTIME" UINT_LIT
              | "BGPID" ip_addr
              | ("PREFIX" | "NLRI") (ip_addr | str_or_ident)
              | "NEXTHOP" ip_addr
              | "COMMAND" (UINT_LIT | str_or_ident)
              | "METRIC" UINT_LIT
              | "TAG" (UINT_LIT | str_or_ident)
              | "VRID" UINT_LIT
              | "ADV_INT" UINT_LIT
              | "VIP" ip_addr
              | "HELLOTIME" UINT_LIT
              | "STATE" UINT_LIT
              | "JOIN_PRUNE" | "REGISTER"
              | "SOURCE" ip_addr
              | "RP" ip_addr
              | "DR_PRIORITY" UINT_LIT
              | "DIAG" UINT_LIT
              | "MY_DISC" UINT_LIT
              | "YOUR_DISC" UINT_LIT
              | "MIN_TX" UINT_LIT
              | "MIN_RX" UINT_LIT
              | "MULT" UINT_LIT
              | "FEATURES_REQ" | "FEATURES_REPLY" | "PACKET_IN" | "PACKET_OUT" | "FLOW_MOD" | "ECHO_REQ"
              | "XID" UINT_LIT

// 9. Layer 4 SCTP Sub-Keywords

              | "STREAM" UINT_LIT

              | "CHUNK" ("DATA" | "INIT" | "INIT_ACK" | "SACK" | "HEARTBEAT" | "HEARTBEAT_ACK" | "ABORT" | "SHUTDOWN" | "COOKIE_ECHO" | "COOKIE_ACK" | UINT_LIT | str_or_ident)
              | "INIT" | "INIT_ACK" | "SACK" | "HEARTBEAT" | "HEARTBEAT_ACK"
              | "ABORT" | "SHUTDOWN" | "COOKIE_ECHO" | "COOKIE_ACK"

// 10. SNMPv1 / SNMPv2c / SNMPv3 Sub-Keywords
snmp_proto_field: "TRAP" | "INFORM" | "GET" | "GETNEXT" | "GETBULK" | "SET" | "RESPONSE" str_or_ident? | "REPORT"
                | "COMMUNITY" STRING_LIT
                | "OID" oid_lit
                | "SYSUPTIME" UINT_LIT
                | "REQID" UINT_LIT
                | "NONREPEATERS" UINT_LIT

                | "AGENTIP" ip_addr

// 12. Lexical Terminals
str_or_ident: STRING_LIT | IDENT | contextual_keyword

contextual_keyword: "CNAME" | "TEXT" | "BINARY" | "PING" | "PONG" | "CLOSE"
                  | "INIT" | "INIT_ACK" | "SACK" | "HEARTBEAT" | "HEARTBEAT_ACK"
                  | "ABORT" | "SHUTDOWN" | "COOKIE_ECHO" | "COOKIE_ACK"
                  | "DATA" | "ACK" | "SYN" | "FIN" | "RST" | "PSH" | "URG"
                  | "SYNC" | "REPORT" | "TRAP" | "INFORM" | "GET" | "GETNEXT" | "GETBULK" | "SET" | "RESPONSE"
                  | "REQUEST" | "REPLY" | "QUERY" | "NOTIFY" | "HELLO" | "OPEN" | "UPDATE" | "KEEPALIVE"
                  | "CONNECT" | "CONNACK" | "PUBLISH" | "SUBSCRIBE" | "DISCONNECT"
                  | "START" | "LOGOFF" | "KEY" | "EAP_PACKET" | "AUTHEN" | "AUTHOR" | "ACCT"
                  | "OK" | "ERR" | "QUIT" | "EHLO" | "HELO" | "DB"

ip_addr: IPV4_ADDR | IPV6_ADDR
oid_lit: OID_LIT | STRING_LIT

IDENT: /[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*/
UINT_LIT: /0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9]+/
INT_LIT: /-?[0-9]+|0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+/
DURATION_LIT: /(?:0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9]+)(?:ns|us|ms|s|m)/
STRING_LIT: /"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"/
HEX_STRING_LIT: /"[0-9a-fA-F: ]*"/
MAC_ADDR: /[0-9a-fA-F]{2}(?::[0-9a-fA-F]{2}){5}|[0-9a-fA-F]{2}(?:-[0-9a-fA-F]{2}){5}|[0-9a-fA-F]{4}(?:\.[0-9a-fA-F]{4}){2}/
IPV4_ADDR: /[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/
IPV6_ADDR: /::[0-9a-fA-F:.]*|[0-9a-fA-F]{1,4}(?::[0-9a-fA-F:.]*)+/
OID_LIT: /\.?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)+/

COMMENT: /\/\/[^\n]*/
WS: /[ \t\r\n]+/

%ignore WS
%ignore COMMENT
```

- **`src/ast/mod.rs` (`HostDef`)**: `HOST <name> { IP <ip_addr> [MAC <mac_addr>] }`
- **`src/ast/mod.rs` (`FrameStatement`)**: `<caller> ->|<- <callee> [L2/L3/L4 modifiers] <Protocol> [ProtocolSpec] [WAIT <duration>]`
- **`src/ast/mod.rs` (`FlowDef`)**: `FLOW <name>(<param1>, <param2>) { <statements> }`

---

# Representative Verified `.fasm` Corpus Examples (All 81 Protocols & Topologies)


## `examples/l2/arp/arp_address_conflict_detection_probe.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RFC 5227 IPv4 Address Conflict Detection (ACD) ARP probe with zero sender IP and subsequent announcement.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ARP, REQUEST, SENDERMAC, SENDERIP, TARGETMAC, TARGETIP, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define newly booting DHCP client probing tentative IPv4 address.
HOST acd_prober {
    IP 192.168.42.77
    MAC 08:00:27:a1:b2:c3
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define local broadcast segment peer receiving ACD probes.
HOST lan_listener {
    IP 192.168.42.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:00:00:99
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define RFC 5227 ARP probe with 0.0.0.0 SPA followed by ARP announcement.
FLOW acd_probe_and_announce(prober, segment) {
    prober -> segment ARP REQUEST SENDERMAC 08:00:27:a1:b2:c3 SENDERIP 0.0.0.0 TARGETMAC 00:00:00:00:00:00 TARGETIP 192.168.42.77
    prober -> segment ARP REQUEST SENDERMAC 08:00:27:a1:b2:c3 SENDERIP 0.0.0.0 TARGETMAC 00:00:00:00:00:00 TARGETIP 192.168.42.77 WAIT 1s
    prober -> segment ARP REQUEST SENDERMAC 08:00:27:a1:b2:c3 SENDERIP 192.168.42.77 TARGETMAC 00:00:00:00:00:00 TARGETIP 192.168.42.77 WAIT 2s
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing IPv4 Address Conflict Detection sequence.
COMPILE {
    acd_probe_and_announce(acd_prober, lan_listener)
}
```

## `examples/l2/arp/arp_anycast_vxlan_distributed_gateway.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: EVPN-VXLAN leaf switch responding to host ARP Request with distributed anycast gateway virtual MAC 00:00:5e:00:01:01.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, VLAN, ARP, REQUEST, SENDERMAC, SENDERIP, TARGETMAC, TARGETIP, WAIT, REPLY, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define tenant bare-metal server querying default gateway MAC on VLAN 100.
HOST tenant_bm_srv {
    IP 10.100.1.55
    MAC 00:25:90:10:01:37
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define EVPN-VXLAN leaf switch serving distributed anycast gateway IP 10.100.1.1.
HOST evpn_anycast_leaf {
    IP 10.100.1.1
    MAC 00:00:5e:00:01:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Exchange broadcast ARP Request and unicast ARP Reply with virtual gateway hardware address on VLAN 100.
FLOW arp_evpn_anycast_gw(srv, leaf) {
    srv -> leaf VLAN 100 ARP REQUEST SENDERMAC 00:25:90:10:01:37 SENDERIP 10.100.1.55 TARGETMAC 00:00:00:00:00:00 TARGETIP 10.100.1.1 WAIT 2ms
    srv <- leaf VLAN 100 ARP REPLY SENDERMAC 00:00:5e:00:01:01 SENDERIP 10.100.1.1 TARGETMAC 00:25:90:10:01:37 TARGETIP 10.100.1.55
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the EVPN-VXLAN distributed anycast gateway ARP resolution trace.
COMPILE {
    arp_evpn_anycast_gw(tenant_bm_srv, evpn_anycast_leaf)
}
```

## `examples/l2/eapol/eapol_5g_akaprime_sim_card_authentication.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: IEEE 802.1X EAP-AKA' (EAP_METHOD 50) authentication for a 5G fixed-wireless CPE with USIM credentials.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, EAPOL, VERSION, TYPE, EAP_PACKET, EAP_CODE, EAP_ID, EAP_METHOD, WAIT, IDENTITY, PAYLOAD, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define 5G fixed-wireless CPE supplicant authenticating via EAP-AKA' (Method 50).
HOST cpe_usim_supp {
    IP 10.50.80.15
    MAC 00:26:bb:50:50:0f
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define carrier aggregation switch authenticator forwarding EAP-AKA' to 3GPP AUSF.
HOST carrier_pae_sw {
    IP 10.50.80.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:50:50:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Complete EAP-Identity and EAP-AKA' (Method 50) challenge/response culminating in EAP-Success (Code 3).
FLOW eapol_akaprime_auth(cpe, sw) {
    cpe <- sw EAPOL VERSION 2 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 1 EAP_ID 10 EAP_METHOD 1 WAIT 2ms
    cpe -> sw EAPOL VERSION 2 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 2 EAP_ID 10 EAP_METHOD 1 IDENTITY "631026000012345@wlan.mnc026.mcc310.3gppnetwork.org" WAIT 5ms
    cpe <- sw EAPOL VERSION 2 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 1 EAP_ID 11 EAP_METHOD 50 PAYLOAD "AKA_PRIME_RAND_AUTN_AT_KDF" WAIT 5ms
    cpe -> sw EAPOL VERSION 2 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 2 EAP_ID 11 EAP_METHOD 50 PAYLOAD "AKA_PRIME_AT_RES_AT_MAC" WAIT 5ms
    cpe <- sw EAPOL VERSION 2 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 3 EAP_ID 11 EAP_METHOD 50
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the 5G EAP-AKA' USIM port authentication trace.
COMPILE {
    eapol_akaprime_auth(cpe_usim_supp, carrier_pae_sw)
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: IEEE 802.1X authentication rejection emitting EAP-Failure (EAP_CODE 4) for an unauthorized contractor device.

    MAC b4:b5:2f:99:00:c8

    IP 10.99.0.1
    MAC 00:1e:14:99:00:01
}

FLOW eapol_auth_failure_reject(cli, sw) {
    cli -> sw EAPOL VERSION 1 TYPE START
```

## `examples/l2/lacp/lacp_5g_upf_dpdk_bond_mode4_hash_distribution.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: 5G UPF DPDK poll-mode driver bonding two 100GbE ports via IEEE 802.1AX LACP (state 0x3F fast active collecting/distributing).
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, LACP, ACTOR_SYS, ACTOR_KEY, ACTOR_PORT, ACTOR_STATE, PARTNER_SYS, PARTNER_KEY, PARTNER_PORT, PARTNER_STATE, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define 5G UPF DPDK bond0 primary 100GbE interface.
HOST upf_dpdk_bond0 {
    IP 100.64.10.10
    MAC 0c:42:a1:40:0a:0a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define leaf switch port-channel 10 member interface.
HOST leaf_po10_port {
    IP 100.64.10.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:40:0a:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Synchronize LACP fast timeout (state 63 = 0x3F) and forward GTP-U payload over the active bond.
FLOW lacp_upf_dpdk_bond(upf, leaf) {
    upf -> leaf LACP ACTOR_SYS 0c:42:a1:40:0a:0a ACTOR_KEY 10 ACTOR_PORT 1 ACTOR_STATE 63 PARTNER_SYS 00:1c:73:40:0a:01 PARTNER_KEY 10 PARTNER_PORT 101 PARTNER_STATE 63 WAIT 2ms
    upf <- leaf LACP ACTOR_SYS 00:1c:73:40:0a:01 ACTOR_KEY 10 ACTOR_PORT 101 ACTOR_STATE 63 PARTNER_SYS 0c:42:a1:40:0a:0a PARTNER_KEY 10 PARTNER_PORT 1 PARTNER_STATE 63
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the 5G UPF DPDK Mode 4 LACP synchronization trace.
COMPILE {
    lacp_upf_dpdk_bond(upf_dpdk_bond0, leaf_po10_port)
}
```

## `examples/l2/lacp/lacp_active_initiator_passive_partner.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Passive switch vs Active server LACP negotiation where only the server sets the LACP Activity bit (0x01).
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, LACP, ACTOR_SYS, ACTOR_KEY, ACTOR_PORT, ACTOR_STATE, PARTNER_SYS, PARTNER_KEY, PARTNER_PORT, PARTNER_STATE, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define Linux bonding server configured in LACP active mode (state 0x3D = 61).
HOST active_linux_bond {
    IP 192.168.120.10
    MAC 52:54:00:78:00:0a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define access switch configured in LACP passive mode (state 0x3C = 60, Activity=0).
HOST passive_access_sw {
    IP 192.168.120.1
    MAC 00:1b:21:78:00:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define Active-to-Passive LACP negotiation exchange.
FLOW lacp_active_vs_passive(srv, sw) {
    srv -> sw LACP ACTOR_SYS 52:54:00:78:00:0a ACTOR_KEY 120 ACTOR_PORT 1 ACTOR_STATE 61 PARTNER_SYS 00:1b:21:78:00:01 PARTNER_KEY 120 PARTNER_PORT 24 PARTNER_STATE 60
    srv <- sw LACP ACTOR_SYS 00:1b:21:78:00:01 ACTOR_KEY 120 ACTOR_PORT 24 ACTOR_STATE 60 PARTNER_SYS 52:54:00:78:00:0a PARTNER_KEY 120 PARTNER_PORT 1 PARTNER_STATE 61 WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing Active/Passive LACP port-channel synchronization.
COMPILE {
    lacp_active_vs_passive(active_linux_bond, passive_access_sw)
}
```

```frameassembly
    MAC 00:11:22:50:00:14
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Access switch executing UplinkFast failover to backup root port and advertising elevated path cost 3000.

    acc <- dist STP ROOT_ID "4096:00:1c:73:0c:01:01" BRIDGE_ID "8192:00:1c:73:0c:01:02" COST 4 PORT_ID 32770 MAX_AGE 20 HELLO_TIME 2 FORWARD_DELAY 15 FLAGS 0 WAIT 2ms
    acc -> dist STP ROOT_ID "4096:00:1c:73:0c:01:01" BRIDGE_ID "49152:00:1c:73:0c:01:0a" COST 3004 PORT_ID 32770 MAX_AGE 20 HELLO_TIME 2 FORWARD_DELAY 15 FLAGS 1
```

## `examples/l2/stp/stp_backbonefast_inferior_bpdu_rlq_recovery.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Distribution switch receiving an inferior BPDU after indirect root link failure and reasserting true Root Bridge identity.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, STP, ROOT_ID, BRIDGE_ID, COST, PORT_ID, MAX_AGE, HELLO_TIME, FORWARD_DELAY, FLAGS, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define distribution switch B losing its direct root link and mistakenly claiming root.
HOST dist_sw_indirect_fail {
    IP 10.15.0.2
    MAC 00:25:90:0f:00:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define peer switch C retaining valid path to Root Bridge A and correcting switch B.
HOST peer_sw_valid_path {
    IP 10.15.0.3
    MAC 00:25:90:0f:00:03
}

// INSTRUCTION: Send inferior self-rooted BPDU from switch B and immediately override with superior Root Bridge BPDU from switch C.
FLOW stp_backbonefast_recovery(sw_b, sw_c) {
    sw_b -> sw_c STP ROOT_ID "32768:00:25:90:0f:00:02" BRIDGE_ID "32768:00:25:90:0f:00:02" COST 0 PORT_ID 32769 MAX_AGE 20 HELLO_TIME 2 FORWARD_DELAY 15 FLAGS 0 WAIT 5ms
    sw_b <- sw_c STP ROOT_ID "4096:00:25:90:0f:00:01" BRIDGE_ID "32768:00:25:90:0f:00:03" COST 2000 PORT_ID 32770 MAX_AGE 20 HELLO_TIME 2 FORWARD_DELAY 15 FLAGS 0
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the STP BackboneFast inferior BPDU recovery sequence.
COMPILE {
    stp_backbonefast_recovery(dist_sw_indirect_fail, peer_sw_valid_path)
}
```

## `examples/l2/vlan/vlan_5g_midhaul_f1u_gtpu_qos_tag.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: 5G O-RAN midhaul F1-U GTP-U user-plane bearer traffic carried over IEEE 802.1Q VLAN 505 with PCP 5.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, VLAN, PCP, DEI, DSCP, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define 5G Centralized Unit User Plane (O-CU-UP) midhaul interface.
HOST oran_cu_up {
    IP 10.55.5.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:37:05:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define 5G Distributed Unit (O-DU) cell site aggregation interface.
HOST oran_du_agg {
    IP 10.55.5.2
    MAC 00:1c:73:37:05:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Transport UDP port 2152 GTP-U bearer frames on VLAN 505 PCP 5 DEI 0 with DSCP EF.
FLOW vlan_midhaul_f1u(cu, du) {
    cu -> du VLAN 505 PCP 5 DEI 0 DSCP 46 UDP SRCPORT 2152 DSTPORT 2152 PAYLOAD "f1u_dl_pdcp_nr_pdu_teid_1001" WAIT 2ms
    cu <- du VLAN 505 PCP 5 DEI 0 DSCP 46 UDP SRCPORT 2152 DSTPORT 2152 PAYLOAD "f1u_ul_pdcp_nr_pdu_teid_2002"
}
```

## `examples/l3/ah/ah_bgp_routing_session_authentication.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RFC 4302 IPsec AH authenticating an inter-domain eBGP control plane session (Next Header 6 TCP).
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, AH, SPI, SEQ, NEXT_HEADER, ICV, DSCP, TTL, PAYLOAD, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define autonomous system border router A with IPv4 and MAC address.
HOST asbr_router_a {
    IP 192.0.2.10
    MAC 00:1b:21:aa:10:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define autonomous system border router B validating AH-protected BGP packets.
HOST asbr_router_b {
    IP 192.0.2.11
    MAC 00:1b:21:aa:10:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define bidirectional AH flow protecting TCP Next Header 6 with CS6 DSCP marking.
FLOW ah_bgp_auth_flow(rtr_a, rtr_b) {
    rtr_a -> rtr_b AH SPI 40100 SEQ 1 NEXT_HEADER 6 ICV "112233445566778899aabbcc" DSCP 48 TTL 255 PAYLOAD "BGP_OPEN_AS65001" WAIT 5ms
    rtr_a <- rtr_b AH SPI 40101 SEQ 1 NEXT_HEADER 6 ICV "ccbbaa998877665544332211" DSCP 48 TTL 255 PAYLOAD "BGP_OPEN_AS65002" WAIT 5ms
    rtr_a -> rtr_b AH SPI 40100 SEQ 2 NEXT_HEADER 6 ICV "aabbccddeeff001122334455" DSCP 48 TTL 255 PAYLOAD "BGP_KEEPALIVE_ACK"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the AH-authenticated eBGP routing session flow.
COMPILE {
    ah_bgp_auth_flow(asbr_router_a, asbr_router_b)
}
```

## `examples/l3/bfd/bfd_admin_down_teardown.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: BFD session graceful administrative shutdown signaling State 0 (AdminDown) and Diag 7.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, BFD, STATE, DIAG, MY_DISC, YOUR_DISC, MULT, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define core router entering maintenance window.
HOST core_maint_rtr { IP 172.18.10.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define adjacent peer router receiving AdminDown notification.
HOST core_peer_rtr { IP 172.18.10.2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define BFD transition from Up (3) to AdminDown (0) with Diag 7.
FLOW bfd_admin_shutdown(maint, peer) {
    maint -> peer BFD STATE 3 DIAG 0 MY_DISC 4010 YOUR_DISC 4020 MULT 3
    maint -> peer BFD STATE 0 DIAG 7 MY_DISC 4010 YOUR_DISC 4020 MULT 3 WAIT 25ms
    maint <- peer BFD STATE 1 DIAG 3 MY_DISC 4020 YOUR_DISC 4010 MULT 3 WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the BFD administrative teardown flow.
COMPILE {
    bfd_admin_shutdown(core_maint_rtr, core_peer_rtr)
}
```

## `examples/l3/bfd/bfd_asymmetric_timer_negotiation.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: BFD asymmetric timer negotiation between fast hardware router and slower software peer.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, BFD, STATE, MY_DISC, YOUR_DISC, MIN_TX, MIN_RX, MULT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define hardware ASIC router capable of 3.3ms intervals.
HOST hw_asic_rtr { IP 10.77.0.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define virtualized software router requiring 250ms minimum RX interval.
HOST sw_vrouter { IP 10.77.0.2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define asymmetric BFD timer advertisement and adaptation.
FLOW bfd_asymmetric_timers(hw, sw) {
    hw -> sw BFD STATE 3 MY_DISC 6001 YOUR_DISC 6002 MIN_TX 3300 MIN_RX 3300 MULT 3
    hw <- sw BFD STATE 3 MY_DISC 6002 YOUR_DISC 6001 MIN_TX 250000 MIN_RX 250000 MULT 5
    hw -> sw BFD STATE 3 MY_DISC 6001 YOUR_DISC 6002 MIN_TX 250000 MIN_RX 3300 MULT 3
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the asymmetric BFD timer negotiation flow.
COMPILE {
    bfd_asymmetric_timers(hw_asic_rtr, sw_vrouter)
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Border Gateway Protocol 4+ peering over IPv6 using TCP 179 with OPEN and KEEPALIVE messages.
```

## `examples/l3/bgp/bgp_add_path_ecmp_multi_nexthop.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RFC 7911 BGP ADD-PATH Route Reflector advertising multiple ECMP next-hops for the same anycast prefix.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, BGP, UPDATE, ASN, PREFIX, NEXTHOP, DSCP, TTL, PAYLOAD, WAIT, KEEPALIVE, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define BGP Route Reflector with RFC 7911 ADD-PATH Send capability enabled.
HOST addpath_rr_server {
    IP 10.79.11.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:79:11:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define ingress WAN border router receiving multiple ECMP paths for 10.200.200.1/32.
HOST addpath_edge_client {
    IP 10.79.11.10
    MAC 00:1c:73:79:11:0a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define sequential BGP UPDATE messages advertising distinct NEXTHOPs for the same anycast /32 prefix.
FLOW bgp_add_path_ecmp_flow(rr, client) {
    rr -> client BGP UPDATE ASN 65000 PREFIX "10.200.200.1/32" NEXTHOP 10.1.1.1 DSCP 48 TTL 64 PAYLOAD "PATH_ID_1_LEAF_A" WAIT 3ms
    rr -> client BGP UPDATE ASN 65000 PREFIX "10.200.200.1/32" NEXTHOP 10.1.1.2 DSCP 48 TTL 64 PAYLOAD "PATH_ID_2_LEAF_B" WAIT 3ms
    rr -> client BGP UPDATE ASN 65000 PREFIX "10.200.200.1/32" NEXTHOP 10.1.1.3 DSCP 48 TTL 64 PAYLOAD "PATH_ID_3_LEAF_C" WAIT 3ms
    rr <- client BGP KEEPALIVE DSCP 48 TTL 64
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the RFC 7911 BGP ADD-PATH ECMP advertisement flow.
COMPILE {
    bgp_add_path_ecmp_flow(addpath_rr_server, addpath_edge_client)
}
```

## `examples/l3/esp/esp_anti_replay_sliding_window_stress.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RFC 4303 Section 3.4.3 IPsec ESP anti-replay 64-packet sliding window verification under out-of-order delivery.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ESP, SPI, SEQ, IV, ICV, NEXT_HEADER, DF, TTL, PAYLOAD, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define multi-path WAN sender transmitting ESP packets across asymmetric links.
HOST multipath_esp_tx {
    IP 10.50.99.1
    MAC 00:22:bd:50:99:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define WAN receiver validating out-of-order ESP sequence numbers within the 64-bit replay bitmap.
HOST multipath_esp_rx {
    IP 10.50.99.2
    MAC 00:22:bd:50:99:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define out-of-order ESP sequence numbers (SEQ 100, 103, 101, 102) advancing the replay window.
FLOW esp_anti_replay_window_test(tx, rx) {
    tx -> rx ESP SPI 99001 SEQ 100 IV "0000000000000064" ICV "010101010202020203030303" NEXT_HEADER 4 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "ESP_PKT_SEQ_100_IN_ORDER" WAIT 2ms
    tx -> rx ESP SPI 99001 SEQ 103 IV "0000000000000067" ICV "040404040505050506060606" NEXT_HEADER 4 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "ESP_PKT_SEQ_103_ADVANCE_TOP" WAIT 2ms
    tx -> rx ESP SPI 99001 SEQ 101 IV "0000000000000065" ICV "070707070808080809090909" NEXT_HEADER 4 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "ESP_PKT_SEQ_101_WINDOW_HIT" WAIT 2ms
    tx -> rx ESP SPI 99001 SEQ 102 IV "0000000000000066" ICV "0a0a0a0a0b0b0b0b0c0c0c0c" NEXT_HEADER 4 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "ESP_PKT_SEQ_102_WINDOW_FILL"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the ESP anti-replay sliding window out-of-order test flow.
COMPILE {
    esp_anti_replay_window_test(multipath_esp_tx, multipath_esp_rx)
}
```

```frameassembly
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, IKEV2, CREATE_CHILD_SA, INITIATOR_SPI, RESPONDER_SPI, MSGID, FLAGS, NEXT_PAYLOAD, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define site A IKEv2 daemon initiating rekey.
HOST rekey_ike_a { IP 172.16.101.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define site B IKEv2 daemon completing rekey.
HOST rekey_ike_b { IP 172.16.101.2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define encrypted CREATE_CHILD_SA exchange with Next Payload 46 (Encrypted and Authenticated).
FLOW ikev2_rekey_sk(a, b) {
    a -> b IKEV2 CREATE_CHILD_SA INITIATOR_SPI 300400500 RESPONDER_SPI 600700800 MSGID 4 FLAGS 8 NEXT_PAYLOAD 46
    a <- b IKEV2 CREATE_CHILD_SA INITIATOR_SPI 300400500 RESPONDER_SPI 600700800 MSGID 4 FLAGS 32 NEXT_PAYLOAD 46 WAIT 15ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the IKEv2 Child SA rekey flow.
COMPILE {
    ikev2_rekey_sk(rekey_ike_a, rekey_ike_b)
}
```

## `examples/l3/ikev2/ikev2_cloud_vpc_redundant_tunnel_bringup.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Enterprise edge router establishing primary IKEv2 SA_INIT and AUTH tunnel with a cloud VPC VPN gateway.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, DSCP, IKEV2, SA_INIT, INITIATOR_SPI, RESPONDER_SPI, MSGID, FLAGS, NEXT_PAYLOAD, WAIT, EXCHANGE, AUTH, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define on-premises enterprise SD-WAN border router.
HOST onprem_vpn_edge {
    IP 198.51.100.45
    MAC 00:1c:73:c6:64:2d
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define cloud VPC virtual private gateway endpoint.
HOST cloud_vpc_vgw {
    IP 203.0.113.200
    MAC 00:1c:73:cb:71:c8
}

// INSTRUCTION: Complete four-message IKE_SA_INIT and IKE_AUTH negotiation between on-premises edge and cloud VGW.
FLOW ikev2_cloud_vpc_setup(edge, vgw) {
    edge -> vgw DSCP 48 IKEV2 SA_INIT INITIATOR_SPI 91002001 RESPONDER_SPI 0 MSGID 0 FLAGS 8 NEXT_PAYLOAD 33 WAIT 10ms
    edge <- vgw DSCP 48 IKEV2 SA_INIT INITIATOR_SPI 91002001 RESPONDER_SPI 92003002 MSGID 0 FLAGS 32 NEXT_PAYLOAD 33 WAIT 10ms
    edge -> vgw DSCP 48 IKEV2 EXCHANGE AUTH INITIATOR_SPI 91002001 RESPONDER_SPI 92003002 MSGID 1 FLAGS 8 NEXT_PAYLOAD 46 WAIT 10ms
    edge <- vgw DSCP 48 IKEV2 EXCHANGE AUTH INITIATOR_SPI 91002001 RESPONDER_SPI 92003002 MSGID 1 FLAGS 32 NEXT_PAYLOAD 46
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the cloud VPC IKEv2 SA_INIT and AUTH negotiation trace.
COMPILE {
    ikev2_cloud_vpc_setup(onprem_vpn_edge, cloud_vpc_vgw)
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: 5G Non-3GPP InterWorking Function (N3IWF) IPsec tunnel protecting NAS and UPF user-plane traffic.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, DSCP, IPSEC, SPI, SEQ, NEXT_HEADER, IV, ICV, PAYLOAD, WAIT, COMPILE
```

## `examples/l3/mld/mld_all_routers_multicast_leave.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Capture multiple IPv6 hosts reporting multicast group membership and one host sending MLD Done to all-routers multicast
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, MLD, REPORT, MULTICAST_ADDR, MAX_RESP_DELAY, SRCMAC, DSTMAC, TTL, WAIT, DONE, QUERY, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the first cluster node participating in an IPv6 multicast group
HOST cluster_node_1 {
    IP fe80::10:1
    MAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the second cluster node participating in the same IPv6 multicast group
HOST cluster_node_2 {
    IP fe80::10:2
    MAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the IPv6 multicast router on the cluster network
HOST cluster_mrouter {
    IP fe80::10:fe
    MAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:fe
}

// INSTRUCTION: Both nodes report membership, node 1 leaves to 33:33:00:00:00:02, and node 2 re-confirms
FLOW mld_cluster_leave_sequence(n1, n2, rtr) {
    n1 -> rtr MLD REPORT MULTICAST_ADDR ff05::c100:1 MAX_RESP_DELAY 0 SRCMAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:01 DSTMAC 33:33:c1:00:00:01 TTL 1 WAIT 10ms
    n2 -> rtr MLD REPORT MULTICAST_ADDR ff05::c100:1 MAX_RESP_DELAY 0 SRCMAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:02 DSTMAC 33:33:c1:00:00:01 TTL 1 WAIT 30ms
    n1 -> rtr MLD DONE MULTICAST_ADDR ff05::c100:1 MAX_RESP_DELAY 0 SRCMAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:01 DSTMAC 33:33:00:00:00:02 TTL 1 WAIT 10ms
    rtr -> n2 MLD QUERY MULTICAST_ADDR ff05::c100:1 MAX_RESP_DELAY 1000 TTL 1 WAIT 10ms
    n2 -> rtr MLD REPORT MULTICAST_ADDR ff05::c100:1 MAX_RESP_DELAY 0 SRCMAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:02 DSTMAC 33:33:c1:00:00:01 TTL 1
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the cluster multicast leave and re-confirmation trace
COMPILE {
    mld_cluster_leave_sequence(cluster_node_1, cluster_node_2, cluster_mrouter)
}
```

## `examples/l3/ndp/ndp_anycast_gateway_evpn_mac_mobility.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: EVPN-VXLAN distributed anycast IPv6 gateway advertising virtual MAC via Neighbor Advertisement after VM vMotion.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, TTL, NDP, NEIGHBOR_SOLICIT, TARGET, SLLA, WAIT, NEIGHBOR_ADVERT, TLLA, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define destination leaf switch advertising distributed anycast IPv6 gateway address.
HOST evpn_leaf_anycast {
    IP 2001:db8:400::1
    MAC 00:00:5e:00:02:64
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define migrated virtual machine resolving default gateway MAC on new rack.
HOST migrated_vm_v6 {
    IP 2001:db8:400::88
    MAC 52:54:00:40:00:88
}

// INSTRUCTION: Resolve anycast gateway via Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement with Hop Limit 255.
FLOW ndp_evpn_anycast_resolve(leaf, vm) {
    vm -> leaf TTL 255 NDP NEIGHBOR_SOLICIT TARGET 2001:db8:400::1 SLLA 52:54:00:40:00:88 WAIT 5ms
    leaf -> vm TTL 255 NDP NEIGHBOR_ADVERT TARGET 2001:db8:400::1 TLLA 00:00:5e:00:02:64 WAIT 10ms
    vm -> leaf TTL 255 NDP NEIGHBOR_ADVERT TARGET 2001:db8:400::88 TLLA 52:54:00:40:00:88
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the EVPN distributed anycast IPv6 gateway NDP resolution trace.
COMPILE {
    ndp_evpn_anycast_resolve(evpn_leaf_anycast, migrated_vm_v6)
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Simulate an OpenFlow controller communicating with switches on both IANA TCP port 6653 and legacy TCP port 6633
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, OPENFLOW, FEATURES_REQ, VERSION, XID, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, WAIT, FEATURES_REPLY, DPID, COMPILE

    IP 10.150.10.1
    MAC 00:25:90:e8:10:01
}

HOST modern_sw {
    IP 10.150.10.11
    MAC 00:25:90:e8:10:11
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the legacy switch listening on TCP port 6633
HOST legacy_sw {
    IP 10.150.10.12
    MAC 00:25:90:e8:10:12
}

// INSTRUCTION: Poll the modern switch on port 6653 and the legacy switch on port 6633
FLOW openflow_custom_ports_poll(ctrl, sw_new, sw_old) {
    ctrl -> sw_new OPENFLOW FEATURES_REQ VERSION 4 XID 101 SRCPORT 52100 DSTPORT 6653 WAIT 10ms
    sw_new -> ctrl OPENFLOW FEATURES_REPLY VERSION 4 XID 101 DPID 1001 SRCPORT 6653 DSTPORT 52100 WAIT 15ms
    ctrl -> sw_old OPENFLOW FEATURES_REQ VERSION 1 XID 201 SRCPORT 52101 DSTPORT 6633 WAIT 10ms
    sw_old -> ctrl OPENFLOW FEATURES_REPLY VERSION 1 XID 201 DPID 2002 SRCPORT 6633 DSTPORT 52101
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the dual-port OpenFlow discovery sequence
COMPILE {
    openflow_custom_ports_poll(multi_port_ctrl, modern_sw, legacy_sw)
}
```

## `examples/l3/ospf/ospf_datacenter_ecmp_leaf_spine_convergence.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Data center leaf-spine OSPF point-to-point fast convergence using 1-second Hello and 4-second Dead intervals.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, DSCP, TTL, OSPF, HELLO, ROUTER_ID, AREA_ID, HELLO_INTERVAL, DEAD_INTERVAL, PRIORITY, WAIT, DBD, LSU, LSACK, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define spine router 1 forming point-to-point OSPF Area 0 adjacency.
HOST dc_spine_rtr1 {
    IP 10.255.1.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:ff:01:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define leaf switch 4 participating in 16-way ECMP OSPF fabric routing.
HOST dc_leaf_sw4 {
    IP 10.255.1.2
    MAC 00:1c:73:ff:01:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Exchange fast OSPF Hellos (1s/4s), Database Description, Link State Update, and Link State Ack.
FLOW ospf_ecmp_fabric_sync(spine, leaf) {
    spine -> leaf DSCP 48 TTL 1 OSPF HELLO ROUTER_ID 10.255.0.1 AREA_ID 0 HELLO_INTERVAL 1 DEAD_INTERVAL 4 PRIORITY 0 WAIT 5ms
    leaf -> spine DSCP 48 TTL 1 OSPF HELLO ROUTER_ID 10.255.0.14 AREA_ID 0 HELLO_INTERVAL 1 DEAD_INTERVAL 4 PRIORITY 0 WAIT 5ms
    spine -> leaf DSCP 48 TTL 1 OSPF DBD ROUTER_ID 10.255.0.1 AREA_ID 0 WAIT 5ms
    leaf -> spine DSCP 48 TTL 1 OSPF LSU ROUTER_ID 10.255.0.14 AREA_ID 0 WAIT 5ms
    spine -> leaf DSCP 48 TTL 1 OSPF LSACK ROUTER_ID 10.255.0.1 AREA_ID 0
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the data center ECMP leaf-spine OSPF fast convergence sequence.
COMPILE {
    ospf_ecmp_fabric_sync(dc_spine_rtr1, dc_leaf_sw4)
}
```

## `examples/l3/pim/pim_assert_multi_access_lan_metric_tiebreak.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RFC 7761 Section 4.6 PIM Assert election resolving duplicate multicast forwarders on a multi-access broadcast VLAN.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, PIM, HELLO, GROUP, SOURCE, DR_PRIORITY, HOLDTIME, VLAN, PCP, DSCP, TTL, PAYLOAD, WAIT, JOIN_PRUNE, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define upstream multicast router 1 with superior Admin Distance and IGP metric.
HOST lan_mcast_fwd_1 {
    IP 172.16.103.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:67:01:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define upstream multicast router 2 pruning its outbound interface upon losing Assert.
HOST lan_mcast_fwd_2 {
    IP 172.16.103.2
    MAC 00:1c:73:67:01:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define competing PIM Assert messages on VLAN 103 and subsequent prune resolution.
FLOW pim_lan_assert_resolution(r1, r2) {
    r1 -> r2 PIM HELLO GROUP 239.16.1.1 SOURCE 10.16.0.10 DR_PRIORITY 200 HOLDTIME 105 VLAN 103 PCP 6 DSCP 48 TTL 1 PAYLOAD "PIM_ASSERT_PREF_110_METRIC_5" WAIT 3ms
    r1 <- r2 PIM HELLO GROUP 239.16.1.1 SOURCE 10.16.0.10 DR_PRIORITY 100 HOLDTIME 105 VLAN 103 PCP 6 DSCP 48 TTL 1 PAYLOAD "PIM_ASSERT_PREF_110_METRIC_20_LOSER" WAIT 3ms
    r1 <- r2 PIM JOIN_PRUNE GROUP 239.16.1.1 SOURCE 10.16.0.10 HOLDTIME 210 VLAN 103 PCP 6 DSCP 48 TTL 1 PAYLOAD "PIM_PRUNE_LOSING_OIL_INTERFACE"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the RFC 7761 multi-access LAN PIM Assert resolution flow.
COMPILE {
    pim_lan_assert_resolution(lan_mcast_fwd_1, lan_mcast_fwd_2)
}
```

## `examples/l3/rip/rip_counting_to_infinity_prevention_holddown.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RIPv2 holddown timer and poison reverse preventing counting-to-infinity routing loops across a 3-hop topology.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, RIP, RESPONSE, PREFIX, METRIC, NEXTHOP, TAG, DSCP, TTL, WAIT, PAYLOAD, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define downstream router R1 detecting failure of 10.99.0.0/24 and advertising metric 16.
HOST rip_loop_r1 {
    IP 10.52.1.1
    MAC 00:0c:29:52:01:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define upstream router R2 acknowledging poison reverse and entering holddown.
HOST rip_loop_r2 {
    IP 10.52.1.2
    MAC 00:0c:29:52:01:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define metric progression from METRIC 3 to METRIC 16 holddown state.
FLOW rip_holddown_infinity_guard(r1, r2) {
    r1 -> r2 RIP RESPONSE PREFIX 10.99.0.0 METRIC 3 NEXTHOP 10.52.1.1 TAG 99 DSCP 48 TTL 1 WAIT 5ms
    r1 -> r2 RIP RESPONSE PREFIX 10.99.0.0 METRIC 16 NEXTHOP 10.52.1.1 TAG 99 DSCP 48 TTL 1 PAYLOAD "HOLDDOWN_TIMER_180S_STARTED" WAIT 5ms
    r1 <- r2 RIP RESPONSE PREFIX 10.99.0.0 METRIC 16 NEXTHOP 0.0.0.0 TAG 99 DSCP 48 TTL 1 PAYLOAD "POISON_ACK_ROUTE_FLUSHED"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the RIPv2 counting-to-infinity holddown prevention flow.
COMPILE {
    rip_holddown_infinity_guard(rip_loop_r1, rip_loop_r2)
}
```

## `examples/l3/vrrp/vrrp_active_active_dual_vrid_mhvrrp.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Multi-group VRRP load sharing where Router A is Master for VRID 101 (Backup for 102) and Router B is Master for VRID 102.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, VRRP, VRID, PRIORITY, ADV_INT, VIP, VERSION, DSCP, TTL, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define Core Router A (Master for VRID 101 VIP 10.10.0.1, Backup for VRID 102).
HOST mhvrrp_router_a {
    IP 10.10.0.252
    MAC 00:00:5e:00:01:65
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define Core Router B (Master for VRID 102 VIP 10.10.0.2, Backup for VRID 101).
HOST mhvrrp_router_b {
    IP 10.10.0.253
    MAC 00:00:5e:00:01:66
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define bidirectional VRRPv3 advertisements load-sharing VRID 101 and VRID 102.
FLOW vrrp_dual_vrid_active_active(rtr_a, rtr_b) {
    rtr_a -> rtr_b VRRP VRID 101 PRIORITY 200 ADV_INT 50 VIP 10.10.0.1 VERSION 3 DSCP 48 TTL 255 WAIT 10ms
    rtr_a <- rtr_b VRRP VRID 102 PRIORITY 200 ADV_INT 50 VIP 10.10.0.2 VERSION 3 DSCP 48 TTL 255 WAIT 10ms
    rtr_a -> rtr_b VRRP VRID 101 PRIORITY 200 ADV_INT 50 VIP 10.10.0.1 VERSION 3 DSCP 48 TTL 255
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the dual-VRID active-active VRRP load-sharing flow.
COMPILE {
    vrrp_dual_vrid_active_active(mhvrrp_router_a, mhvrrp_router_b)
}
```

## `examples/l3/wireguard/wireguard_anti_replay_out_of_order_window.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: WireGuard RFC 6479 2000-bit anti-replay sliding window accepting out-of-order UDP transport DATA packets.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, WIREGUARD, TYPE, DATA, RECEIVER, COUNTER, DF, TTL, PAYLOAD, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define multi-WAN WireGuard sender striping packets across asymmetric paths.
HOST wg_multipath_tx {
    IP 10.51.82.10
    MAC 00:22:bd:51:82:0a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define WireGuard receiver validating out-of-order COUNTER values (100, 103, 101, 102).
HOST wg_multipath_rx {
    IP 10.51.82.20
    MAC 00:22:bd:51:82:14
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define out-of-order WireGuard DATA packets within the 2000-packet replay window.
FLOW wg_anti_replay_window_flow(tx, rx) {
    tx -> rx WIREGUARD TYPE DATA RECEIVER 82001 COUNTER 100 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "WG_COUNTER_100_IN_ORDER" WAIT 1ms
    tx -> rx WIREGUARD TYPE DATA RECEIVER 82001 COUNTER 103 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "WG_COUNTER_103_ADVANCE_HEAD" WAIT 1ms
    tx -> rx WIREGUARD TYPE DATA RECEIVER 82001 COUNTER 101 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "WG_COUNTER_101_REORDERED_OK" WAIT 1ms
    tx -> rx WIREGUARD TYPE DATA RECEIVER 82001 COUNTER 102 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "WG_COUNTER_102_REORDERED_OK"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the WireGuard RFC 6479 anti-replay sliding window flow.
COMPILE {
    wg_anti_replay_window_flow(wg_multipath_tx, wg_multipath_rx)
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: WireGuard packet sequence exercising bare INITIATION, COOKIE, and DATA keywords alongside explicit TYPE RESPONSE.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, WIREGUARD, INITIATION, SENDER, DF, TTL, WAIT, COOKIE, RECEIVER, TYPE, RESPONSE, DATA, COUNTER, PAYLOAD, COMPILE

    MAC 00:50:56:51:99:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define complete sequence exercising bare INITIATION, COOKIE, TYPE RESPONSE, and bare DATA.
FLOW wg_bare_keyword_sequence(cli, srv) {
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: 4G LTE MME and eNodeB exchanging S1AP UE Context Release Command and Complete over SCTP port 36412 (PPID 18).
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, DSCP, SCTP, CHUNK, DATA, VTAG, STREAM, SSN, PPID, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, SACK, COMPILE

    MAC 00:1c:73:24:0c:32

    mme -> enb DSCP 46 SCTP CHUNK DATA VTAG 364121 STREAM 1 SSN 12 PPID 18 SRCPORT 36412 DSTPORT 36412 PAYLOAD "s1ap_ue_context_release_cmd_cause_normal" WAIT 2ms
```

## `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_3_way_handshake.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Establish a standard TCP 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) on HTTPS port 443 with explicit sequence and acknowledgment numbers.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, TCP, SYN, SEQ, DSTPORT, ACK, ACKNUM, SRCPORT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define an enterprise client with IP 10.10.10.10.
HOST enterprise_client { IP 10.10.10.10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define an enterprise server with IP 10.20.20.20.
HOST enterprise_server { IP 10.20.20.20 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow representing a standard TCP 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK).
FLOW three_way_handshake(client, server) {
    client -> server TCP SYN SEQ 100 DSTPORT 443
    client <- server TCP SYN ACK SEQ 500 ACKNUM 101 SRCPORT 443
    client -> server TCP ACK SEQ 101 ACKNUM 501 DSTPORT 443
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the TCP handshake flow.
COMPILE {
    three_way_handshake(enterprise_client, enterprise_server)
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RFC 5881 BFD over IPv4/UDP using Control port 3784 and Echo port 3785 with TTL 255 GTSM validation.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, TTL, DSCP, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, HEXPAYLOAD, WAIT, PAYLOAD, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define core router A running hardware-offloaded BFD Echo.

    a -> b TTL 255 DSCP 48 UDP SRCPORT 49152 DSTPORT 3784 HEXPAYLOAD "20c0031800000101000001020000c3500000c3500000c350"
    a <- b TTL 255 DSCP 48 UDP SRCPORT 49153 DSTPORT 3784 HEXPAYLOAD "20c0031800000102000001010000c3500000c3500000c350" WAIT 1ms
```

## `examples/l7/amqp/amqp_celery_task_queue_worker_dispatch.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Python Celery distributed task queue publishing a celery task message and delivering it to a worker pool.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, AMQP, BASIC_PUBLISH, CHANNEL, EXCHANGE, ROUTING_KEY, PAYLOAD, BASIC_DELIVER, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the Django web application queuing background image resizing tasks.
HOST django_web {
    IP 10.115.60.11
    MAC 00:1a:2b:73:60:11
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the Celery worker node consuming from the default celery queue.
HOST celery_worker {
    IP 10.115.60.22
    MAC 00:1a:2b:73:60:22
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the RabbitMQ task broker.
HOST task_broker {
    IP 10.115.60.1
    MAC 00:1a:2b:73:60:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Enqueue a Celery task from the Django web node.
FLOW enqueue_celery_task(w, b) {
    w -> b AMQP BASIC_PUBLISH CHANNEL 1 EXCHANGE "celery" ROUTING_KEY "celery" PAYLOAD "{'task':'media.tasks.resize_avatar','id':'c49a-8812','args':[4091]}"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Deliver the queued Celery task to the worker node.
FLOW deliver_celery_task(c, b) {
    c <- b AMQP BASIC_DELIVER CHANNEL 1 EXCHANGE "celery" ROUTING_KEY "celery" PAYLOAD "{'task':'media.tasks.resize_avatar','id':'c49a-8812','args':[4091]}"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the Celery task enqueue and worker delivery flows.

    deliver_celery_task(celery_worker, task_broker)
}
```

```frameassembly
    IP 10.110.140.1
    MAC 00:1a:2b:6e:e0:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Send POST to /bs, receive 2.04 Changed, then receive server-initiated CON PUT provisioning /0/0.
FLOW coap_lwm2m_bootstrap(d, b) {
    d -> b COAP CON CODE "0.02" MSGID 14001 TOKEN 801 URI_PATH "bs"
    d <- b COAP ACK CODE "2.04" MSGID 14001 TOKEN 801 WAIT 2ms
    d <- b COAP CON CODE "0.03" MSGID 9001 TOKEN 802 URI_PATH "0/0" CONTENT_FORMAT 11542 HEXPAYLOAD "c80014636f6170733a2f2f"
    d -> b COAP ACK CODE "2.04" MSGID 9001 TOKEN 802
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the CoAP LwM2M bootstrap provisioning flow.
COMPILE {
    coap_lwm2m_bootstrap(fresh_device, bootstrap_srv)
}
```

## `examples/l7/dnp3/dnp3_analog_input_deadband_group34_tuning.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: DNP3 WRITE to Analog Input Deadband (Group 34 Variation 2) adjusting feeder current reporting threshold.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, DNP3, FUNC, SRC, DST, GROUP, VARIATION, WAIT, HEXPAYLOAD, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the distribution management system (DMS) master.
HOST dms_master {
    IP 10.125.20.1
    MAC 00:1a:2b:7d:20:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the pole-top recloser controller outstation.
HOST recloser_rtu {
    IP 10.125.20.14
    MAC 00:1a:2b:7d:20:14
}

// INSTRUCTION: Read current Analog Input Deadbands (Group 34 Var 2) and write updated deadband value.
FLOW dnp3_deadband_write(m, r) {
    m -> r DNP3 FUNC "READ" SRC 1 DST 14 GROUP 34 VARIATION 2
    m <- r DNP3 FUNC "RESPONSE" SRC 14 DST 1 GROUP 34 VARIATION 2 WAIT 2ms
    m -> r DNP3 FUNC "WRITE" SRC 1 DST 14 GROUP 34 VARIATION 2 HEXPAYLOAD "0005000f00"
    m <- r DNP3 FUNC "RESPONSE" SRC 14 DST 1 GROUP 34 VARIATION 2
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the DNP3 Analog Input Deadband configuration flow.
COMPILE {
    dnp3_deadband_write(dms_master, recloser_rtu)
}
```

## `examples/l7/dnp3/dnp3_analog_output_crc_override.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: DNP3 Analog Output setpoint command (Group 41 Variation 2) with explicit CRC override.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, DNP3, FUNC, SRC, DST, GROUP, VARIATION, CRC, PAYLOAD, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define turbine governor PLC outstation.

// INSTRUCTION: Issue Direct Operate on Analog Output Block (Group 41 Var 2) with custom CRC.

    m <- p DNP3 FUNC "RESPONSE" SRC 20 DST 10 GROUP 41 VARIATION 2 CRC 0x91c4
}
```

## `examples/l7/http/http_auth_401_unauthorized_bearer.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: HTTP API authentication challenge with 401 Unauthorized followed by authenticated Bearer token request.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, HTTP, METHOD, URI, HOST_HDR, WAIT, STATUS, REASON, HEADER, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define API client consumer.
HOST api_consumer {
    IP 10.45.12.33
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define OAuth protected API server host.
HOST oauth_resource {
    IP 10.45.12.1
}

// INSTRUCTION: Exchange unauthenticated probe and retry with valid Bearer token.
FLOW http_auth_challenge(c, s) {
    c -> s HTTP METHOD "GET" URI "/secure/data"
           HOST_HDR "api.enterprise.com" WAIT 2ms
    c <- s HTTP STATUS 401 REASON "Unauthorized"
           HEADER "WWW-Authenticate" "Bearer realm=\"enterprise\"" WAIT 5ms
    c -> s HTTP METHOD "GET" URI "/secure/data"
           HOST_HDR "api.enterprise.com"
           HEADER "Authorization" "Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9" WAIT 2ms
    c <- s HTTP STATUS 200 REASON "OK"
           HEADER "Content-Type" "application/json"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile 401 authentication challenge flow.
COMPILE {
    http_auth_challenge(api_consumer, oauth_resource)
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: HTTP 401 Unauthorized challenge with WWW-Authenticate header and authenticated retry.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, HTTP, METHOD, URI, HOST_HDR, STATUS, REASON, HEADER, BODY, COMPILE

    c -> s HTTP METHOD "GET" URI "/api/secrets" HOST_HDR "vault.internal" HEADER "Authorization" "Bearer tok_998877"
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: 3GPP 5G N12 interface HTTP/2 exchange between AMF and AUSF performing UE 5G-AKA authentication on Stream 17.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, HTTP2, HEADERS, STREAM_ID, DSCP, DATA, PAYLOAD, COMPILE

    MAC 00:1e:49:1f:0c:0a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define 5G Authentication Server Function (AUSF).
HOST ausf_node {
    IP 172.31.12.20
    MAC 00:1e:49:1f:0c:14
}

// INSTRUCTION: Execute Nausf_UEAuthentication POST request and 201 Created response on HTTP/2 Stream 17.
FLOW http2_5g_n12_ausf(amf, ausf) {
    amf -> ausf HTTP2 HEADERS STREAM_ID 17 DSCP 34
    amf -> ausf HTTP2 DATA STREAM_ID 17 DSCP 34 PAYLOAD "{'supiOrSuci':'suci-0-001-01-0'}"

    amf <- ausf HTTP2 DATA STREAM_ID 17 DSCP 34 PAYLOAD "{'authType':'5G_AKA'}"
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Simulate an IPFIX transit peering accounting export reporting high-volume HTTPS flow octets on Observation Domain 400.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, IPFIX, DOMAIN_ID, SRCIP, DSTIP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PROTO, PACKETS, OCTETS, DSCP, WAIT, COMPILE

    MAC 00:1b:21:47:39:c8
}

// INSTRUCTION: Export two peering traffic flow records on Observation Domain 400 over UDP port 4739.
FLOW ipfix_peering_billing(exp, col) {
    exp -> col IPFIX DOMAIN_ID 400 SRCIP 203.0.113.45 DSTIP 192.0.2.180 SRCPORT 54321 DSTPORT 443 PROTO 6 PACKETS 18500 OCTETS 26640000 DSCP 16 WAIT 5ms
    exp -> col IPFIX DOMAIN_ID 400 SRCIP 192.0.2.180 DSTIP 203.0.113.45 SRCPORT 443 DSTPORT 54321 PROTO 6 PACKETS 9200 OCTETS 644000 DSCP 16
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the IPFIX peering accounting export flow.
COMPILE {
    ipfix_peering_billing(peering_exporter, billing_collector)
}
```

## `examples/l7/ldap/ldap_ad_netlogon_rootdse_ping.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Simulate an Active Directory CLDAP UDP port 389 Netlogon DnsDomain ping and response.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, LDAP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, MSGID, SEARCH_REQ, BASE_DN, FILTER, WAIT, SEARCH_ENTRY, SEARCH_DONE, RESULT_CODE, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the Windows domain member locating the closest site-aware domain controller.
HOST domain_member {
    IP 10.45.12.90
    MAC 00:15:5d:2d:0c:5a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the Active Directory Domain Controller answering CLDAP pings.
HOST site_dc {
    IP 10.45.1.10
    MAC 00:15:5d:2d:01:0a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Send an LDAP RootDSE Netlogon filter search and receive the Netlogon attribute entry and completion.
FLOW cldap_netlogon_ping(c, s) {
    c -> s LDAP SRCPORT 58412 DSTPORT 389 MSGID 1 SEARCH_REQ BASE_DN "" FILTER "(&(DnsDomain=CORP.EXAMPLE.COM)(Host=WIN-CLIENT01)(NtVer=\06\00\00\00))" WAIT 2ms
    c <- s LDAP SRCPORT 389 DSTPORT 58412 MSGID 1 SEARCH_ENTRY BASE_DN "" WAIT 1ms
    c <- s LDAP SRCPORT 389 DSTPORT 58412 MSGID 1 SEARCH_DONE RESULT_CODE 0
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the Active Directory Netlogon LDAP ping trace into a PCAP file.
COMPILE {
    cldap_netlogon_ping(domain_member, site_dc)
}
```

## `examples/l7/mdns/mdns_apple_timemachine_adisk_discovery.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Create an mDNS Time Machine backup discovery flow querying _adisk._tcp.local and receiving TXT and SRV records.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, MDNS, QUERY, TXID, QNAME, QTYPE, TTL, WAIT, RESPONSE, RDATA, ANS_TTL, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the macOS laptop searching for network Time Machine backup volumes.
HOST macbook_pro {
    IP 192.168.15.42
    MAC f0:18:98:15:00:42
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the network-attached storage appliance advertising _adisk._tcp.local.
HOST timemachine_nas {
    IP 192.168.15.200
    MAC 00:11:32:15:02:00
}

// INSTRUCTION: Query _adisk._tcp.local PTR and receive the SRV and TXT volume metadata responses.
FLOW adisk_timemachine_lookup(client, nas) {
    client -> nas MDNS QUERY TXID 0 QNAME "_adisk._tcp.local" QTYPE "PTR" TTL 255 WAIT 4ms
    client <- nas MDNS RESPONSE TXID 0 QNAME "_adisk._tcp.local" QTYPE "PTR" RDATA "Vault-NAS._adisk._tcp.local" ANS_TTL 4500 TTL 255 WAIT 2ms
    client <- nas MDNS RESPONSE TXID 0 QNAME "Vault-NAS._adisk._tcp.local" QTYPE "TXT" RDATA "dk0=adVN=TimeMachine,adVF=0x82" ANS_TTL 4500 TTL 255
}

COMPILE {
    adisk_timemachine_lookup(macbook_pro, timemachine_nas)
}
```

## `examples/l7/memcached/memcached_admin_version_and_flush_all.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Simulate an administrative Memcached FLUSH_ALL cache invalidation and VERSION check during a blue-green deployment.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, MEMCACHED, CMD, KEY, OPAQUE, WAIT, PAYLOAD, EXPTIME, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the deployment automation runner flushing stale schema caches during cutover.
HOST deploy_runner {
    IP 10.12.99.5
    MAC 00:16:3e:0c:63:05
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the staging Memcached instance being reset.
HOST staging_cache {
    IP 10.12.99.20
    MAC 00:16:3e:0c:63:14
}

// INSTRUCTION: Query server VERSION and then execute FLUSH_ALL with a 10-second grace delay.
FLOW admin_flush_and_version(c, s) {
    c -> s MEMCACHED CMD "VERSION" KEY "server" OPAQUE 1 WAIT 1ms
    c <- s MEMCACHED CMD "VERSION" KEY "server" OPAQUE 1 PAYLOAD "VERSION 1.6.22\r\n" WAIT 5ms
    c -> s MEMCACHED CMD "FLUSH_ALL" KEY "all" EXPTIME 10 OPAQUE 2 WAIT 2ms
    c <- s MEMCACHED CMD "OK" KEY "all" OPAQUE 2 PAYLOAD "OK\r\n"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the administrative Memcached VERSION and FLUSH_ALL trace into a PCAP file.
COMPILE {
    admin_flush_and_version(deploy_runner, staging_cache)
}
```

## `examples/l7/memcached/memcached_append_prepend_qinq_mpls.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Generate a Memcached APPEND and PREPEND log buffer aggregation flow over QinQ and MPLS encapsulation.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, MEMCACHED, SET, KEY, EXPTIME, OPAQUE, PAYLOAD, QINQ, INNER_VLAN, MPLS, DSCP, TTL, WAIT, CMD, GET, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the audit trail collector appending event IDs into a Memcached list key.
HOST audit_worker {
    IP 10.150.12.30
    MAC 00:1e:67:96:0c:1e
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the remote Memcached aggregation server across an MPLS core.
HOST remote_memcache {
    IP 10.150.1.10
    MAC 00:1e:67:96:01:0a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Initialize a list with SET, APPEND a newer event ID, PREPEND a header tag, and GET the combined string over QinQ/MPLS.
FLOW append_prepend_qinq_mpls(c, s) {
    c -> s MEMCACHED SET KEY "audit:batch:42" EXPTIME 600 OPAQUE 601 PAYLOAD "evt100," QINQ 350 INNER_VLAN 25 MPLS 51000 DSCP 24 TTL 61 WAIT 3ms
    c <- s MEMCACHED CMD "STORED" KEY "audit:batch:42" OPAQUE 601 QINQ 350 INNER_VLAN 25 MPLS 51000 DSCP 24 TTL 61 WAIT 2ms
    c -> s MEMCACHED CMD "APPEND" KEY "audit:batch:42" OPAQUE 602 PAYLOAD "evt101" QINQ 350 INNER_VLAN 25 MPLS 51000 DSCP 24 TTL 61 WAIT 3ms
    c <- s MEMCACHED CMD "STORED" KEY "audit:batch:42" OPAQUE 602 QINQ 350 INNER_VLAN 25 MPLS 51000 DSCP 24 TTL 61 WAIT 2ms
    c -> s MEMCACHED GET KEY "audit:batch:42" OPAQUE 603 QINQ 350 INNER_VLAN 25 MPLS 51000 DSCP 24 TTL 61 WAIT 3ms
    c <- s MEMCACHED GET KEY "audit:batch:42" OPAQUE 603 PAYLOAD "evt100,evt101" QINQ 350 INNER_VLAN 25 MPLS 51000 DSCP 24 TTL 61
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the QinQ and MPLS Memcached APPEND trace into a PCAP file.
COMPILE {
    append_prepend_qinq_mpls(audit_worker, remote_memcache)
}
```

## `examples/l7/mqtt/mqtt_broker_bridge_qinq_mpls.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Build an MQTT inter-datacenter broker bridge synchronization flow over QinQ 700/40 and MPLS label 88100.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, MQTT, CONNECT, CLIENT_ID, QINQ, INNER_VLAN, MPLS, DSCP, WAIT, CONNACK, RETURN_CODE, SUBSCRIBE, TOPIC, QOS, PKT_ID, SUBACK, PUBLISH, PAYLOAD, PUBACK, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the regional edge MQTT broker bridging local sensor topics to the central cloud broker.
HOST edge_bridge_broker {
    IP 10.180.40.5
    MAC 00:50:56:b4:28:05
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the central core MQTT broker receiving bridged publications over MPLS.
HOST core_cloud_broker {
    IP 10.180.1.5
    MAC 00:50:56:b4:01:05
}

// INSTRUCTION: Establish the MQTT bridge session, subscribe to downward command topics, and forward an upward QoS 1 event over QinQ/MPLS.
FLOW broker_bridge_qinq_mpls(c, s) {
    c -> s MQTT CONNECT CLIENT_ID "bridge-site40-primary" QINQ 700 INNER_VLAN 40 MPLS 88100 DSCP 32 WAIT 6ms
    c <- s MQTT CONNACK RETURN_CODE 0 QINQ 700 INNER_VLAN 40 MPLS 88100 DSCP 32 WAIT 3ms
    c -> s MQTT SUBSCRIBE TOPIC "cmd/site40/+/setpoint" QOS 1 PKT_ID 1 QINQ 700 INNER_VLAN 40 MPLS 88100 DSCP 32 WAIT 6ms
    c <- s MQTT SUBACK PKT_ID 1 QOS 1 QINQ 700 INNER_VLAN 40 MPLS 88100 DSCP 32 WAIT 5ms
    c -> s MQTT PUBLISH TOPIC "telemetry/site40/chiller1/temp" QOS 1 PKT_ID 2 PAYLOAD "6.8" QINQ 700 INNER_VLAN 40 MPLS 88100 DSCP 32 WAIT 6ms
    c <- s MQTT PUBACK PKT_ID 2 QINQ 700 INNER_VLAN 40 MPLS 88100 DSCP 32
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the QinQ and MPLS MQTT broker bridge trace into a PCAP file.
COMPILE {
    broker_bridge_qinq_mpls(edge_bridge_broker, core_cloud_broker)
}
```

## `examples/l7/opcua/opcua_aborted_chunk_transfer.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: OPC UA aborted message chunk (CHUNK_TYPE "A") when payload generation is interrupted.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, OPCUA, MSG_TYPE, CHUNK_TYPE, SECURE_CHANNEL_ID, TOKEN_ID, SEQ_NUM, REQID, WAIT, HEXPAYLOAD, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define SCADA supervisor host.
HOST supervisor { IP 10.90.1.5 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define RTU OPC UA agent host.
HOST rtu_agent { IP 10.90.1.50 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define intermediate chunk C followed by abort chunk A.
FLOW opcua_chunk_abort(c, s) {
    c <- s OPCUA MSG_TYPE "MSG" CHUNK_TYPE "C" SECURE_CHANNEL_ID 15 TOKEN_ID 2 SEQ_NUM 80 REQID 301 WAIT 4ms
    c <- s OPCUA MSG_TYPE "MSG" CHUNK_TYPE "A" SECURE_CHANNEL_ID 15 TOKEN_ID 2 SEQ_NUM 81 REQID 301 HEXPAYLOAD "00008080"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the aborted chunk scenario.
COMPILE {
    opcua_chunk_abort(supervisor, rtu_agent)
}
```

## `examples/l7/postgres/postgres_acid_transaction_commit.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: PostgreSQL transactional BEGIN, INSERT, and COMMIT batch with COMMAND_COMPLETE replies.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, POSTGRES, SQL, WAIT, COMMAND_COMPLETE, READY_FOR_QUERY, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define payment service client.
HOST pay_svc { IP 10.50.10.22 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define ledger PostgreSQL server.
HOST ledger_db { IP 10.50.10.10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define SQL transaction lifecycle from BEGIN to COMMIT.
FLOW pg_acid_txn(c, s) {
    c -> s POSTGRES SQL "BEGIN" WAIT 2ms
    c <- s POSTGRES COMMAND_COMPLETE WAIT 2ms
    c -> s POSTGRES SQL "INSERT INTO ledger (acct_id, amount) VALUES (1042, 5000)" WAIT 5ms
    c <- s POSTGRES COMMAND_COMPLETE WAIT 2ms
    c -> s POSTGRES SQL "COMMIT" WAIT 3ms
    c <- s POSTGRES COMMAND_COMPLETE READY_FOR_QUERY
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile PostgreSQL ACID transaction flow.
COMPILE {
    pg_acid_txn(pay_svc, ledger_db)
}
```

## `examples/l7/postgres/postgres_advisory_lock_coordination.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: PostgreSQL advisory lock acquisition and release coordinating distributed cron workers.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, POSTGRES, SQL, WAIT, COMMAND_COMPLETE, READY_FOR_QUERY, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define distributed cron scheduler node A.
HOST cron_node_a { IP 10.77.1.11 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define distributed cron scheduler node B.
HOST cron_node_b { IP 10.77.1.12 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define central coordination PostgreSQL database.
HOST coord_db { IP 10.77.1.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define pg_try_advisory_lock and pg_advisory_unlock flow.
FLOW pg_advisory_lock(worker, db) {
    worker -> db POSTGRES SQL "SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(9001)" WAIT 3ms
    worker <- db POSTGRES COMMAND_COMPLETE READY_FOR_QUERY WAIT 10ms
    worker -> db POSTGRES SQL "SELECT pg_advisory_unlock(9001)" WAIT 3ms
    worker <- db POSTGRES COMMAND_COMPLETE READY_FOR_QUERY
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile advisory lock flow across both cron worker nodes.
COMPILE {
    pg_advisory_lock(cron_node_a, coord_db)
    pg_advisory_lock(cron_node_b, coord_db)
}
```

## `examples/l7/ptp/ptp_5g_fronthaul_ecpri_domain_24_qinq.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Simulate a 5G eCPRI fronthaul O-DU to O-RU PTPv2 phase distribution on Domain 24 over QinQ 800/24.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, PTP, SYNC, DOMAIN, SEQ_ID, CLOCK_ID, QINQ, INNER_VLAN, DSCP, WAIT, FOLLOW_UP, DELAY_REQ, DELAY_RESP, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the IEEE 1588v2 PTP Grandmaster clock endpoint.
HOST ptp_grandmaster {
    IP 10.24.0.1
    MAC 00:1b:21:31:90:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the IEEE 1588v2 PTP Ordinary or Boundary slave clock endpoint.
HOST ptp_slave_clock {
    IP 10.24.0.10
    MAC 00:1b:21:31:90:25
}

// INSTRUCTION: Execute the IEEE 1588v2 Precision Time Protocol message exchange.
FLOW ptp_scenario_flow(gm, slv) {
    gm -> slv PTP SYNC DOMAIN 24 SEQ_ID 7701 CLOCK_ID "0024e8fffe240001" QINQ 800 INNER_VLAN 24 DSCP 46 WAIT 1ms
    gm -> slv PTP FOLLOW_UP DOMAIN 24 SEQ_ID 7701 CLOCK_ID "0024e8fffe240001" QINQ 800 INNER_VLAN 24 DSCP 46 WAIT 1ms
    gm <- slv PTP DELAY_REQ DOMAIN 24 SEQ_ID 7701 CLOCK_ID "0024e8fffe24000a" QINQ 800 INNER_VLAN 24 DSCP 46 WAIT 1ms
    gm -> slv PTP DELAY_RESP DOMAIN 24 SEQ_ID 7701 CLOCK_ID "0024e8fffe240001" QINQ 800 INNER_VLAN 24 DSCP 46
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the PTPv2 timing synchronization flow into a PCAP file.
COMPILE {
    ptp_scenario_flow(ptp_grandmaster, ptp_slave_clock)
}
```

## `examples/l7/quic/quic_bgp_over_quic_core_peering.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Next-generation BGP over QUIC (BoQ) core router peering session on UDP port 179 with DSCP CS6.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, QUIC, INITIAL, VERSION, DCID, SCID, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, DSCP, TTL, PKT_NUM, WAIT, HANDSHAKE, SHORT, PAYLOAD, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define Autonomous System 65001 border router.
HOST as65001_rtr {
    IP 192.0.2.101
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define Autonomous System 65002 peer router.
HOST as65002_rtr {
    IP 192.0.2.102
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define BGP over QUIC session establishment and OPEN message exchange with DSCP 48 (CS6).
FLOW quic_bgp_peering(r1, r2) {
    r1 -> r2 QUIC INITIAL VERSION 1 DCID 0x65001001 SCID 0x65002001 SRCPORT 50179 DSTPORT 179 DSCP 48 TTL 255 PKT_NUM 1 WAIT 3ms
    r1 <- r2 QUIC HANDSHAKE VERSION 1 DCID 0x65002001 SCID 0x65001001 SRCPORT 179 DSTPORT 50179 DSCP 48 TTL 255 PKT_NUM 1 WAIT 3ms
    r1 -> r2 QUIC SHORT DCID 0x65001001 SRCPORT 50179 DSTPORT 179 DSCP 48 TTL 255 PKT_NUM 2 PAYLOAD "BGP_OPEN_AS65001"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the BGP over QUIC core peering scenario.
COMPILE {
    quic_bgp_peering(as65001_rtr, as65002_rtr)
}
```

## `examples/l7/radius/radius_access_challenge_mfa_otp.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RADIUS two-factor MFA OTP flow using Access-Challenge before final Access-Accept.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, RADIUS, ACCESS_REQUEST, USER, NAS_IP, SERVICE_TYPE, WAIT, ACCESS_CHALLENGE, PAYLOAD, ACCESS_ACCEPT, FRAMED_IP, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define SSL-VPN firewall NAS.
HOST sslvpn_nas { IP 10.28.65.10 MAC 00:1b:17:28:65:0a }

// INSTRUCTION: Define MFA-enabled RADIUS server.
HOST mfa_radius { IP 10.28.65.1 MAC 00:1b:17:28:65:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define initial login, OTP challenge, OTP submission, and Framed-IP assignment.
FLOW radius_mfa_challenge(nas, aaa) {
    nas -> aaa RADIUS ACCESS_REQUEST USER "sec_engineer" NAS_IP 10.28.65.10 SERVICE_TYPE 2 WAIT 5ms
    nas <- aaa RADIUS ACCESS_CHALLENGE USER "sec_engineer" PAYLOAD "Enter 6-digit TOTP code" WAIT 10ms
    nas -> aaa RADIUS ACCESS_REQUEST USER "sec_engineer" NAS_IP 10.28.65.10 SERVICE_TYPE 2 PAYLOAD "TOTP:482910" WAIT 5ms
    nas <- aaa RADIUS ACCESS_ACCEPT USER "sec_engineer" FRAMED_IP 10.254.0.42 SERVICE_TYPE 2
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile RADIUS MFA Access-Challenge flow.
COMPILE {
    radius_mfa_challenge(sslvpn_nas, mfa_radius)
}
```

## `examples/l7/rtsp/rtsp_302_redirect_load_balancer.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RTSP REDIRECT (302 Moved Temporarily) load-balancing client to an edge media node.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, RTSP, METHOD, URI, CSEQ, WAIT, STATUS, TRANSPORT_HDR, SESSION, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define streaming client endpoint.
HOST viewer_client { IP 10.90.55.25 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define RTSP director load balancer.
HOST rtsp_director { IP 10.90.55.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define edge RTSP streaming node.
HOST rtsp_edge { IP 10.90.55.2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define initial DESCRIBE returning 302 redirect from director.
FLOW rtsp_redirect_302(c, dir) {
    c -> dir RTSP METHOD "DESCRIBE" URI "rtsp://10.90.55.1/live/sports" CSEQ 1 WAIT 4ms
    c <- dir RTSP STATUS 302 CSEQ 1
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define client connecting to redirected edge server.
FLOW rtsp_connect_edge(c, edge) {
    c -> edge RTSP METHOD "SETUP" URI "rtsp://10.90.55.2/live/sports/track1" CSEQ 2 TRANSPORT_HDR "RTP/AVP;unicast;client_port=6000-6001" WAIT 4ms
    c <- edge RTSP STATUS 200 CSEQ 2 WAIT 4ms
    c -> edge RTSP METHOD "PLAY" URI "rtsp://10.90.55.2/live/sports" CSEQ 3 SESSION "edge_sess_55"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile RTSP 302 redirect followed by edge playback.
COMPILE {
    rtsp_redirect_302(viewer_client, rtsp_director)
    rtsp_connect_edge(viewer_client, rtsp_edge)
}
```

```frameassembly
}

// INSTRUCTION: Export sFlow v5 samples transported over MPLS label 3010.
FLOW sflow_5g_upf(sw, col) {
    sw -> col SFLOW AGENT_IP 172.29.10.1 SUB_AGENT_ID 3 UPTIME 12800000 SAMPLES 20 MPLS 3010 EXP 4 BOS 1 MPLS_TTL 64
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the 5G UPF user-plane sFlow sampling scenario.
COMPILE {
    sflow_5g_upf(upf_agg_sw, telco_sflow_col)
}
```

## `examples/l7/sip/sip_302_moved_temporarily_call_forwarding.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: SIP 302 Moved Temporarily call forwarding redirecting incoming INVITE to mobile voicemail URI.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, SIP, INVITE, URI, FROM, TO, CALL_ID, CSEQ, WAIT, STATUS, REASON, CONTACT, ACK, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define originating SIP trunk proxy.
HOST orig_proxy {
    IP 10.22.15.10
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define user agent returning 302 redirect to voicemail server.
HOST redirect_uas {
    IP 10.22.15.50
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define voicemail media server receiving redirected INVITE.
HOST voicemail_srv {
    IP 10.22.15.99
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define initial INVITE redirected via 302 Moved Temporarily and ACK.
FLOW sip_302_redirect(p, uas) {
    p -> uas SIP INVITE URI "sip:bob@10.22.15.50" FROM "sip:alice@10.22.15.10" TO "sip:bob@10.22.15.50" CALL_ID "fwd-302" CSEQ 1 WAIT 4ms
    p <- uas SIP STATUS 302 REASON "Moved Temporarily" CALL_ID "fwd-302" CSEQ 1 CONTACT "sip:bob-vm@10.22.15.99" WAIT 4ms
    p -> uas SIP ACK URI "sip:bob@10.22.15.50" CALL_ID "fwd-302" CSEQ 1
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define follow-up INVITE sent to the Contact URI on the voicemail server.
FLOW sip_vm_connect(p, vm) {
    p -> vm SIP INVITE URI "sip:bob-vm@10.22.15.99" FROM "sip:alice@10.22.15.10" TO "sip:bob-vm@10.22.15.99" CALL_ID "fwd-302-vm" CSEQ 1 WAIT 4ms
    p <- vm SIP STATUS 200 REASON "OK" CALL_ID "fwd-302-vm" CSEQ 1
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the SIP 302 call forwarding scenario.
COMPILE {
    sip_302_redirect(orig_proxy, redirect_uas)
    sip_vm_connect(orig_proxy, voicemail_srv)
}
```

## `examples/l7/smtp/smtp_421_service_not_available_ratelimit.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Model an SMTP 421 4.7.0 Service not available connection rate-limit banner dropping an aggressive client.
// TOKENS: HOST, MAC, IP, FLOW, TCP, SYN, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, ACK, SMTP, CODE, REPLY, FIN, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the bulk mail sender and rate-limiting inbound MX server.
HOST bulk_sender {
    MAC 00:21:9b:44:55:66
    IP 198.51.100.144
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the ratelimit_mx mail endpoint.
HOST ratelimit_mx {
    MAC 00:21:9b:44:55:01
    IP 203.0.113.5
}

// INSTRUCTION: Connect on TCP port 25, receive 421 4.7.0 rate limit exceeded, and close the TCP connection.
FLOW smtp_421_rate_limit_drop(bulk_sender, ratelimit_mx) {
    bulk_sender -> ratelimit_mx TCP SYN SRCPORT 59025 DSTPORT 25
    ratelimit_mx -> bulk_sender TCP SYN ACK
    bulk_sender -> ratelimit_mx TCP ACK
    ratelimit_mx -> bulk_sender SMTP CODE 421 REPLY "4.7.0 mx.example.com Too many concurrent connections from your IP"
    ratelimit_mx -> bulk_sender TCP FIN ACK
    bulk_sender -> ratelimit_mx TCP FIN ACK
    ratelimit_mx -> bulk_sender TCP ACK
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the SMTP 421 rate limit banner drop flow.
COMPILE {
    smtp_421_rate_limit_drop(bulk_sender, ratelimit_mx)
}
```

## `examples/l7/smtp/smtp_451_greylisting_temporary_fail.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Simulate an SMTP greylisting temporary deferral returning 451 4.7.1 Try again later on RCPT TO.
// TOKENS: HOST, MAC, IP, FLOW, TCP, SYN, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, ACK, SMTP, CODE, REPLY, EHLO, MAIL_FROM, PARAM, RCPT_TO, QUIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the remote mail server and greylisting MX gateway.
HOST remote_mta {
    MAC 00:25:90:12:25:01
    IP 203.0.113.90
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the greylist_mx mail endpoint.
HOST greylist_mx {
    MAC 00:25:90:12:25:02
    IP 198.51.100.10
}

// INSTRUCTION: Attempt mail delivery and receive a 451 4.7.1 Greylisting temporary failure response.
FLOW smtp_451_greylisting_deferral(remote_mta, greylist_mx) {
    remote_mta -> greylist_mx TCP SYN SRCPORT 54025 DSTPORT 25
    greylist_mx -> remote_mta TCP SYN ACK
    remote_mta -> greylist_mx TCP ACK
    greylist_mx -> remote_mta SMTP CODE 220 REPLY "mx.secure.net ESMTP"
    remote_mta -> greylist_mx SMTP EHLO "mta1.partner.org"
    greylist_mx -> remote_mta SMTP CODE 250 REPLY "mx.secure.net"
    remote_mta -> greylist_mx SMTP MAIL_FROM PARAM "<news@partner.org>"
    greylist_mx -> remote_mta SMTP CODE 250 REPLY "2.1.0 Sender OK"
    remote_mta -> greylist_mx SMTP RCPT_TO PARAM "<ops@secure.net>"
    greylist_mx -> remote_mta SMTP CODE 451 REPLY "4.7.1 Greylisted, please try again in 300 seconds"
    remote_mta -> greylist_mx SMTP QUIT
    greylist_mx -> remote_mta SMTP CODE 221 REPLY "2.0.0 Closing connection"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the SMTP 451 greylisting deferral flow.
COMPILE {
    smtp_451_greylisting_deferral(remote_mta, greylist_mx)
}
```

## `examples/l7/snmp/snmpv1/snmpv1_all_supported_v1_varbind_types.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Generate an SNMPv1 trap containing all 7 SMIv1-compatible VARBIND types (STRING, INT, TIMETICKS, IPVAL, OIDVAL, COUNTER32, GAUGE32) in a single packet.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, SNMP1, TRAP, COMMUNITY, ENTERPRISE, AGENTIP, GENTRAP, SPECTRAP, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, STRING, INT, TIMETICKS, IPVAL, OIDVAL, COUNTER32, GAUGE32, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a multi-service edge router with IP 10.108.0.1.
HOST edge_agent { IP 10.108.0.1 MAC 00:1a:a1:08:00:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define an SMIv1 trap receiver with IP 10.108.0.100.
HOST smiv1_nms { IP 10.108.0.100 MAC 00:1a:a1:08:00:64 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow sending a single SNMPv1 trap carrying STRING, INT, TIMETICKS, IPVAL, OIDVAL, COUNTER32, and GAUGE32 varbinds.
FLOW snmpv1_all_smiv1_varbinds(agent, nms) {
    agent -> nms SNMP1 TRAP COMMUNITY "public" ENTERPRISE 1.3.6.1.4.2.8072
        AGENTIP 10.108.0.1 GENTRAP 6 SPECTRAP 99 SYSUPTIME 50000
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "edge-rtr-01"
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.1.0 INT 24
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 TIMETICKS 50000
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.4.20.1.1.10.108.0.1 IPVAL 10.108.0.1
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0 OIDVAL 1.3.6.1.4.2.8072.3.2.10
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10.1 COUNTER32 9876543
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5.1 GAUGE32 1000000000
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to emit the multi-varbind SNMPv1 trap.
COMPILE {
    snmpv1_all_smiv1_varbinds(edge_agent, smiv1_nms)
}
```

## `examples/l7/snmp/snmpv2c/snmpv2c_all_nine_varbind_types.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Demonstrate all 9 supported FrameAssembly VARBIND value types (NULLVAL, STRING, INT, TIMETICKS, IPVAL, OIDVAL, COUNTER32, GAUGE32, COUNTER64) within a single.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, SNMP2, GET, COMMUNITY, REQID, VARBIND, NULLVAL, WAIT, RESPONSE, STRING, INT, TIMETICKS, IPVAL, OIDVAL, COUNTER32, GAUGE32, COUNTER64, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a comprehensive MIB test client with IP 10.127.0.10.
HOST mib_tester { IP 10.127.0.10 MAC 00:16:3e:27:00:10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a reference SNMPv2c agent with IP 10.127.0.20.
HOST ref_snmp_agent { IP 10.127.0.20 MAC 00:16:3e:27:00:20 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow that sends an SNMPv2c GET and receives a RESPONSE containing all 9 VarBind data types.
FLOW snmpv2c_all_nine_varbinds(tester, agent) {
    tester -> agent SNMP2 GET COMMUNITY "all_types" REQID 9999
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 NULLVAL
        WAIT 10ms
    tester <- agent SNMP2 RESPONSE COMMUNITY "all_types" REQID 9999
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.4.2 NULLVAL
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "ref-agent-01"
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.4.2.9999.1.1.0 INT -42
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 TIMETICKS 360000
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.4.20.1.1.10.127.0.20 IPVAL 10.127.0.20
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0 OIDVAL 1.3.6.1.4.2.8072.3.2.10
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10.1 COUNTER32 500000
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5.1 GAUGE32 100000000
        VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.6.1 COUNTER64 9876543210123
        WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the 9-varbind SNMPv2c showcase flow.
COMPILE {
    snmpv2c_all_nine_varbinds(mib_tester, ref_snmp_agent)
}
```

## `examples/l7/ssh/ssh_ansible_automation_bastion_jump.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Simulate an Ansible automation controller establishing an SSH-2.0 session through a bastion jump host on VLAN 22.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, SSH, BANNER, VLAN, PCP, WAIT, KEXINIT, PAYLOAD, NEWKEYS, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the Ansible AWX automation runner on management VLAN 22.
HOST ansible_runner {
    IP 10.22.100.15
    MAC 00:50:56:22:64:0f
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the hardened SSH bastion host on management VLAN 22.
HOST ssh_bastion_gw {
    IP 10.22.100.1
    MAC 00:50:56:22:64:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Exchange SSH-2.0 banners, KEXINIT, NEWKEYS, and publickey authentication messages over VLAN 22.
FLOW ssh_ansible_bastion_flow(runner, bastion) {
    runner -> bastion SSH BANNER "SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6p1 Ansible-Runner" VLAN 22 PCP 4 WAIT 2ms
    runner <- bastion SSH BANNER "SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6p1 Bastion-Hardened" VLAN 22 PCP 4 WAIT 2ms
    runner -> bastion SSH KEXINIT PAYLOAD "curve25519-sha256,aes256-gcm@openssh.com" VLAN 22 PCP 4 WAIT 3ms
    runner <- bastion SSH KEXINIT PAYLOAD "curve25519-sha256,aes256-gcm@openssh.com" VLAN 22 PCP 4 WAIT 3ms
    runner -> bastion SSH NEWKEYS VLAN 22 PCP 4
    runner <- bastion SSH NEWKEYS VLAN 22 PCP 4
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the VLAN 22 Ansible bastion SSH handshake flow.
COMPILE {
    ssh_ansible_bastion_flow(ansible_runner, ssh_bastion_gw)
}
```

## `examples/l7/ssh/ssh_automated_backup_batch_loop.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Automated configuration backup probe loop across network routers.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, SSH, BANNER, NEWKEYS, COMPILE, LOOP

// INSTRUCTION: Define configuration audit controller.
HOST audit_ctrl { IP 172.22.1.100 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define target router.
HOST target_rtr { IP 172.22.1.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define recurring configuration pull flow.
FLOW ssh_audit_flow(c, s) {
    c -> s SSH BANNER "SSH-2.0-Ansible_Automation"
    c <- s SSH BANNER "SSH-2.0-Cisco-1.25"
    c -> s SSH NEWKEYS
    c <- s SSH NEWKEYS
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing 3 repeated audit checks.
COMPILE {
    LOOP 3 {
        ssh_audit_flow(audit_ctrl, target_rtr)
    }
}
```

## `examples/l7/stun/stun_binding_error_retry_recovery.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Generate a STUN unauthenticated Binding Request rejected with a Binding Error response, followed by a successful retry.
// TOKENS: HOST, MAC, IP, FLOW, STUN, BINDING_REQUEST, SOFTWARE, BINDING_ERROR, WAIT, BINDING_RESPONSE, XOR_MAPPED_ADDR, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define host endpoint ice_client.
HOST ice_client {
    MAC 00:1b:21:34:78:01
    IP 172.16.30.15
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define host endpoint turn_server.
HOST turn_server {
    MAC 00:1b:21:34:78:02
    IP 172.16.30.1
}

// INSTRUCTION: Send initial Binding Request, receive BINDING_ERROR, wait 10ms, and succeed on retry.
FLOW stun_error_and_retry_flow(ice_client, turn_server) {
    ice_client -> turn_server STUN BINDING_REQUEST SOFTWARE "PJSIP-pjnath/2.14"
    turn_server -> ice_client STUN BINDING_ERROR SOFTWARE "coturn-4.6.2" WAIT 10ms
    ice_client -> turn_server STUN BINDING_REQUEST SOFTWARE "PJSIP-pjnath/2.14"
    turn_server -> ice_client STUN BINDING_RESPONSE XOR_MAPPED_ADDR 203.0.113.15 SOFTWARE "coturn-4.6.2"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the STUN error challenge and retry flow.
COMPILE {
    stun_error_and_retry_flow(ice_client, turn_server)
}
```

```frameassembly
    qa_harness -> syslog_verify SYSLOG FACILITY 1 SEVERITY 1 HOSTNAME "qa-box" APP "sevtest" PROCID "100" MSG "Alert: action must be taken immediately"
    qa_harness -> syslog_verify SYSLOG FACILITY 1 SEVERITY 2 HOSTNAME "qa-box" APP "sevtest" PROCID "100" MSG "Critical: critical conditions"
    qa_harness -> syslog_verify SYSLOG FACILITY 1 SEVERITY 3 HOSTNAME "qa-box" APP "sevtest" PROCID "100" MSG "Error: error conditions"
    qa_harness -> syslog_verify SYSLOG FACILITY 1 SEVERITY 4 HOSTNAME "qa-box" APP "sevtest" PROCID "100" MSG "Warning: warning conditions"

    qa_harness -> syslog_verify SYSLOG FACILITY 1 SEVERITY 6 HOSTNAME "qa-box" APP "sevtest" PROCID "100" MSG "Informational: informational messages"
    qa_harness -> syslog_verify SYSLOG FACILITY 1 SEVERITY 7 HOSTNAME "qa-box" APP "sevtest" PROCID "100" MSG "Debug: debug-level messages"
```
